  • Documentation
  • 8 in. Plastic Omni Wheel
    This revision has higher quality rubber rollers than the previous version.

    Usage With Axle and Hub:
    • If you wish to drive this wheel with an axle and hub, you can pick your hub by fitting any of the AndyMark hubs to this wheel. Hubs are not included with this wheel. If this is your choice, then no bearing is needed. To install a hub onto this wheel, use #10 screws and nuts. #10-24x3/4 thread forming screws.

    Usage With Sprockets and Bearings:

    • If you wish to drive this wheel with a sprocket, then the sprocket needs to be attached to the side of the wheel with #10 screws and nuts. You will also need to press ball bearings into the wheel so that it may spin on a shaft or bolt. The ball bearing must have a 1.125 in. od. For a 1/2 in. shafts, use am-0181. title: Battery Power Cable custom length up to 36 in.
body_html:
This is a custom-length battery cable, built to the same high standards as our standard 12 in. battery cable.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • This is a custom-length battery cable, built to the same high standards as our standard 12 in. battery cable. Once the overall length is selected, the red and black wire lengths are both equal to the chosen length.

    The cable is made of 6 gauge multi-strand wire while the connectors are securely crimped and protected with heat shrink tubing. The cable uses the same wire and crimped connector components as used on the standard length Battery Cable, which uses our robust 6-ton pneumatic crimping tool. One end includes the SB-50A APP Connector and the other end includes the 1/4 in. diameter crimped ring terminals.

    The selected cable length can be between 6 in. and 36 in. Simply select your desired length from the drop-down menu on the right to choose the overall length of this cable. All cable lengths are +/- 1 in.

    FRC Competition Tip: As your battery cable length increases, so does the internal resistance of the wire. This creates a voltage drop that means less power going to your motors and control system. For best results, you'll want to keep this cable as short as your design allows safely. Please also see R103, longer versions of this cable may not be exempt from the robot weight limit.

title: FIRST Tech Challenge Perimeter Kit
body_html:
This is the official FIRST Tech Challenge Perimeter.
  • Description
  • What's in the Box?
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • This is the official FIRST Tech Challenge Perimeter. This perimeter may be referenced as am-0481, am-0481a, or am-0481b in documentation. This is reusable from year to year and does not include soft tiles, game-specific hardware, components, or game pieces. This "b" revision is compatible with the previous "a" revision, meaning "b" version corners and panels can be used as replacement in "a" version perimeters.

    The perimeter is comprised of eight hinged panels and four straight panels. Once assembled, the perimeter creates an 11 feet 9 inch by 11 feet 9 inch square enclosure. The hinged corners and quick release pins make for easy assembly, requiring no tools. Side panels include a built-in wire way for easy cable management.

    An adjustable Perimeter Strap (am-2270a) placed under this playing surface help keep the walls square during game play.

    What’s New?

    The fastening method for fixing the polycarbonate sheets to the aluminum rails has changed. The previous mechanical press fit has been removed, and rivets now hold the polycarbonate sheet in place. Each Panel (am-2160b) is now comprised of two toothless aluminum extrusion rails (am-2556a), one sheet of 3 mm polycarbonate (am-2582a), and six rivets (am-1226).

    We have made this change to make the panels more consistent, as well as to allow for our customers to replace pieces of a panel as needed.

    Additional Perimeter Panels (not included):
    Corner Assemblies consist of two panels attached with hinges. Individual Panels and corner assemblies are available as Panels am-2160b and am-2600b respectively. If you wish to build a custom size arena for non tournament use, combine any number of corner assemblies or panels using two Field Links (am-2580a) and four Quick Release Pins per intersection.

    Field Flooring & Soft Tiles (not included):
    FIRST Tech Challenge tournaments are conducted inside this perimeter kit with Soft Tiles making up the floor. These are not included with the perimeter kit, but are available as a Full Field Set of Soft Tiles (am-2499-36) or as individual Soft Tiles (am-2499).

    Storage and Transportation (not included):
    This perimeter and soft tiles that are available separately can be stored and transported easily in bags designed specifically for them. Two Panel Bags (am-2313a) fit a standard tournament size perimeter. Two Soft Tile Bags (am-2500c) fit a tournament's set of soft tiles, each holding eighteen tiles.

    Shipping:
    This perimeter will ship in two 52 inch x 14 inch x 8 inch boxes, each 40 pounds. The total weight for this product, both boxes included, is 80 pounds.

    Not Included:
    Soft tiles for field flooring are not included within the perimeter kit. This perimeter kit does not include any game-specific hardware, components, or game pieces.

    See how AndyMark can help your team tackle FIRST Tech Challenge

  • Included Items:

title: 8 in. Pneumatic Wheel Kit
body_html:
The 8 in. Pneumatic Wheel Kit is a high-traction wheel which includes a grippy rubber tire, an pneumatic inner tube, and a strong plastic hub.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • Here is a high-traction wheel which includes a grippy rubber tire, an pneumatic inner tube, and a strong plastic hub. These parts are shipped to you in kit form. The unique aspect about this product is the competition-ready hub. The hub accepts any 200x50mm tire and inner tube, 1.125 in. (outside diameter) ball bearings (2 per wheel are needed), and the mounting holes needed to install hardware to be sprocket-driven or hub-driven. This wheel ships as a separate tire, inner tube, and hub halves. Assembly is required.

    Important Notes:


    • Diameter: The nominal diameter for this wheel is actually 7.65 in. when inflated normally.
    • Tube pinching: When assembling the tube within the two hub halves, be careful not to pinch the tube rubber between the plastic hub halves. If assembled with the tube pinched between the hub halves, the tube may puncture and leak.

    RPM Rating and notes:


    These wheels are designed to be propulsion wheels for driving a robot or wheel chair. The design intent is to be contacting the ground, being driven by a gearbox at a maximum speed of approximately 500 rpm (which results in 17 feet/sec).

    Within some applications, this wheel has been used as a shooter of objects, spinning at a very high rpm. For these applications, a higher rpm shows that the wheel may wobble, since the valve stem is mounted off to one side of the center of the wheel hub. We have seen properly balanced wheels, using securely mounted hardware (longer screws, washers) that can handle 5,000 rpm. When spinning this wheel at speeds up to 5,000 rpm, please take proper safety precautions.

    Included Items:

    • Tire for 8 Inch Pneumatic Wheel (Metric Size 200x50mm)
    • Inner Tube for 8 Inch Pneumatic Wheel, with 90 Degree Stem (for 200x50mm Tire)
    • Hub Assembly for 8 inch Pneumatic Wheel, which includes two (2) black plastic hub halves and six (6) 4-40 x1 Pan Head Phillips thread rolling screws

    NOT Included Hardware:

    • Bearings
    • #10 Screws and Nuts Needed to Mount a Hub (2 Inch Long Screws are Needed) or a Sprocket (2.25 Inch Long Screws are Needed)
    • Aluminum Hub, if Driven by a Shaft
    ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    Wheel Structure:

    The hub halves are held together with the #4-40 screws. This wheel can accept #10-32 screws for mounting sprockets or hubs, but these are NOT included since different length screws are needed to mount hubs or sprockets. These #10 screws can be mounted to the included 1.875 inch diameter bolt circle. The hub halves need to be assembled together so that the valve stem clearance holes line up. Locating features are present for easy alignment.

    Usage:
    With Axle and Hub:
    • In order to drive this wheel with a hub, use Hardware Kit 11, which includes #10-32x2 screws (6) and #10-32 nylock nuts (6)
    With Sprocket:
    • In order to drive this wheel with a plate sprocket, use Hardware Kit 12, which includes a 550 Sprocket Spacer, #10-32x2.25 screws (6) and #10-32 nylock nuts (6).
    • Two (2) bearings are needed for this wheel, if being driven by a sprocket. Use bearings with a 1.125 inch outer diameter. No flange is needed on either of the bearings.
    Use as a caster:
    • If you want to let this wheel spin without being driven, you will need to install two (2) bearings with 1.125 inch outer diameter.
    • Bolt Pattern: 6 holes, 0.20 diameter on 1.875 in. diameter bolt circle
    • Bore: 1.00 in. diameter through hole, with two 1.125 in. diameter bearing pockets
    • Diameter: 7.65 in.
    • Load Capacity: 120 lbs.
    • Material: Black Polycarbonate, gray rubber
    • Maximum Pressure: 35 psi
    • Tread Width: 2 in.
    • Valve Stem: The valve stem may stick out up to 0.375 in. from hub
    • Weight: 1.13 lbs.
    • Width Across Middle: 1.8 in.

  • This is the "500EX Key Hub". It is a slightly different version of the 500 Key Hub. It is manufactured differently, as it is extruded. Also, there is a 1.124 in. diameter boss on each side of the hub flange, providing a location for 1.125 in. bore flat sprockets. Are you having a hard time keeping your sprocket concentric with your hub? This hub is the trick.

    The bore is a 1/2 in. hole with two 1/8 in. keyways. Only one keyway is needed to drive most wheels, so the second one is extra.

    Also, the keyways are consistently aligned with the mounting holes.

title: AM14U5 - 6 Wheel Drop Center Robot Drive Base
body_html:
This is the "AM" "One" "For" You" chassis.
  • Description
  • What's in the Box?
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • This is the "AM" - "ONE" - "FOR" - "YOU"!

    Perfect for prototyping robotic applications as well as being part of the final design! This large format, infinitely configurable drive platform was designed to be built with performance in mind. The AM14U5 drive chassis has three main configurations (Long, Square & Wide) as starting options. The drop center wheel allows for smoother turning ability, while maintaining stability.

    What Can You Do?

    Want to learn what you can change and accomplish with the AM14U5? Start here for a look at all the things this frame can do for you.

    This is the 5th major upgrade to this popular chassis with many more minor revisions. Our AM14U family of products has evolved and changed based on customer feedback since the first AM14U was released in 2014, and it was a major upgrade to the C-base chassis that was part of the FIRST Kit of Parts since 2009.

    This product ships as an un-assembled kit. It features HiGrip Wheels, Toughbox Mini Gearboxes, and Gates HTD Belts.

    Assembly and cutting of aluminum is required. See the Assembly Videos below.

    If this chassis is being used for the FIRST Robotics Competition, please consider the robot perimeter rules and size this chassis accordingly. The manual helps clearly show where to make cuts for different sizes, you can adapt your cuts to fit as needed.

    Gear Ratio:

    In the 2024 FIRST® Robotics Competition CRESCENDO℠ presented by Haas the KOP Chassis has 8.46 :1 Gear Ratio. Here we've included the various gear ratios for your convenience. If you would like to know more about gear ratios and how they effect your robot, watch our How Do I Change Motor Speed and Torque? video.

    Various Frame Size Configurations:

    Built on the same great features of previous AM14U family chassis, this can be configured into many different perimeter, wheel, and gearbox configurations. There are literally thousands of possible playing configurations.

    • Smallest Frame size: 24.3 in. x 27 in.
    • Largest Frame size: 32.3 in. x 31 in.

    It is shipped as a Kit with plates that can build in a large square configuration. This makes it the largest possible size and allows for the user to trim the length and width of the chassis to become a long, wide, or a smaller square to fit different the size constraints of each specific year. The assembly instructions show how it can be changed, be sure to check out the assembly videos as well.

    Multiple Wheel And Build Configuration Options:

    For even more wheel and build configurations, check out our AM14U4 & AM14U5 Wheel Upgrades!

    Encoder Options:

    The AM14U5 does not include encoders. The Toughbox Mini gearboxes included in the AM14U5 ship with an output shaft (am-4722) that has two holes in the end for optional included 1/4 in. diameter steel dowels (am-1323) that are compatible with the US Digital E4T Encoder (am-3132) and the REV Through Bore Encoder (am-4650). Teams also have the option of purchasing a magnetic dowel (am-3505) to replace the steel dowel allowing the use of the SRX Magnetic Encoder (am-3445). In order to use this encoder on the Toughbox Mini, our SRX Magnetic Encoder Mounting Hardware Kit (am-3565) must also be used to mount each encoder.

    Assembly Video Guides:

    Assembly videos can be found by clicking here.

    Control Options:

    To control this drive, you will need a power and control system like the Electronic Bundles kit, roboRIO, Spark Max, 4 CIM motors, and PDP (BCRX4CP). Many options are available!

    The chassis requires a minimum of two CIM style motors (am-0255), but we recommend four CIMs to be competitive in situations like heavy robots, high traction, and pushing match situations that put a lot of load on the motors. You will also need at least one battery. We recommend the 2 Pack of MK ES17-12 12V SLA Batteries (am-0844), and the 3 Bank SB50 NOCO Battery Charger (am-4968_3). There are many options available here as well, take your pick!

    Center Pulley Screws:

    Fear not friends with robots! The 2022 Kit of Parts Chassis was identified to have screws that backed out on the center pulleys. These screws were replaced with screws that performed as intended. AndyMark evaluated and implemented those replacement screws in full for the 2023 Kit of Parts Chassis. You may find that the screws look similar, but rest assured, these pulley screws will not cause you this alarm.


  • What comes in the beautiful 34x7x7 in. box:

    • 2 - AM14U5 Inside Plate (am-3922a)
    • 2 - AM14U Family End Plate (am-3920)
    • 2 - AM14U5 Outside Plate (am-3921a)

  • Please note, there is an error in the included printed instructions for this product. The amount called out to cut off the inside and outside plates was incorrect. The updated guide has been attached to the "Documentation" section of this page. If you have already cut your plates in error please contact us.

    This is the "AM" - "ONE" - "FOR" - "YOU"!

    The perfect base for prototyping robotic applications as well as being part of the final design! This large format, infinitely configurable drive platform was designed to be built with performance in mind. The AM14U6 drive chassis has three main configurations (Long, Square & Wide) as starting options. The drop center wheel allows for smoother turning ability, while maintaining stability. This is the 6th generation of this popular chassis now includes "on grid" #10 clearance holes that make it much easier to interface popular upper structure options such as pre-drilled tubing and gussets.

    This product ships as an un-assembled kit. It features HiGrip Wheels, Toughbox Mini S Gearboxes, and HTD Belts.

    Assembly and cutting of aluminum is required. See the Assembly Videos.



    If this chassis is being used for the FIRST Robotics Competition, please consider the robot perimeter rules and size this chassis accordingly. The manual helps clearly show where to make cuts for different sizes, you can adapt your cuts to fit as needed.

    Gear Ratio:

    In the 2025 FIRST® Robotics Competition the KOP Chassis has 8.46:1 Gear Ratio. On this page you can select all possible gear ratios. If you would like to know more about gear ratios and how they affect your robot, watch our How Do I Change Motor Speed and Torque? video.

    Various Configurations:

    Built on the same great features of previous AM14U family chassis, this can be configured into many different perimeter, wheel, and gearbox configurations. There are literally thousands of possible playing configurations.

    • Smallest Frame size: 24.3 in. x 27 in.
    • Largest Frame size: 32.3 in. x 31 in.

    It is shipped as a Kit with plates that can build in a large square configuration. This makes it the largest possible size and allows for the user to trim the length and width of the chassis to become a long, wide, or a smaller square to fit different the size constraints of each specific year. The assembly instructions show how it can be changed, be sure to check out the assembly videos as well.

    Encoder Options:

    The AM14U6 does not include encoders. The included Toughbox Mini S Gearboxes ship with an output shaft that has holes in the ends for optional included 1/4 in. diameter steel dowels (am-1323) that are compatible with the US Digital E4T Encoder (am-3132) and the REV Through Bore Encoder (am-4650). Teams also have the option of purchasing a magnetic dowel (am-3505) to replace the steel dowel allowing the use of the SRX Magnetic Encoder (am-3445). In order to use this encoder on the Toughbox Mini S, our SRX Magnetic Encoder Mounting Hardware Kit (am-3565) must also be used to mount each encoder.

    Control Options:

    To control this drive, you will need a power and control system like the Electronic Bundles kit, roboRIO, Spark Max, 4 CIM motors, and PDP (BCRX4CP). Many options are available!

    The chassis requires a minimum of two CIM style motors (am-0255), but we recommend four CIMs to be competitive in situations like heavy robots, high traction, and pushing match situations that put a lot of load on the motors. You will also need at least one battery. We recommend the 2 Pack of MK Batteries (am-0844), and the 3 Bank SB50 NOCO Battery Charger (am-4968_3). There are many options available here as well.

title: AM14U5/6 Wheel Upgrades
body_html:
All of these options include various upgraded wheel components for the 2023 AM14U5 chassis.

  • Description
  • What's in the Box?
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • COMPATIBILITY NOTE:

    The upgrade kits with SKU starting as am-14u5_ are compatible with the 2023-2024 AM14U5 and the 2025 AM14U6 that use the new ToughBox Mini S Gearbox. For upgrade kits that that are compatible with the older 2022 AM14U5 and the 2019-2021 AM14U4 the part number will need to start with am-14u4_

    The AM14U6 is the most versatile chassis for FIRST Robotics Competition teams. The chassis was named as such because there is a flavor of this AndyMark chassis for every one of you. A version of the AM14U family of chassis exists for every teams need. All of the options available through this page include the upgrade components ONLY and will not ship with a chassis.

    Wheel Diameter Options:

    • 4 inch
    • 6 inch
    • 8 inch

    Drive Style Options:

    • 6 Wheel Drop Center
    • 8 Wheel Drop Center
    • 4 Wheel, Mecanum

    Wheel Type Options:

    • HD Mecanum, rigid small profile mecanum wheels for precise driving in all directions.
    • SR Mecanum, incredibly smooth-rolling mecanum wheels.
    • MK Mecanum, large and high capacity mecanum wheels.
    • Performance, high strength high load capacity metal wheels to be used with 1 in. wide replaceable tread.
    • XL Performance, the same perks of Performance, but wider! These performance wheels are 0.5 in. wider than regular.
    • DuraOmni, these omni wheels can be used in the corners of a U4 to create a rapid turning machine with virtually no scrub.
    • Pneumatic SD, plastic hubbed wheels with inflated inner tubes to create a squishy grippy drive.
    • Pneumatic HD, metal hubbed wheels with inflated inner tubes. A squishy grippy drive with an unbreakable hub.
    • HiGrip, plastic wheels with a strong polycarbonate center and a grippy TPU outside.

    Changes Beyond Bundles:

    While we only list sixteen different upgrade kits here, you can further tweak these options by trying different types of tread on performance wheels, different durometers and diameters of HiGrip wheels, or adjusting the ratio in your gearboxes. If you don't see an option you like or want help configuring an option, contact us and we can help you find the right one.


  • Included Items:

    Each of the upgrade options we offer includes the wheels, hardware, and if necessary, the gearboxes, to add the desired wheel arrangement to the stock AM14U5 or 6. Details of what goes in each upgrade kit can be found in this Bill of Materials Section.

    • Diameter Options: 4in., 6in., 8in
    • Style Options: 4-Wheel Mecanum, 6-Wheel Drop-Center, 8-Wheel Drop-Center

title: 0.5 in. Hex and Keyed Shaft Coupling
body_html:
This coupling has geometry to capture 1/2 in. hex shafts with an inside hex profile as well as 1/2 in. keyed shafts with an additional 1/8th in. keyway.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • Whether you have shafts that are too short or shafts of different types, this coupling will solve every component connection issue you've had! Need to combine multiple 1/2 in. hex shafts, multiple 1/2 in. keyed shafts, or convert between hex and keyed? This coupling solves all at a better price than anyone else can offer!

    Shaft Compatibility

    Clamping

    The clamping force is provided by four 10-32 x 0.5 in. socket head cap screws for a high-strength clamping solution that won't strip out when you need it most. These screws are bigger than most used in the comparable shaft couplings from other suppliers. You can even replace the 10-32 screw if it becomes lost, with the screws historically used in the AM14U family of chassis.

    Use Near Bearings

    The best shaft coupling available has been thoughtfully designed with small bosses on each side. These allow these collar clamps to be installed directly adjacent to an FR8ZZ Round or FR8ZZ Hex bearing without rubbing on the outer races for smooth operation.

    • Bore: 0.500 in. [12.7 mm] (1/2) Hex

    • Key Width: 0.125 in.
    • Length: 1.5 in.
    • Material: 6061-T6 Aluminum

title: M3 Heat Set Threaded Insert
body_html:
These inserts can be used to create a connection point in a 3d printed or plastic object.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • Instead of gluing bits together, or screwing plastic screws directly into your 3D prints, use strong and reusable machine screws and heat-set inserts. The grooved outside allows them to dig into the plastic and retain their place, and an M3 threaded inside makes them compatible with many fasteners. Threaded inserts hold stronger than tapped threads in plastic and allow the screw threads to last longer.

    These inserts can be installed in plastic components using a warm soldering iron. Simply heat the insert with the tip of the soldering iron and firmly press the brass insert into the part. Once cool, the insert will be firmly held in the part and ready for use.

title: 0.375 in. Hex Shaft Coupling
body_html:
This coupler joins two hex shafts for more length.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • Whether you have shafts that are too short or are looking for a quick disconnect, this coupling will solve every component connection issue you've had! Need to combine multiple 3/8 in. hex shafts? This coupling is just what you're looking for.

    Shaft Compatibility

    This coupling has geometry to capture 3/8 in. hex shafts with an inside hex profile.

    Clamping

    The clamping force is provided by four 10-32 x 0.5 in. socket head cap screws for a high-strength clamping solution that won't strip out when you need it most. These screws are bigger than most used in the comparable shaft couplings from other suppliers. You can even replace the 10-32 screw if it becomes lost, with the screws historically used in the AM14U family of chassis.

    Use Near Bearings

    The best shaft coupling available has been thoughtfully designed with small bosses on each side. These allow these collar clamps to be installed directly adjacent to an FR8ZZ Round or FR8ZZ Hex bearing without rubbing on the outer races for smooth operation.

    • Bore: 0.375 in. [9.5 mm] (3/8) Hex
    • Length: 1 in.
    • Material: 6061-T6 Aluminum
    • Outside Diameter: 1 in.

title: Viair 90C Air Compressor
body_html:
VIAIR 90C compressor (air pump) offers a light duty solution for smaller air requirements.
  • Description
  • What's in the Box?
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • Warranty

  • These compact compressors and are meant to fill no larger than a 1.0 gallon air tank. These products are used on mobile competition robots and outdoor equipment.

    Performance Test:

    • Manufacturer Specifications as of 2/2020: 1.03 CFM
    • Results of 2014 AndyMark bench test for determining CFM rates:
    Pressure Flow rate Amp Draw
    0 psi 0.88 cfm 7 amps
    10 0.50 8
    20 0.43 8
    30 0.36 9
    40 0.30 9
    50 0.27 9
    60 0.25 10
    70 0.24 10
    80 0.24 10
    90 0.23 11
    100 0.22 11
    110 0.22 10
    • For this test, flow rate was determined by this calculation:
      • (change of pressure) / 14.7 psi * volume of system / time elapsed
      • For example, at 10 psi:
        • change of pressure = 10 psi
        • volume of system = 0.1095 cubic feet
        • time elapsed = 9 seconds (0.15 minutes)
        • CFM = 10 psi / 14.7 psi * 0.1095 cubic feet / 0.15 minute = 0.50 cfm
    • Fill Rate for Number of Clippard tanks (574 ml) to fill from 0 to 110 psi:
      • 1 Tank = 34 Seconds
      • 2 Tanks = 64 Seconds
      • 3 Tanks = 103 Seconds
      • 4 Tanks = 140 Seconds
      • 5 Tanks = 176 Seconds

    VIAIR is a proud sponsor of FIRST Robotics and supporter of their mission.

body_html:

  • THIS GAME IS A PAST SEASON, be sure that this item is for the correct game you are looking for.

    Each CUBE (am-4700_bpc) is made of purple PVC fabric and is marked with a FIRST logo. The CUBE is a cube-like shape, inflated to 9 ½ in. (~24 cm) +/- ¼ in. (~6 mm) as measured from face to face, but these ship deflated. A CUBE has rounded corners, may not have flat surfaces, and the length, width, and height of the sides may not be equal dimensions. A CUBE weighs 2.5 oz (~71 g).

    No longer available: The UNOFFICIAL Orange Cone (am-4700_soc) is a close approximation of the game piece for the 2023 FIRST Robotics Competition Game, CHARGED UP! The only difference is the color. It is an orange, 1 ft. ¹³⁄₁₆ in. (~33 cm) tall rubber marker cone and weighs 1lb 7oz (~653 g). Each CONE has an 8⅜ in. (~21 cm) +/- ⅛in. (~3 mm) square base with ¼ in. (~7 mm) tall feet.

    No longer available: Each CONE (am-4700_syc) is a yellow 1 ft. ¹³⁄₁₆ in. (~33 cm) tall rubber marker cone and weighs 1lb 7oz (~653 g). Each CONE has an 8⅜ in. (~21 cm) +/- ⅛in. (~3 mm) square base with ¼ in. (~7 mm) tall feet.

    No longer available: The Cube Measurement Jig (am-4700_cmj) is a tool developed by FIRST to calibrate CUBE inflation at events. How does it work? Field staff simply measure each Cube as they are inflated to ensure that jig is lifted off the ground and ensuring that both sides of the cube do not touch the jig at the same time. The total weight of the jig is important in determining the minimum bound. See the demonstration video for proper usage technique.

    CONES and CUBES may become damaged during use, testing, robot interaction, and gameplay. This is expected. AndyMark will not replace damaged CONES and CUBES.

title: RAW Box
body_html:
The RAW Box is a strong, compact gearbox utilizing NEO or CIM motors located at a right angle from the output shaft.
  • Description
  • Gearbox Ratios
  • What's in the Box?
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • The RAW Box is a strong, compact gearbox utilizing NEO, or CIM Motors. Steel and brass worm gears are used in order to provide a setup where the CIM Motors are located at a right angle from the output shaft. Since one or two motors can be used as input for this gearbox, and the gears are made of strong materials, this gearbox can provide a high level of torque.

    The worm gear shaft is driven by a spur gear. This spur gear is driven by another spur gear located on the output shaft of the motor. These two spur gears can have their position swapped in order to change the overall reduction of the gearbox. The Standard Ratio (14.2:1) is how the gearbox is pre-assembled and shipped. The Switched Ratio (7.1:1) is what the user can get, after re-positioning these gears.

    Product Usage:

    All AndyMark gearboxes require grease for proper operation and long life. We suggest using our red tacky grease, am-2768. We also encourage that the user powers the gearbox continuously for 30 minutes without grease to allow the gear teeth to wear in. While we do design with short run times in mind, this 'run in' period for smooth gearbox operation, is recommended. Once this is completed, thoroughly grease the gear teeth periodically to ensure smooth operation.

    NOTE: When operated correctly the angle of the worm in the RAW Box allows it to back-drive.

    Design Background:

    This gearbox design is heavily influenced by the two-motor Right Angle Worm gearbox made by student designer Joey Milia of FRC team 192, GRT (Gunn Robotics Team) from California. Joey and GRT came up with this successful design for the 2012 FIRST Robotics Competition. Thanks, Joey and team 192 for providing this design to AndyMark so that the robotics community can utilize this design!


  • Please contact support@andymark.com if you do not see a Ratio Table

title: FTDI Serial TTL USB Cable
body_html:
This is a USB to 5V serial adapter cable designed to program Ethernet Arduino boards.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • This is a USB to 5V serial adapter cable designed to program Ethernet Arduino boards. It requires it's own drivers found at the FTDI Website. Unlike some other Arduino boards, the Ethernet Arduino does not have an onboard USB-to-serial driver, so an external one is required for programming.
    This cable will also power the Arduino and automatically reset it after loading a sketch.

title: 6 in. Pneumatic Wheel Hub Assembly
body_html:
This is the strong polycarbonate plastic hub for a 6-inch Pneumatic Wheel.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • The hub accepts any 6 x 1 1/4 tire and inner tube, 1.125 in. (outside diameter) ball bearings (2 per wheel are needed), and the mounting holes needed to install hardware to be sprocket-driven or hub-driven. This product is shipped in kit form.

    Included Items:

    Included Hardware:
    • Two (2) black plastic hub halves
    • Six (6) #4-40x1 Pan Head Phillips thread rolling screws

    NOT Included Hardware:

    • bearings
    • #10 screws and nuts needed to mount a hub (2 inch long screws are needed) or a sprocket (2.25 inch long screws are needed)
    • tire and inner tube: Any 150x50mm tire and inner tube can fit this hub, as long as the inner tube has a 90-degree valve stem.
    ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
    Wheel Structure:
    The hub halves are held together with the #4-40 screws. This wheel can accept #10-32 screws for mounting sprockets or hubs, but these are NOT included since different length screws are needed to mount hubs or sprockets. These #10 screws can be mounted to the included 1.875-inch diameter bolt circle. The hub halves need to be assembled together so that the valve stem clearance holes line up. Locating features are present for easy alignment.

    Usage:
    With Axle and Hub:
    • In order to drive this wheel with a hub, use six (6) #10-32x2.25 screws (am-1156) and six (6) #10-32 nylock nuts (am-1042).

    With Sprocket:

    • In order to drive this wheel with a plate sprocket,use six (6) #10-32x2.25 screws (am-1156) and six (6) #10-32 nylock nuts (am-1042).
    • Two (2) bearings are needed for this wheel when being driven by a sprocket. Use bearings with a 1.125 inch outer diameter. No flange is needed on either of the bearings.

    Use as a caster:

    • If you want to let this wheel spin without being driven, you will need to install two (2) bearings with 1.125 inch outer diameter.

title: F6 Flexible 1/2 in. Self-Wrap Split Braided Sleeving, 10ft section
body_html:
This braided sleeving is the ideal solution to bundle, protect, and conceal cords and cables.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • F6's unique split, semi-rigid braided construction makes it the ideal solution for situations where ease of installation is of primary importance. The lateral split allows the tube to open up to accommodate a wide variety of bundling requirements, and the semi-rigid braid configuration simply closes around the entire installation without the need for any additional fasteners (velcro, tape, etc.) The 10 mil PET braid is lightweight, quiet and flexible. The 25% edge overlap (at nominal diameter) allows coverage around inline plugs, connectors and splices. F6 will bend to a tight radius without distorting or splitting open and, unlike full rigid tubing, will not impair or affect the flexibility of harnesses.

body_html:
This hardare kit is a great start to being able to use a string potentionmeter.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • A great start to being able to use a string pot sensor is here. This kit excludes the potentiometer and housing so you can use components you have in house.
    Two options are available, as you can download 3D Prints for the Cap, Case, and Spool. Or you can buy a complete kit that only needs to be assembled.
    A portion of the proceeds of this sale will be given to Chap Robotics FRC team 2468, who developed and used this idea on their competition robots.

    Included Hardware:
    • Three - 4-40 x 0.75 in. Screws (to seal the enclosure)
    • One - 4-40 x 3/8 in. SHCS (to capture the potentiometer shaft)
    • One - Retractable String component
      • Retractable String Length: ~27 inch

title: RadioLink T8S with Mecanum Mixer
body_html:
This is an easy plug-and-play kit for a mecanum wheel chassis.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • The goBILDA Mecanum mixer allows for simple RC-control of a mecanum drive robot. The Mecanum mixer plugs into a standard RC receiver using three input channels. Four motor speed controllers get plugged into the mecanum mixer, then the Mixer takes over and its signal mixing will handle the rest. Are some of your wheels spinning the wrong direction? This mixer features switches to easily reverse the direction of each of the motors individually.

    Included Hardware:

    • RadioLink T8S Wireless Controller & R8EF Receiver (am-4422)
    • Mecanum Mixer (am-5212)

    Binding the Transmitter and Receiver:

    1. Put the transmitter and the receiver close to each other (about 1 foot) and power on the receiver.
    2. Switch on the transmitter, and the LED on R8EF will start flashing slowly.
    3. There is a black binding button (ID SET) on the side of the receiver. Press the button until the LED is flashing quickly and release, meaning the binding process is ongoing.
    4. When the LED stops flashing and is always on, binding is complete. If not successful, the LED will flash slowly, if this happens, repeat the above steps.

    Wiring:

    Three male-to-male servo extensions come included to mate your mixer to your receiver.

title: Voltage Regulator Module
body_html:
The Voltage Regulator Module is a DC to DC convertor that is capable of both boost and buck voltage regulation.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • Warranty
  • NOTE: This product is not included in any Sales or Discounts.

    The Voltage Regulator Module (VRM) is a DC to DC convertor that is capable of both boost and buck voltage regulation. The device features two independent SEPIC (Single Ended Primary-inductor Converter) regulators allowing the input voltage to be above or below the desired output voltage. There are two regulators (one 5V and one 12V) each with two current limiting PTC’s (500mA and 2A). Reverse polarity protection is included.
    The VRM has been used in the 2015-2021 FIRST Robotics Competition Kit of Parts. As of Sept 10, 2020 according to FIRST blog these will continue to remain competition legal in future years.

title: Thrifty Throttle 3
body_html:
The Thrifty Throttle 3 provides a solid PWM signal for testing electro-mechanical systems.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • This can be very useful for FRC teams before their control software is complete or trouble shooting issues that arise during competition. There are new features on this version for the same price!

    Features:

    • PWM Generation
      • Standard Range (For Speed Controllers): 1000us - 2000us
      • Extended Range (For Speed Controllers): 500us -­2400us
    • Handheld
      • Comfortable form factor, one hand operation
      • 9V battery operation
    • Improvements from Original Thrifty Throttle
      • Cypress PSOC4 running at 24Mhz for solid PWM generation
      • Drive servos with external power source using Y cable
      • RGB LED for visual PWM range mode indication
      • Low battery indication - Fading Yellow LED
    Driving Servos:
    Since there are so many servos with varying power requirements, it was decided not to power servos directly from the Thrifty Throttle. However, you can easily power such devices from your own power source (e.g. RC battery pack) using a Y cable (am-2261 or am-2581).

    Basic Operation:
    The push button in the upper right hand corner enables and disables the PWM control.

    • From the neutral mode (white LED heartbeat blink)
      • If you do a quick push button press you will enter the standard PWM range (This is used on common speed controllers in FRC)
        • 1000us 2000us
          • In this range the LED colors are as follows:
            • Neutral is Orange
            • Forward is Green
            • Reverse is Red
      • If you hold the push button for about 2 seconds you will enter the extended PWM range (This is used in many ESCs in common RC applications as well as servos)
        • ~500us ~2400us
        • In this range the LED colors are as follows:
          • Neutral is Blue
          • Forward is Turquoise
          • Reverse is Violet
      • Now you can adjust the speed and direction by moving the red throttle wheel with your thumb
        • Clockwise from center =­ forward
        • Counter-clockwise from center = reverse
        • The blink speed will change with the PWM speed
      • To exit and return to neutral simply press the push button again

  • The NeveRest 40 is a gearmotor with an attached encoder. The output shaft geometry and the gearbox housing diameter is similar to what FTC teams are familiar with. The shaft is a 6 mm D and the gearbox housing is 37 mm diameter.

    The power cable which feeds into the black encoder housing has two different options that are already crimped to the end of the cable. (select your needs above):
    1. NEW for 2020! JST-VH-2 connectors Option: this option plugs directly into the FIRST Tech Challenge REV Controller
    2. Anderson Powerpole 15A connectors Option

    FIRST Legality:

    • According to the FIRST Tech Challenge Game Manual, all versions of the NeveRest motor are legal in FTC.
    • According to the FIRST Robotics Competition Game Manual, all versions of the NeveRest motor are legal in FRC as it uses the NeveRest am-3104 motor.

    Encoder:
    There is an encoder mounted to the backside of this motor. It is a 7 pulse per revolution (ppr), hall effect encoder. Since the motor's gearbox has a 40:1 reduction, then the NeverRest 40 output shaft provides 280 ppr.

    Encoder Cable Options:
    NeveRest motors do not come with an encoder cable as we offer 3 cable options:

    am-3926a allows you to connect the encoder directly to the FIRST Tech Challenge REV Controller.
    am-2992 has the 4 encoder pins joined in one housing using standard 0.1 in. spacing.
    am-2993 allows you to break out the 4 pins separately if you need them in a different order.

Just note if you get motors with pre-installed pinions you'll have two pinions left over.

    F.A.Q.
    • Will my FRC Team receive the roboRIO 2.0 in the 2024 KOP?
      • Rookie FRC teams get the roboRIO 2.0 in the 2024 kickoff kit - Gray Tote.
    • Is the roboRIO still legal for FRC?
      • roboRIO and roboRIO 2 are both legal through the end of the 2026 season.
    • What programming languages does roboRIO 2.0 support?
      • It supports LabVIEW, Java, and C++.
    • How is roboRIO 2.0 different from roboRIO 1.0?
      • New features are discussed in the FIRST Robotics Competition Blog
    • Can non FRC customers purchase a roboRIO 2.0?
      • FRC teams, affiliates, partners, and organizers can purchase a roboRIO 2.0 from AndyMark provided they will be used to support FRC teams or competitions.
      • Contact NI with inquiries for non-FRC uses
    • Can I get more information on the roboRIO 2.0?
      • NI will post information on the NI website as it becomes available
    • We lost our power connector, where can I get more?
      • The Sauro Connector (CTF020V8) is the same one included with the roboRIO 2.0.

    • If I have a roboRIO 1.0 with an issue can I get a roboRIO 2.0 as replacement?
      • At this time the version of roboRIO you have is what will be replaced if NI deems a replacement is needed. You will need to start by contacting NI through the FIRST Support Forums
    • Is an SD card included with the roboRIO 2.0?

title: navX2 MXP Robotics Navigation Sensor
body_html:
The navX2-MXP is a second-generation 9-axis inertial/magnetic sensor and motion processor.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • Warranty

  • This item is restricted for shipment in some countries. Please check international shipping restrictions before ordering.

    BRAND NEW NEXT-GENERATION SENSOR NOW AVAILABLE - leveraging new sensors and state-of-the-art algorithms to deliver a leap forward in accuracy and performance.

    “Generation 2” navX2-MXP is a drop-in replacement for “Classic” navX-MXP, adding significant performance enhancements. See the Frequently Asked Questions (FAQ) for more information about navX2-MXP's new and enhanced capabilities.

    navX2 MXP 4.1

    Key specifications include:

    • 9-Axis Inertial/Magnetic Sensor (Gyro / Accelerometer / Magnetometer)
    • Intelligent Motion Processor
    • RoboRIO Expansion I/O
    • Check out all the features

    Many capabilities:

    • Field-oriented drive, auto-balancing, collision detection, motion detection, auto-rotate-to-angle, linear velocity vectors and more…
    • 10 Digital I/Os, 4 Analog Inputs, 2 Analog Outputs, and TTL UART / I2C / SPI ports.
    • Easily installed via RoboRIO’s MXP Expansion connector or USB port.
    • C++, Java and LabView libraries and sample application code simplify integration.
    • Existing navX-MXP users can upgrade easily.
    • Free software libraries & example code are available for easy integration and use.

    What's New and Improved in navX2-MXP

    • Significantly improved yaw accuracy and stability, even during Extreme inertial events. navX2-MXP features very high-accuracy orientation (yaw/pitch/roll), with minimal yaw drift of ~0.5 degree per minute when moving, and < 0.2 degrees/hour when still. navX2-MXP is incredibly stable, and averages a yaw drift of only 2 degrees per DAY when still. navX2-MXP's new Industrial-class ISM330DHCX IMU sensor handles high rotation (4000 degree/second) and impact (16G, operates in higher temperature environments and can survive extreme shock events (20,000G).
    • Rapid (5-second) auto-calibrating startup.
    • navX2-MXP features an upgraded 180Mhz 32-bit floating-point ARM processor, the new sensors, and new state-of-the-art software algorithms which take navX technology to the next level, including a blazing-fast 416-Khz Kalman Filter, enhanced sensor calibration and algorithms which fuse gyro, accelerometer and magnetometer data into a “9-axis heading”.
    • As a result of these upgrades, the accuracy of Velocity Vector Measurements and Displacement Estimates is also improved.

    More technical details are available in the navX2 MXP technical specifications and there's even more information at navX2-MXP Online.

    • Connector Type: Power: USB and/or 5VDC/GND Pins on MXP Connector
    • Current: 60 mA consumption

title: NeveRest Classic 60 Gearmotor
body_html:
The NeveRest 60 is a gearmotor with an attached encoder.

  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • The output shaft geometry and the gearbox housing diameter is similar to what FTC teams are familiar with. The shaft is a 6 mm D and the gearbox housing is 37 mm diameter.

    The power cable which feeds into the black encoder housing has two different options that are already crimped to the end of the cable. (select your needs above):
    1. NEW for 2020! JST-VH-2 connectors Option: this option plugs directly into the FIRST Tech Challenge REV Controller
    2. Anderson Powerpole 15A connectors Option

    FIRST Legality:

    • According to the FIRST Tech Challenge Game Manual, all versions of the NeveRest motor are legal in FTC.
    • According to the FIRST Robotics Competition Game Manual, all versions of the NeveRest motor are legal in FRC as it uses the NeveRest am-3104 motor.

    Encoder:
    There is an encoder mounted to the backside of this motor. It is a 7 pulses per revolution (ppr), hall effect encoder. Since the motor's gearbox has a 60:1 reduction, then the NeverRest 60 output shaft provides 420 ppr.

    Encoder Cable Options:
    NeveRest motors do not come with an encoder cable as we offer 3 cable options:

    am-3926a allows you to connect the encoder directly to the FIRST Tech Challenge REV Controller.
    am-2992 has the 4 encoder pins joined in one housing using standard 0.1 in. spacing.
    am-2993 allows you to break out the 4 pins separately if you need them in a different order.

    Performance Specs:
    Time to Failure at Stall: 2 minutes, 54 seconds
    Motor Case Temperature at Failure: 190 degrees F
    If you need the output shaft to be a 1/2 in. Hex, check out the 6 mm D to 0.5 in. Hex-Shaft Adapter (am-3744a)
    • Back Drive Force: 0.1 ft-lb [0.14 N-m]

    • Overall Length: 5.3 in.

    • Shaft Hardness: 45-50 Rockwell C
    • Stall Current: 11.5 A
    • Stall Torque: 2.734 ft-lb [3.707 N-m]
    • Ticks Per Revolution: 1680
    • Voltage: 12 VDC

body_html:

  • This is ONLY the motor that is featured in the NeveRest Series gearmotors. This motor has a pinion gear pre-installed that interfaces with either our NeveRest Classic gearboxes (12T) or our NeveRest Orbital and gearboxes (17T). To produce a reasonable amount of torque for either driving your robot or moving a mechanism you will need one of these gearboxes or a different reduction method such as the NeveRest Sport series gearboxes. Watch this video for step by step instruction on a similar gearbox, and reference this document for steps on using it with the NeveRest Sport. We recommend choosing the 12T option for these as that gear is easier to remove.

title: Blue Roughtop Nitrile Track Timing Belt
body_html:
This is an endless, spliced belt, designed to be a track drive component for a mobile robot.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • It's made of steel-reinforced urethane timing belt, with an abrasion-resistant blue nitrile roughtop tread. The center of the timing belt includes a "V" for tracking the belt to the center of a grooved pulley. We have pulleys (am-3298a) specially designed to drive this belt.

    This belt is featured in the Raptor Track Drive Module and Rhino Track Drive Module (am-3322)

    AndyMark also offers a similar flat urethane black belt (am-4017).

    During normal use of this belt, the blue rubber tread may begin to delaminate (split apart from the timing belt). If this happens, please follow these steps to fix the belt:

    • Keep the belt mounted to the drive pulley mechanism (do not remove the belt from your robot)
    • Clean both surfaces where the delamination is happening, removing debris and dirt
    • Take time to allow the cleaned area to dry
    • Use a rubber to rubber adhesive such as super glue. This has great bonding properties to adhere the tread (roughtop carbox, in this case) to the urethane timing belt material.
    • Keep pressure on the newly glued area by moving this area over an end pulley. This applies continual contact between the rubber and timing belt.
    • Wait 20-30 minutes for the adhesive to cure.
    • Length: 65.5 in., spliced endless loop
    • Material: Carbox Nitrile
    • Teeth: 131
    • Weight: 1.63 lbs.
    • Width: 2.01 in.

title: Rhino Track Drive Module
body_html:
The Rhino Track Drive is a tank track module utilizing a two inch wide timing belt tread.
  • Description
  • What's in the Box?
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • Four robust molded pulleys direct the path of a belt, driven by an optional AndyMark gearbox or transmission. Two of these modules can be used to create a tank drive-base. The Rhino Track Drive features rigid, 3/16 inch thick aluminum plates and an easily adjustable belt tension mechanism. This is an ambidextrous module, so it can be used for the left or right side just by switching the plates from one side to the other. The Rhino Track Drive Module ships in an un-assembled kit. Please see the assembly instructions for assembly assistance.

    This module includes one belt. In order to create a typical drive system for most applications, two modules will need to be purchased. We suggest the use of four (4) pieces of 1 in. wide extrusion as bracing structure between two Rhino Track Drive Modules. Pictures of this setup version are shown below.

    During normal use of the Blue Nitrile Tread, the blue rubber may begin to delaminate (split apart from the timing belt). If this happens, please follow these steps to fix the belt:

    • Keep the belt mounted to the drive pulley mechanism (do not remove the belt from your robot)
    • Clean both surfaces where the delamination is happening, removing debris and dirt
    • Take time to allow the cleaned area to dry
    • Use a rubber to rubber adhesive such as super glue. This has great bonding properties to adhere the tread to the urethane timing belt material.
    • Keep pressure on the newly glued area by moving this area over an end pulley. This applies continual contact between the rubber and timing belt.
    • Wait 20-30 minutes for the adhesive to cure.

    Not Included:

    • A gearbox, such as the Toughbox Mini, as shown in the layout print and example pictures.
    • Bumper brackets are also not included.

    Belt Tension:

    • Proper belt tension is detailed in this document.

title: PicoBox Solo
body_html:
The PicoBox Solo is a robust mounting solution for chain driven mechanisms.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • The PicoBox gearboxes are designed specifically for FIRST Tech Challenge teams. These highly configurable gearboxes are a robust solution for teams to make fine adjustments to the output speed and torque of drivetrains, mechanisms and more. All PicoBox gearboxes are designed to work with other building systems that FIRST Tech Challenge teams are familiar with, because they are built to work around a base 16 mm center-to-center hole pattern. The flanges on the PicoBox gearboxes are reversible while maintaining a base 16 mm hole pattern.

    The PicoBox Solo is a unique member of the PicoBox line. It's purpose is to provide a robust mounting solution for chain driven mechanisms with its included 16 tooth #25 series Ninja Star sprocket, and 6 mm bearing to support the end of a NeveRest Classic motor shaft. This product is ideal to pair with robot mechanisms such as arms, intakes, elevators and more!

    Motor Input:

title: PicoBox Uno
body_html:
he PicoBox Uno is a single reduction, single motor input gearbox that utilizes steel 32DP gears.
  • Description
  • Gearbox Ratios
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • The PicoBox gearboxes are designed specifically for FIRST Tech Challenge teams. These highly configurable gearboxes are a robust solution for teams to make fine adjustments to the output speed and torque of drivetrains, mechanisms and more. All PicoBox gearboxes are designed to work with other building systems that FIRST Tech Challenge teams are familiar with, because they are built to work around a base 16 mm center-to-center hole pattern. The flanges on the PicoBox gearboxes are reversible while maintaining a base 16 mm hole pattern. Additionally, all PicoBox gearboxes utilize the same plate design as both the input plate and output plate, allowing for different configurations such as mounting the motor and output shaft onto the same side of the gearbox.

    This gearbox accepts one NeveRest motor as its input, and has a robust steel 6 mm D shaft for it's output.

    Gear Ratios:
    The kit comes with 3 different gear ratio options, so that you can experiment and understand how changing the gear ratio affects the driving performance of the TileRunner.
    • 45 Tooth and 35 Tooth gear combination yields a 1:0.78 over drive
    • Two 40 Tooth gears yield a 1:1 ratio
    • 35 Tooth and 45 Tooth gear combination yields a 1:1.28 reduction

    Motor Input:
    The PicoBox Uno is not compatible with the NeveRest Motor Only (am-3104) or NeveRest Orbital line, as the PicoBox Uno requires the use of the NeveRest Classic gearbox as part of the motor input assembly. The PicoBox Uno accepts up to one of the following motors at a time:
    • NeveRest Classic 40 (am-2964a)
    • NeveRest Classic 60 (am-3103)
    Weight: ~1 lbs.

    Product Usage:
    All AndyMark gearboxes require grease for proper operation and long life. We suggest using our red tacky grease, am-2768. We also encourage that the user powers the gearbox continuously for 30 minutes without grease to allow the gear teeth to wear in. While we do design with short runtimes in mind, this 'run in' period for smooth gearbox operation, is recommended. Once the run in period is complete, clean the gears, then thoroughly grease the gear teeth to ensure smooth operation. The gears should regularly be cleaned, inspected, and greased again to ensure proper operation and longer life of your gearbox.


    Individual Components within Kit:
    • 4 - Nut, Nylock Jam 1/4-20 (am-1102)
    • 6 - Screw, SHCS M3-0.5 x 6 mm (am-1254)
    • 8 - Screw, Hex Head, 6-32 x 1/2 in. (am-1436)
    • 4 - Screw, Hex Head, 1/4-20 x 1 3/4 in.
    • 2 - 6 mm D Bore Double Boss Nub w/Set Screw (am-3215)
    • 2 - 6x12x4 Flanged Bearing (am-3377)
    • 4 - Spacer for PicoBox (am-3406)
    • 2 - Gear, 40T for PicoBox (am-3407)
    • 1 - Gear, 35T for PicoBox (am-3408)
    • 1 - Gear, 45T for PicoBox (am-3409)
    • 2 - PicoBox Uno Plate (am-3423)
    • 1 - Spacer, aluminum, 12.7 mm OD x 6.15 mm ID x 9 mm (am-3426)
    • 1 - 6 mm D Shaft, 100 mm, plated (am-3226-100)
    • 1 - Red Tacky Grease (am-2768)
    If you need the output shaft to be a 1/2 in. Hex, check out the 6 mm D to 0.5 in. Hex-Shaft Adapter (am-3744a)

  • Please contact support@andymark.com if you do not see a Ratio Table

  • Description

  • This item is restricted for shipment in some countries. Please check international shipping restrictions before ordering.

It can be connected to the Talon SRX for power and communication via UART, or it can be wired to the CAN bus while powered from a separate 12V source. The Pigeon 2.0 eliminates the need for on-boot calibration and temperature calibration and does not require stillness upon boot-up.

title: USB 2.0 to Ethernet Adapter
body_html:
This adapter plugs into any usb port and an Ethernet cable.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • Don't let a bad Ethernet port cause you to lose a match again! A loose Ethernet port on a driver station can lead to loss of connection to your robot during a match and can even keep your driver station from connecting to the field at all. Keep one of these adapters on your robot cart or in a back pocket and ensure you always have a way to connect to the field. In fact, keep three with you. That way if an alliance partner cannot connect their driver station you can help them and the FTA out!

    This adapter plugs into any usb port on your driver station and an Ethernet cable at the field. For the best results at the field, ensure your firewall settings are disabled, wifi is disabled, and the adapter is securely plugged in.

body_html:
S3 Tubing is part of AndyMark's system for building Simple Super Structure.
  • Description

  • S3 Tubing is part of AndyMark's system for building Simple Super Structure! These custom aluminum tubes are designed to allow FIRST Tech Challenge and others building toaster-to-microwave-sized robots a bolt-together solution for rigid, robust structures. We sweated all the details with S3 Tubing, including:

    • Custom-extruded 16 mm square profile, chosen to allow ample compatibility with common FTC parts while taking up less space on volume-limited robots.
    • Fully-boxed profile, which is stronger than C-channels for long life.
    • Designed for 6-32 hardware throughout to maintain harmony with our other FTC-friendly parts and the most popular building systems in FTC. Whether it's a Nub, a TileRunner, a PicoBox, or a NeveRest Sport, it'll find a home here.

  • The PicoBox gearboxes are designed specifically for FIRST Tech Challenge teams. These highly configurable gearboxes are a robust solution for teams to make fine adjustments to the output speed and torque of drivetrains, mechanisms and more. All PicoBox gearboxes are designed to work with other building systems that FIRST Tech Challenge teams are familiar with, because they are built to work around a base 16 mm center-to-center hole pattern. The flanges on the PicoBox gearboxes are reversible while maintaining a base 16 mm hole pattern.

    The PicoBox LEO is a unique member of the PicoBox line. Its purpose is to provide a mounting solution for chain driven mechanisms with it's included 16 tooth #25 series Ninja Star sprocket. This product is ideal to pair with robot mechanisms such as intakes, shooters and more!

    The LEO is named after Low Earth Orbit. Satellites such as the International Space Station orbit in Low Earth Orbit which is the first 100 to 200 miles of space. For more information about orbits, go here!

    Motor Input:
    The PicoBox LEO is not compatible with the NeveRest Motor Only (am-3104) or the NeveRest Classic series of gearmotors.
    The PicoBox LEO is designed specifically for the NeveRest Orbital gearmotor series.

  • The PicoBox gearboxes are designed specifically for FIRST Tech Challenge teams. These highly configurable gearboxes are a robust solution for teams to make fine adjustments to the output speed and torque of drivetrains, mechanisms and more. All PicoBox gearboxes are designed to work with other building systems that FIRST Tech Challenge teams are familiar with, because they are built to work around a base 16 mm center-to-center hole pattern. The flanges on the PicoBox gearboxes are reversible while maintaining a base 16 mm hole pattern.

    The PicoBox MEO is a single reduction, single motor input gearbox that utilizes steel 32DP gears. This gearbox accepts one NeveRest 3.7 motor as it's input, and has a robust steel 6 mm D shaft for it's output.

    The MEO is named after Mid Earth Orbit. Medium Earth orbits range in altitude from 2,000 km (1,240 miles) to just below geosynchronous orbit at 35,786 kilometers (22,236 mi). Also known as an intermediate circular orbit. These are "most commonly at 20,200 kilometers (12,600 mi), or 20,650 kilometers (12,830 mi), with an orbital period of 12 hours.     The PicoBox Solo is not compatible with the NeveRest Motor Only (am-3104) or the NeveRest Classic series of gearmotors.
    The PicoBox MEO is designed specifically for the NeveRest Orbital series of gearmotors.

    Product Usage:
    All AndyMark gearboxes require grease for proper operation and long life. We suggest using our red tacky grease, am-2768. We also encourage that the user powers the gearbox continuously for 30 minutes without grease to allow the gear teeth to wear in. While we do design with short runtimes in mind, this 'run in' period for smooth gearbox operation, is recommended. Once this is completed, thorough grease of the gear teeth periodically to ensure smooth operation.

body_html:
The PicoBox gearboxes are designed specifically for FIRST Tech Challenge teams, built to work with a base 16mm hole pattern.

  • The PicoBox gearboxes are designed specifically for FIRST Tech Challenge teams. These highly configurable gearboxes are a robust solution for teams to make fine adjustments to the output speed and torque of drivetrains, mechanisms and more. All PicoBox gearboxes are designed to work with other building systems that FIRST Tech Challenge teams are familiar with, because they are built to work around a base 16 mm center-to-center hole pattern. The flanges on the PicoBox gearboxes are reversible while maintaining a base 16 mm hole pattern.

    The PicoBox GEO is a single reduction, double motor input gearbox that utilizes steel 32DP gears. This gearbox accepts two NeveRest Orbital gearmotors as its input, and it has a robust steel 6 mm D shaft for its output. The motors can be installed on each side of the output shaft, or the motors can be installed side by side with the output shaft installed on one of the ends of the gearbox. The PicoBox GEO can also be built as a double reduction, single motor input, single output gearbox with an included 36 mm D shaft to facilitate stacking two gears on a cluster shaft that would be installed in the middle of the gearbox.

    The GEO is named after Geostationary Earth Orbit. Geosynchronous orbits are also called geostationary. Satellites that stay above a location on Earth are in geosynchronous Earth orbit, or GEO. These satellites orbit about 23,000 miles (37,015 km) above the equator and complete one revolution around Earth precisely every 24 hours. For more information about orbits, go here!

title: DeCIMate Assembled Gearbox
body_html:
This pre-assembled gearbox is used with AndyMark RedLine Motors to give more power than a CIM motor.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • This gearbox comes with two AndyMark RedLine Motors (am-3775) to give you a total package of about the same output speed, size and weight of one CIM motor, but with almost 700 watts of power! Use this anywhere you would use a CIM with its identical output shaft and mounting geometry. Please note, this gearbox is louder than most due to the open case and and extremely fast spinning gears.

    Possess your own 775 motors and want to save money? Only want to use one motor? This gearbox is available in a motor-less, unassembled version by the part number am-3745g.

    Product Usage:
    All AndyMark gearboxes require grease for proper operation and long life. We suggest using our Red Tacky Grease, am-2768. We also encourage that the user powers the gearbox continuously for 30 minutes without grease to allow the gear teeth to wear in. While we do design with short run times in mind, this 'run in' period for smooth gearbox operation, is recommended. For this gearbox some tape over the front vent holes of the motors during the run-in is recommended to prevent metal dust from getting inside the motor. Once this is completed, thoroughly grease the gear teeth periodically to ensure smooth operation.


    *Specifications are theoretical with two AndyMark RedLine Motors installed.
    • Motor Input: 775
    • Motor Quantity: 1, 2
    • Ratio: 3.75:1
    • Weight: 2.1 lbs.

title: BattHawk Pack of 4
body_html:
BattHawk is a voltmeter which can take the place of a battery flag.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • The BattHawk is designed and manufactured by East Central Indiana Robotics, FRC Team 1720, PhyXTGears. It measures the battery voltage without discernible drain during a robot competition time frame. This product is especially useful for rows of batteries. When a BattHawk is plugged into each battery in a line, the status of all batteries is always visible. This allows for monitoring of the charge of each battery with just a glance. The purchase of the BattHawk helps fund ongoing efforts for FRC team 1720.

    BattHawk Features:


    • Immediate visual check of all batteries not currently being charged or in use
    • Voltage range from 4.5 volts to 30 volts (Accuracy 1%)
    • Low trickle-drainage (16 ma, one five thousandth the current of an FRC robot)
    • Measures state of charge (SOC)
    • Replaces the Battery Flag
    • Instant comparison of available batteries
    • Provie grab-and-o of the highest charged battery in the pit or robot cart
    • Mates with FRC battery connector (Anderson Power Products SB-50A 600V)
    • Intended for continuous use while at competitions
    • Comes with a convenient, cinch drawstring storage/transportation pouch
    • Made of durable polypropylene
    • Colored bright green for easy identification
    • Keyed for correct instant insertion
    • When used with am-2070a Power Pole Adapter, BattHawk can be used with TETRIX® or FTC batteries
    • The BattHawk is angled such that the voltage display is not blocked during insertion

    Battery Life with BattHawk:


    A BattHawk may be left in a battery for weeks without harming the battery. Batteries should NOT be stored with the BattHawk inserted as it will eventually discharge the battery fully (about 47 days).

    How to Use:


    1. Charge Battery
    2. Unplug from Charger
    3. Test Battery with Battery Beak
    4. Plug in BattHawk
    5. See Constant Visual Status of all Batteries!

    Recommended Usage Cases:


    • 12.0 and below: Seriously? Put that one on the charger!
    • 12.1-13.0: Practice ready: go break your robot!
    • 13.1-13.3: Competition ready: head directly to Einstein!

    Testimonials:


    "Our team used the BattHawk to be sure our batteries are ready to go as we zoom out of the pits to the next match! It has allowed us to grab a fresh battery when we are in a hurry from the practice field directly to a match!" - John

    "During the playoffs, we had four charged batteries on our cart ready to go. In the heat of the battle it's sometimes confusing which batteries are fully charged and which one just came from our robot's last match. With a BattHawk plugged into every battery, the choice is obvious! Just grab and go!" - Mike

    "Just for grins, we inserted several BattHawks into our batteries back at home, and the battery stayed fully charged for over a week when we stopped our test. We calculated that our standard 18Ah (amp hour) robot batteries would last 1,125 hours with a continuously attached BattHawk. That's 46+ days! Yep, we love this device!" - Rob

    If you have product questions please contact via email at phyxtgears@gmail.com.

    Note:


    Please know this is a totally different product than the popular Battery Beak, which tests batteries under a load. The Battery Beak's test is a battery health condition test along with a load test, while the BattHawk is simply a voltmeter. We suggest a robot competition team to have 1 or 2 Battery Beaks and at least 4 BattHawks.

Measures distance, velocity, and signal strength of cooperative and non-cooperative targets at distances from zero to more than 40 meters. Offering the highest performance available in a single beam ranging sensor in its class. The new LIDAR-Lite has all of the same specifications as the legacy sensor: Up to 40-meter range capability with 1cm resolution, small size, low power consumption, and lightweight.

    • Min detectable signal: 1nW - 256 integrated bursts (maximum integration time)

    • I2C communication operates at 100kbits/s or 400kbits/
    • Broadly compatible with the most basic of I2C drivers and most micro-controller boards. A status register (0x01) can be queried to indicate sensor status
    • The previous measurement value can be read anytime during an acquisition until it is overwritten by a new value. No need to wait for the sensor to become available to read data.
    • Individual sensors can have a unique I2C address
    • The base address of 0x62 can be used as the default in single sensor applications and it will also be available in multi-sensor applications as a broadcast address to initiate a command to all the LIDAR-Lites on the I2C bus

title: PicoBox Servo
body_html:
These highly configurable gearboxes are a robust solution for teams to make fine adjustments to the output speed and torque of drivetrains, mechanisms and more.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • The PicoBox gearboxes are designed specifically for FIRST Tech Challenge teams. All PicoBox gearboxes are designed to work with other building systems that FIRST Tech Challenge teams are familiar with, because they are built to work around a base 16 mm center-to-center hole pattern. The flanges on the PicoBox gearboxes are reversible while maintaining a base 16 mm hole pattern. Additionally, all PicoBox gearboxes utilize the same overall plate style for both the input plate and output plate, allowing for different configurations such as mounting the servo and output shaft onto the same side of the gearbox.

    The PicoBox Servo is a unique member of the PicoBox line. Its purpose is to provide a robust mount for a HiTec standard servo, Futaba standard servo, or any standard servo. This Gearbox includes a 16 tooth #25 series Ninja Star sprocket and a Servo Nub. This product is ideal for when mechanisms need a stronger anchor point but don't need the power and torque of a motor, or when you want to use a servo with set screw and a standard 6 mm output shaft. This incredible gearbox comes in under 0.5 pounds.

    Compatible Servos:
    This gearbox does not include a servo, so you can install the right one for your application. We have tested and confirmed it works great with am-2587. Other servos may work as well if they feature a 24 Tooth C1 Spline and fit inside the servo body cavity of the servo plate. The servo cavity is 1.6 inches tall by 0.8 inches wide.

title: PicoBox Super Servo
body_html:
These highly configurable gearboxes are a robust solution for teams to make fine adjustments to the output speed and torque of drivetrains, mechanisms and more.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • The PicoBox gearboxes are designed specifically for FIRST Tech Challenge teams. All PicoBox gearboxes are designed to work with other building systems that FIRST Tech Challenge teams are familiar with, because they are built to work around a base 16 mm center-to-center hole pattern. The flanges on the PicoBox gearboxes are reversible while maintaining a base 16 mm hole pattern. Additionally, all PicoBox gearboxes utilize the same overall plate style for both the input plate and output plate, allowing for different configurations such as mounting the servo and output shaft onto the same side of the gearbox.

    The PicoBox Super Servo is a single reduction, single servo input gearbox that utilizes steel 32DP gears. This gearbox accepts one HiTec standard servo, Futaba standard servo, or any other standard servo as its input, and has a robust steel 6 mm D shaft for it's output. Both axles could be tied to their own output implements allowing for easy synchronized movements.

    Gear Ratios:
    The kit comes with 3 different gear ratio options, so that you can experiment and understand how changing the gear ratio affects the driving performance of the TileRunner.
    45 Tooth and 35 Tooth gear combination yields a 1:0.78 overdrive
    Two 40 Tooth gears yield a 1:1 ratio
    35 Tooth and 45 Tooth gear combination yields a 1:1.28 reduction

    Compatible Servos:
    This gearbox does not include a servo, so you can install the right one for your application. We have tested and confirmed it works great with am-2587. Other servos may work as well if they feature a 24 Tooth C1 Spline and fit inside the servo body cavity of the servo plate. The servo cavity is 1.6 inches tall by 0.8 inches wide.

    Product Usage:
    All AndyMark gearboxes require grease for proper operation and long life. We suggest using our red tacky grease, am-2768. We also encourage that the user powers the gearbox continuously for 30 minutes without grease to allow the gear teeth to wear in. While we do design with short runtimes in mind, this 'run in' period for smooth gearbox operation, is recommended. Once the run-in period is complete, clean the gears, then thoroughly grease the gear teeth to ensure smooth operation. The gears should regularly be cleaned, inspected, and greased again to ensure proper operation and longer life of your gearbox.
    • Motor Input: Servo
    • Motor Quantity: 1
    • Ratio: 1:0.78, 1:1, 1:1.28
    • Weight: 0.68 lbs. Including Servo

title: Four Slot CKD Pneumatic Manifold
body_html:
This 4-bank aluminum manifold will distribute compressed air to multiple paths from a single source.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • Now, you can put your CKD valves on a light weight 4-bank aluminum manifold. Let's build one!
    1. Purchase the Manifold base (am-3982), listed on this very page.
    2. Fill the 4 slots. You must pick a total of exactly 4 items from these 3 choices (or use older CKD valves you may already have)*
      1. CKD Single Solenoid Valve (am-3983)
      2. CKD Double Solenoid Valve (am-4002)
      3. Blank cover (am-4003) for every unwanted slot
    3. Choose your valve fittings:
      1. If your manifold has 4 valves, buy the Fitting Pack for 4-Valve Manifold (am-3982_f4)
      2. If your manifold has 3 valves, buy the Fitting Pack for 3-Valve Manifold (am-3982_f3)
      3. If your manifold has 1 or 2 valves, buy qty 2 or 4 of the usual CKD fitting (am-2384)
      4. You cannot just use the usual CKD fitting (am-2384) on all the valves since the valves are packed so tightly together on the manifold. Every other valve needs fitting extensions (am-4004). These are included in the above Fitting Packs.
    4. Manifold fittings:
      1. Air needs to be supplied to the manifold. Two universal 1/8 in. pipe thread to 1/4 in. tube fittings are included. These screw into the middle ports on either end of the manifold. You may want to plug one of them if you are only using one manifold on your robot. You can do this with the included plug. Alternatively you can add the second universal fitting to the other side of the center port to extend pressure to a second manifold or high pressure storage.
    5. Assemble your manifold:
      1. Mount each valve in it's position, with its rubber gasket between the valve and manifold.
      2. Install the fittings so that the extensions are placed on every other valve. This gives proper spacing for mounting fittings.
    *You can remove the metal bases of popular CKD single solenoid (am-2344) and CKD double solenoid (am-2343) valves and place them directly on one of these manifolds.
    • Material: 6061-T6 Aluminum
    • Maximum Pressure: 125 psi
    • Weight: 0.35 lbs.

title: 3 in. BB Mecanum Wheels
body_html:
The 3 in. BB Mecanum Wheel is a small, lightweight, slim omni-directional wheel.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • The 3 in. BB Mecanum Wheel is a lightweight, slim wheel. BB stands for Ball Bearing, referring to the bearings inside of each roller that make for incredibly smooth motion. This wheel was optimized for an FTC Chassis with additional features to make these wheels more versatile than ever before. The hub nut pockets can take a recessed 10-32 screw or nut allowing for both live and dead axle setups. Note: These wheels ship as an unassembled kit.
    A full set consists of 2 "right" wheels and 2 "left" wheels. The "right" and "left" refer to the direction the rollers are pointing when viewing the wheel as if you're about to get run over by the wheel itself. If the roller in the middle of the wheel points up and to the right, it's a "right" wheel, and up and to the left would be a "left" wheel.

    The configuration of these "right" and "left" wheels is important to a mecanum drive system! Be aware that the "right" wheel should not mean that it goes on the right side of your robot. The proper configuration would be to have the wheels create an "X" pattern when viewing your robot from above and drawing lines parallel to the rollers as viewed.
    This means that a "right" wheel would be the FRONT RIGHT, and the REAR LEFT position, while the "left" wheel would be in the FRONT LEFT, and REAR RIGHT, of your robot when viewed from above. All 4 wheels are required to make a Mecanum drive holonomic system work properly.

    Wheel Bores:

    • 3/8 in. Hex Bore

title: Black Flat Urethane Track Timing Belt Tread
body_html:
This is an endless track drive belt, designed to be a track drive component for a mobile robot.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • It's made of steel-reinforced urethane timing belt, with a flat, black urethane coating for high traction. The center of the timing belt includes a "V" for tracking the belt to the center of a grooved pulley. We have pulleys (am-3298a) specially designed to drive this belt.

    This belt works with the Raptor Track Drive Module and Rhino Track Drive Module (am-3322)

    AndyMark also offers a similar belt with blue roughtop coating (am-3288).

    During normal use of this belt, the urethane tread may begin to de-laminate (split apart from the timing belt). If this happens, please follow these steps to fix the belt:

    • Keep the belt mounted to the drive pulley mechanism (do not remove the belt from your robot)
    • Clean both surfaces where the delamination is happening, removing debris and dirt
    • Take time to allow the cleaned area to dry
    • Use a rubber to rubber adhesive such as super glue. This has great bonding properties to adhere the tread (roughtop carbox, in this case) to the urethane timing belt material.
    • Keep pressure on the newly glued area by moving this area over an end pulley. This applies continual contact between the rubber and timing belt.
    • Wait 20-30 minutes for the adhesive to cure.
    • Length: 65.5 in., spliced endless loop
    • Material: Urethane
    • Teeth: 131
    • Weight: 1.75 lbs.
    • Width: 2 in.
