title: Peanut Drill Guide
body_html:
This guide provides proper alignment for drilling into Peanut Extrusion.

  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • Our Peanut Extrusion (am-3090) is named for the peanut-shaped rib in the middle that provides additional strength for attachments. For proper alignment to the connecting piece you want to hit that rib--but we know that's not always easy when the surface is curved. This 3D-printed hole guide will help by clipping onto the peanut extrusion for better alignment. There are three sets of holes and 2 additional handy features. Two set of holes are for drilling a horizontal pair of holes. These holes will either be entirely through the internal "peanut" feature vertically or miss the "peanut" feature and pierce just the center ribs. There is also a pair of vertical holes for drilling either into the extruded holes at a 90 degree angle or for drilling on either side of the "peanut" feature. There is also a slot letting you see the end of the extrusion and lining up the horizontal set of holes with the end as well as a gap to let you clamp the guide in place while you drill.

    Parts Included:


    • 1 - 3D printed Peanut Extrusion Guide
    • 2 - 0.5 in OD 0.25 in Long Steel Press Fit Bushing (am-1511)
    • Bushing Material: Steel
    • Printed Material: PLA

These two wires must be connected to each other with this resister inbetween to terminate the CAN bus

This kit can be used vertically, horizontally or at any angle in between. This easy to assemble kit attaches to S3 extrusions so that you can customize the length of each stage and carriage. title: 6 in. Pneumatic Wheel Kit
body_html:
This is a kit of the 6 in. version of our pneumatic wheel.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • Here is a six-inch version of the high-traction wheel kit you know and love which includes a grippy rubber tire, a pneumatic inner tube, and a strong plastic hub. These parts are shipped to you in kit form. The unique aspect about this product is the competition-ready hub. The hub accepts any 150x50mm tire and inner tube, 1.125 in. (outside diameter) ball bearings (2 per wheel are needed), and the mounting holes needed to install hardware to be sprocket-driven or hub-driven. This wheel ships as a separate tire, inner tube, and hub halves. Assembly is required.

    Important Notes:

    • Tube pinching: When assembling the tube within the two hub halves, be careful not to pinch the tube rubber between the plastic hub halves. If assembled with the tube pinched between the hub halves, the tube may puncture and leak.

    RPM Rating and notes:
    These wheels are designed to be propulsion wheels for driving a robot or wheel chair. The design intent is to be contacting the ground, being driven by a gearbox at a maximum speed of approximately 500 rpm (which results in approximately 13 feet/sec).

    Within some applications, this wheel has been used as a shooter of objects, spinning at a very high rpm. For these applications, a higher rpm shows that the wheel may wobble, since the valve stem is mounted off to one side of the center of the wheel hub. We have seen properly balanced wheels, using securely mounted hardware (longer screws, washers) that can handle 5,000 rpm. When spinning this wheel at speeds up to 5,000 rpm, please take proper safety precautions.

    Included Items:

    • Tire for 6 Inch Pneumatic Wheel (Metric Size 150x50mm), am-2474
    • Inner Tube for 6 Inch Pneumatic Wheel, with 45 Degree Stem (for 150x50mm Tire), am-2475
    • Hub Assembly for 6 inch Pneumatic Wheel, which includes two (2) black plastic hub halves and six (6) 4-40 x1 Pan Head Phillips thread rolling screws

    NOT Included Hardware:

    • Bearings
    • #10 Screws and Nuts Needed to Mount a Hub (2 Inch Long Screws are Needed) or a Sprocket (2.25 Inch Long Screws are Needed)
    • Aluminum Hub, if driven by a shaft
    ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    Wheel Structure:

    The hub halves are held together with the #4-40 screws. This wheel can accept #10-32 screws for mounting sprockets or hubs, but these are NOT included since different length screws are needed to mount hubs or sprockets. These #10 screws can be mounted to the included 1.875 inch diameter bolt circle. The hub halves need to be assembled together so that the valve stem clearance holes line up. Locating features are present for easy alignment.

    Assembly:
    This is a helpful step by step guide on how to assemble the wheel, it can be a bit tricky.
    Usage:
    With Axle and Hub:
    • In order to drive this wheel with a hub, use six (6) #10-32x2.25 screws (am-1156) and six (6) #10-32 nylock nuts (am-1042).
    With Sprocket:
    • In order to drive this wheel with a plate sprocket, use six (6) #10-32x2.25 screws (am-1156) and six (6) #10-32 nylock nuts (am-1042).
    • Two (2) bearings are needed for this wheel when being driven by a sprocket. Use bearings with a 1.125 inch outer diameter. No flange is needed on either of the bearings.
    Use as a caster:
    • If you want to let this wheel spin without being driven, you will need to install two (2) bearings with 1.125 inch outer diameter.
    • Bolt Pattern: 6 holes, 0.20 diameter on 1.875 in. diameter bolt circle
    • Bore: 0.96 in. diameter through hole, with two 1.125 in. diameter bearing pockets
    • Diameter: 6 in.
    • Load Capacity: 120 lbs.
    • Material: Black Polycarbonate, gray rubber
    • Maximum Pressure: 35 psi
    • Tread Width: 1.39 in.
    • Valve Stem: The valve stem may stick out up to 0.25 in. from the hub
    • Weight: 0.71
    • Width Across Middle: 2.190 in.

title: 4:1 Sport Add-on Stage
body_html:
This Add-on Stage will reduce the spped and increase the torque of an blue Sport Gearbox.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • This accessory for blue Sport gearboxes is an easy-to-use device that adds an extra 4:1 overall ratio to the input of any blue Sport gearbox. Because every Sport gearbox uses a 4:1 ratio as it’s input stage, this makes for a simple addition to reduce the speed and increase the torque of any blue sport gearbox. Simply install this device between your desired input motor (such as a RedLine, CIM, Falcon or Dual Motor Input,) and the body of the gearbox, and you’re good to go. For example, you can turn a 4:1 gearbox that you already have into a 16:1 gearbox with this accessory.

    Product Note: It is possible to exceed the maximum rated output torque when using this product with high powered motors and higher ratio configurations of the blue Sport gearboxes. Please carefully consider these load ratings when choosing to use this 4:1 add-on stage in these configurations.

    Each add-on stage comes with two 10-32 Socket Head Cap Screws used to mount the motor block.

    • Gear Material: Steel
    • Material: Aluminum
    • Ratio: 4:01
    • Weight: 0.23 lbs.

title: 2.25 in. HD Mecanum Vectored Intake Wheel
body_html:
• Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • Found most commonly on the front intake rollers of FIRST Robotics Competition robots, these 2.25 in. HD Mecanum Vectored Intake wheels are a perfect simple solution to serialize game pieces on the floor before they enter your robot. They also help extend the effective "width" of an intake to help draw game pieces in from the corners of your robot. They can also be used to help serialize game pieces within a conveyor system inside your robot and pair great with our 2.25 in. Compliant Wheels. Made of high strength materials, these intake wheels are designed to be tough enough to withstand the rigors of FRC match play with rollers that are better retained for in high impact situations on the playing field.

    The 2.25 in. HD Mecanum Vectored Intake Wheel comes as an unassembled kit of parts. Each order for these wheels will contain two 1/16 in. Allen Wrenches (am-4405) which are required for assembly. Because of the size of the hex socket on the fasteners, it is important to use sharp-ended fresh hex keys for assembly, and not ball-end drivers.

    A traditional full set consists of 2 "right" wheels and 2 "left" wheels. The "right" and "left" refer to the direction the rollers are pointing when viewing the across it's rolling axis. If the roller in the middle of the wheel points up and to the right, it's a "right" wheel, and up and to the left would be a "left" wheel.

    If using these as a drive wheel for a small robot platform, the configuration of these "right" and "left" wheels is important. Be aware that the "right" wheel does not mean that it goes on the right side of your robot. The proper configuration would be to have the wheels create an "X" pattern when viewing your robot from above and drawing lines parallel to the rollers as viewed. This means that a "right" wheel would be the FRONT RIGHT, and the REAR LEFT position, while the "left" wheel would be in the FRONT LEFT, and REAR RIGHT, of your robot when viewed from above. All 4 wheels are required to make a Mecanum drive holonomic system work properly.

    Wheel Design:

    Six nylon rollers spin smoothly on high strength steel axles, retained into 0.09 in. steel side plates. The steel plates geometrically interface with two interior polycarbonate hubs, which form the interior of the wheel. These steel plates rest against the flange on the injection molded hub, which increases the overall bending strength of each roller seat. The two injection molded polycarbonate interior hubs are held together by the tension in all six roller axles around the wheel, with steel roll pins pressed in around the hex bore to keep everything aligned.

title: RadioLink T8S Wireless Controller & R8EF Receiver
body_html:
This eight-channel controller and receiver combination works for any robot-driving situation.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • The next generation of robot remote control is here. Want features? It has features, so many features, more than you can count! This eight-channel controller receiver combination works for any and all situations. Connect it via USB micro to a computer and adjust settings as you see fit! Need to change on the fly? Change settings over Bluetooth from your smartphone!

    The return spring for both joysticks is preinstalled to provide perfect tank-style robot driving. To use as a throttle controller, remove the spring return and enjoy flight style control.

    Controller Charging

    The built-in battery of T8S is 1S lithium. When the voltage becomes low, the green indicator will flash with a warning tone. Make sure to charge the battery in time to avoid possible damage by over-discharge. T8S charging is as simple, just plug in the micro USB data cable to a computer or portable charger. It takes approximately 40 minutes to fully charge T8S.

    Binding

    1. Put the transmitter and the receiver close to each other (about 1 foot) and power on the receiver.
    2. Switch on the transmitter, and the LED on R8EF will start flashing slowly.
    3. There is a black binding button (ID SET) on the side of the receiver. Press the button until the LED is flashing quickly and release, meaning the binding process is ongoing.
    4. When the LED stops flashing and is always on, binding is complete. If not successful, the LED will flash slowly, if this happens, repeat the above steps.
    • Current: Controller <150 (±5) mA, Receiver <30 mA
    • Dimensions: Controller 6.4 in. x 3.76 in. x 2.24 in., Receiver 0.71 in. x 0.51 in.
    • Frequency Band: 2.4 GHz ISM (2400 MHz ~ 2483.5 MHz)
    • Frequency Band Width: 400KHz
    • Interface(s): 2.4 GHz Wireless, PWM, Bluetooth, Micro USB
    • Modulation Mode: GFSK
    • Receiver Weight: 6.6 g
    • Transmission Rate: 38 kbps
    • Transmitter Power: 20 db
    • Voltage: Controller 3.7 - 4.2 V, Receiver 4.8 ~ 6 V

title: Ratchet Sport
body_html:
This ratchet assembly works with the Sport gearboxes to control back drive.

  • Description
  • What's in the Box?
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • This kit is the perfect addition to a Sport Gearbox to control back drive. This all-metal ratchet assembly is as rock solid and easy to use as the Sport gearboxes it works with. In fact, you can even add it to an already installed gearbox without changing the motor or the gearbox. Just detach the motor, add the ratchet to it, and reattach the assembly.

    The ratchet was designed from the ground up with releasability in mind, meaning you can release the ratchet UNDER LOAD in just about any application you can come up with, including supporting a full weight FRC robot without having to lift any of the weight off! This also opens up a whole new set of potential mechanism applications as there is an off-the-shelf solution for easy in-match actuation via a small air cylinder or Servo.

    This product can be set to lock either clockwise or counterclockwise depending on how it is assembled. Check out the assembly instructions in the Documentation tab of this page for more details. Please note, when using the servo, the standard cover plate is replaced by the servo version of the cover plate.

    To learn more about this ratchet, check out our video about it!

title: Circuit Playground Express Crickit
body_html:
This Crickit interface board connects up with the Circuit Playground Express controller to expand its connectivity.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • You can find these components used in one of our three Skitter robot options.

    Bolt-on your Circuit Playground using the included stand-off bolts and start controlling motors, servos, solenoids.

    The Crickit is powered by seesaw an I2C-to-whatever bridge firmware. So you only need to use two data pins to control the huge number of inputs and outputs on the Crickit. All those timers, PWMs, sensors are offloaded to the co-processor.

    Features:

    • 4 - Analog or Digital Servo control with 16-bit timers
    • 2 - Bi-directional brushed DC motor control, 1 Amp current limited each, with 8-bit PWM speed control
    • 4 - High current "Darlington" 500mA drive outputs with kick-back diode protection. For solenoids, relays, large LEDs, or one uni-polar stepper
    • 4 - Capacitive touch sensors with alligator-pads
    • 8 - Signal pins, digital in/out or analog inputs
    • 1 - NeoPixel driver with 5V level shifter
    • 1 - Class D, 4-8 ohm speaker, 3W-max audio amplifier
    All are powered via 5V DC, so you can use any 5V-powered servos, DC motors, steppers, solenoids and, relays. This board will not work with different voltage components.

    Please note this robot board does not require any soldering but you will need a power supply and a Circuit Playground Express to go along with the Crickit and these are not included!
    • Manufacturer: Adafruit Industries
    • Manufacturer Part #: 3093
    • Voltage: 5 VDC

title: FeatherWing Crickit
body_html:
• Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • This Cricket interfaces with Feather style controllers with stacking headers. We use it to interface the ESP32 Feather in our Skitter robots. Plug in the same ESP32 Feather or any other and your robot projects are on their way!

    This Crickit is powered by seesaw, an I2C-to-whatever bridge firmware. So you only need to use two I2C data pins to control the huge number of inputs and outputs on the Crickit. All those timers, PWMs, sensors are offloaded to the co-processor.

    The only thing that is not managed by seesaw is the audio output. On our Feather M0's this is a true analog output (DAC) and you can play audio clips with CircuitPython or Arduino.

    You get to use all the non-I2C signal pins on your feather and get a boat-load of extra in/out pins, motor controllers, capacitive touch sensors, a NeoPixel driver and amplified speaker output. It complements & extends your Feather so you can still use all the goodies, including stacking FeatherWings on top.

    Features:

    • 4 - Analog or Digital Servo control with 16-bit timers
    • 2 - Bi-directional brushed DC motor control, 1 Amp current limited each, with 8-bit PWM speed control

title: Circuit Playground Express
body_html:
Circuit Playground Express is the perfect controller for newcomers to electronics and programming.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • This board can be programmed with Microsoft MakeCode block-based, Javascript programming, or even Arduino IDE. Then, you can use the same board to try CircuitPython, with the Python interpreter running right on the Express.

    The round board has alligator-clip pads around it so you don't have to solder or sew to make it work. You can power it from USB, a AAA battery pack, or with a Lipoly battery. Circuit Playground Express has built-in USB support. Built in USB means you plug it in to program it and it just shows up, no special cable or adapter required. Just program your code into the board then take it on the go!

    Circuit Playground Express Features:
    • 10 - mini NeoPixels
    • 1 - Motion Sensor (LIS3DH triple-axis accelerometer with tap detection, free-fall detection)
    • 1 - Temperature Sensor (thermistor)
    • 1 - Light Sensor
    • 1 - Sound Sensor (MEMS microphone)
    • 1 - Mini speaker with class D amplifier
    • 2 - Push Buttons
    • 1 - Slide Switch
    • 1 - Infrared receiver and transmitter
    • 8 - alligator-clip friendly input/output pins
    • Includes I2C, UART, 8 pins that can do analog inputs, multiple PWM output
    • 7 pads can act as capacitive touch inputs and the 1 remaining is a true analog output
    • Green "ON" LED so you know its powered
    • Red "#13" LED for basic blinking
    • Reset button
    • ATSAMD21 ARM Cortex M0 Processor, running at 3.3V and 48MHz
    • 2 MB of SPI Flash storage, used primarily with CircuitPython to store code and libraries.
    • MicroUSB port for programming and debugging
    • USB port can act like serial port, keyboard, mouse, joystick or MIDI!

    The infrared receiver and transmitter can receive and transmit any remote control codes, as well as send messages between Circuit Playground Expresses. Can also act as a proximity sensor.

    • Manufacturer: Adafruit Industries
    • Manufacturer Part #: 3333

title: ESP32 Feather Board with Stacking Headers
body_html:
This tiny controller can be at the center of some powerful and cool projects
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • This ESP32 microcontroller is designed into a Feather Board format with stacking headers. !
    This board is packed with features! Built in USB-to-Serial converter, automatic bootloader reset, Lithium Ion/Polymer charger, and lots of GPIOs. This board interfaces with the Crickit for Feathers.
    This version of the ESP32 Feather comes with stacking headers already soldered in so its ready for instant gratification and Feather fun!

    That module nestled at the end of this Feather contains a dual-core ESP32 chip, 4 MB of SPI Flash, tuned antenna, and all the passives you need to take advantage of this powerful new processor. The ESP32 has both WiFi and Bluetooth Classic/LE support. That means it's perfect for just about any wireless or Internet-connected project.

    The ESP32 is a perfect upgrade from the popular ESP8266. In comparison, the ESP32 has way more GPIO, plenty of analog inputs, two analog outputs, multiple extra peripherals (like a spare UART), two cores so you don't have to yield to the WiFi manager, and a much higher-speed processor!

    Please note: Not all peripherals are fully documented with example code, and there are some bugs still being found and fixed. We got all of our FeatherWings working under Arduino IDE, so you can expect things like I2C and SPI and analog reads to work. But other elements are still under development. For that reason, we recommend this Feather for makers who have some experience with microcontroller programming and not as a first dev board.

    Espressif ESP32 MCU Features and Specs:
    • Processor - 240 MHz dual-core Tensilica LX6 Microcontroller
    • Memory - 520 KB SRAM
    • Wireless Connectivity
      • 802.11b/g/n HT40 Wi-Fi transceiver, baseband, stack, and LWIP
      • Integrated dual-mode Bluetooth (classic and BLE)
    • Ultra-low noise analog amplifier
    • 4 MByte flash include in the WROOM32 module
    • On-board PCB antenna
    • Hall sensor
    • 10x capacitive touch interface
    • 32 kHz crystal oscillator
    • 3 x UARTs (only two are configured by default in the Feather Arduino IDE support, one UART is used for bootloading/debug)
    • 3 x SPI (only one is configured by default in the Feather Arduino IDE support)
    • 2 x I2C (only one is configured by default in the Feather Arduino IDE support)
    • 12 x ADC input channels
    • 2 x I2S Audio
    • 2 x DAC
    • PWM/timer input/output available on every GPIO pin
    • OpenOCD debug interface with 32 kB TRAX buffer
    • SDIO master/slave 50 MHz
    • SD card interface support
    • Bluetooth: Dual Mode Classic and BLE
    • Inputs: 12xADC
    • Interfaces: WiFi, Bluetooth, Micro USB, I2S Audio, I2C, SPI, UART, GPIO, Capacitive Touch Sensor, DAC, ADC, IR, Pulse Counter
    • Manufacturer: Adafruit Industries
    • Wireless: 802.11 b/g/n HT40, Baseband, Stack, LWIP

title: RadioLink Basics Control Bundle
body_html:
This bundle features the basic components to power the RadioLink radio and receiver.
  • Description
  • What's in the Box?
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • The next generation of robot remote control is here. Want features? It has features, so many features, more than you can count! This eight-channel controller receiver combination works for any and all situations. Connect it via USB micro to a computer and adjust settings as you see fit! Need to change on the fly? Change settings over Bluetooth from your smartphone!

    The return spring for both joysticks is preinstalled to provide perfect tank-style robot driving. To use as a throttle controller, remove the spring return, and enjoy flight style control.
    Image is only representative of exact items, PWM cable is shorter than it appears.

    Controller Charging

    The built-in battery of T8S is 1S lithium. When the voltage becomes low, the green indicator will flash with a warning tone. Make sure to charge the battery in time to avoid possible damage by over-discharge. T8S charging is as simple, just plug in the micro USB data cable to a computer or portable charger. It takes approximately 40 minutes to fully charge T8S.

    Binding

    1) Put the transmitter and the receiver close to each other (about 1 foot) and power on the receiver.
    2) Switch on the transmitter, and the LED on R8SM will start flashing slowly.
    3) There is a black binding button (ID SET) on the side of the receiver. Press the button until the LED is flashing
    quickly and release, meaning the binding process is ongoing.
    4) When the LED stops flashing and is always on, binding is complete. If not successful, the LED will flash slowly, if this happens, repeat the above steps.

  • Included Items

    • 1 - RadioLink Controller and Receiver (am-4422)
    • 1 - Power Converter 12/24 VDC to 5 VDC (am-3068)
    • 1 - 12 in. 22 Gauge PWM Wire (am-0693b)

title: Absolute Orientation IMU Fusion Breakout
body_html:
This Adafruit sensor makes taking orientation data and turning into an actual 3D space easy.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • This item is restricted for shipment in some countries. Please check international shipping restrictions before ordering.

    This absolute marvel of an orientation sensor makes taking orientation data and turning into an actual 3D space easy! The Absolute Orientation IMU Fusion Breakout in a Stemma QT format has a smart 9-DOF sensor that does the sensor fusion all on its own.

    The Absolute Orientation IMU Fusion Breakout can output the following sensor data:

    Absolute Orientation (Euler Vector, 100Hz) - Three axis orientation data based on a 360° sphere
    Absolute Orientation (Quaternion, 100Hz) - Four point quaternion output for more accurate data manipulation
    Angular Velocity Vector (100Hz) - Three axis of 'rotation speed' in rad/s
    Acceleration Vector (100Hz) - Three axis of acceleration (gravity + linear motion) in m/s^2
    Magnetic Field Strength Vector (20Hz) - Three axis of magnetic field sensing in micro Tesla (uT)
    Linear Acceleration Vector (100Hz) - Three axis of linear acceleration data (acceleration minus gravity) in m/s^2
    Gravity Vector (100Hz) - Three axis of gravitational acceleration (minus any movement) in m/s^2
    Temperature (1Hz) - Ambient temperature in degrees Celsius

    Here you can find a tutorial on assembly, wiring, CircuitPython & Arduino libraries, and Processing graphical interface, and more!

title: West Coast Drive Style Bearing Block Kit
body_html:
• Description
  • What's in the Box?
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • A West Coast style drivetrain can be finicky to create without precision machining capabilities. This Bearing Block Kit makes it much more accessible for teams to create high performance West Coast Drive style platforms with limited fabrication resources. Simply drill a clearance hole for a shaft to pass through your drive rail, pull your chain or belt tight, and clamp it down with the included hardware. Featuring machined pockets to capture 10-32 Nylock Nuts, these blocks can be used and reused without worrying about damaging threads upon installation. Because each block is the same part, you can keep the screw heads pointing to the outside of your robot for easy maintenance.

    This unassembled kit ships with enough hardware to provide significant clamping pressure to help keep your powertrain components tensioned properly, and can withstand upwards of 1500lbs of force along the axis of the tube when properly installed. This means that for most FRC use cases, a team can install these without the need for tensioning devices to keep things aligned.

    The AndyMark West Coast Drive Bearing Block Kit is designed to be used with flanged ball bearings with a 1.125 in. outer race, such as our FR8ZZ-HexHD Bearing.

    The AndyMark West Coast Drive Bearing Block Kit also includes mounting geometry for components that utilize 2 in. and 1.875 in. bolt circles, such as motors, gearboxes, sprockets, hubs and gears. This makes this product great for many uses outside of your drivetrain, such as a robust interface to make a rotary arm, or an easy-to-use mounting interface for motors to power your mechanisms. The bearing plate is also 2 in. wide, making it perfect to keep two 20DP gears (of which the total teeth add up to 80) meshed together.

title: Tube Roller
body_html:
This Roller kit is everything you need to make a custom-length roller up to 36 inches.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • This Roller kit is everything you need to make a custom-length roller - up to 3 feet long! This economical roller system uses Hex Spacer extrusion as a core with incredibly grippy surgical tubing as the outer surface. The roller is designed to be supported with any 3/8 in. round bearings. Use these rollers for intakes to get game pieces into your robot quickly, or chain multiple rollers together to make an internal conveyer system. You can mix and match the ends to get a roller that simply sits and spins with two idle ends, or a roller that is powered at both ends with two hex inserts.
    Assembly:
    • Cut the hex spacer extrusion to the desired length for the roller.
      • This will be the total distance between your bearings minus the 1.25 in. for the hex end and the 0.25 in. for the idle end.
    • Slide the surgical tubing over the hex spacer extrusion.
      • There are a few methods for this, but we recommend lubricating the hex spacer extrusion with an alcohol based hand sanitizer, and pushing the surgical tubing over. The alcohol will evaporate and leave the two components stuck together.
    • Trim the surgical tubing so that ~1 in. of hex spacer extrusion is exposed at either end.
    • Measure 3/4 in. from both ends of the hex spacer extrusion and drill 0.201 in. cross hole to secure the inserts.
      • You do not have to worry about aligning these holes to the hex profile
    • Place the inserts into the tube and secure via provided #10-32 screws through the cross hole
    • Place your motion components and hex spacers onto the hex end.
    • Place the assembly into position in your structure between two 3/8 in. round bearings.
    • Insert the shoulder bolts through the bearings and thread them into the inserts in the roller.
    Items Included:
    • 1 - Tube Roller Idle End Insert Kit (am-4679)
    • 1 - Tube Roller Hex End Insert Kit (am-4680)
    • 1 - 36 in. 0.5 in. Hex Aluminum Spacer Stock (am-3896-3)
    • 1 - 5/8 in. ID, 7/8 in. OD Black Surgical Tubing (am-4656-3)
    • Diameter: ~ 1 in.
    • Durometer: 50A
    • Surface Material: Latex Rubber

title: Distance Sensor with Pulse Width Output
body_html:
This sensor takes continuous distance measurements as long as it is enabled.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • This sensor takes continuous distance measurements as long as it is enabled, up to 120 in. (300 cm) away. It uses a simple digital pulse width interface (similar to a hobby servo control signal) which can then be timed by a microcontroller using a single digital microcontroller pin. Eye-safe laser light is emitted from a short-range lidar module to hit the nearest object and then be reflected back. The sensor measure the time it takes to receive the reflected light to gauge distance with a resolution of 2 mm.

    This sensor has three connections that are necessary for use: VIN, GND, and Out. The connections work with standard 0.1 in. Headers.

    • Connect the VIN to a 3V - 5.5V source
    • Connect GN to 0 volts
    • The sensor outputs digital pulses from the OUT pin.
    The board has an optional ENABLE pin that can be driven low to put it into a low-power state that consumes approximately 0.4 mA. This pin can be accessed through a via or its neighboring surface-mount pad on the back side labeled “EN”.

    Note: The maximum range of 300 cm is only achievable for high-reflectance objects in good ambient conditions. Lower-reflectivity targets or poor ambient conditions will reduce the maximum range.

    Sample code can be found here.

    • Field of View: 15°
    • Mounting Hole: One #2 or M2 Screw
    • Operating Voltage: 3.0 V - 5.5 V
    • Output Type: Digital Pulse Width
    • Range: 4 cm - 300 cm
    • Sampling Rate: 30 Hz
    • Size: 0.85 in. x 0.35 in. x 0.136 in.
    • Supply Current: 30 mA
    • Weight: 0.004 lbs.

title: 4 in. BB Mecanum Wheels
body_html:
The 4 in. BB Mecanum Wheel is a slim, smoother-rolling version of the onmi-directional motion wheel.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • The 4 in. BB Mecanum Wheel is a lightweight, slim wheel. BB stands for Ball Bearing, referring to the bearings inside of each roller that make for incredibly smooth motion. This wheel was optimized for an FTC Chassis, such as the MecanAM Chassis. These wheels ship as an unassembled kit.
    A full set consists of 2 "right" wheels and 2 "left" wheels. The "right" and "left" refer to the direction the rollers are pointing when viewing the wheel as if you're about to get run over by the wheel itself. If the roller in the middle of the wheel points up and to the right, it's a "right" wheel, and up and to the left would be a "left" wheel.

    The configuration of these "right" and "left" wheels is important to a mecanum drive system! Be aware that the "right" wheel should not mean that it goes on the right side of your robot. The proper configuration would be to have the wheels create an "X" pattern when viewing your robot from above and drawing lines parallel to the rollers as viewed.
    This means that a "right" wheel would be the FRONT RIGHT, and the REAR LEFT position, while the "left" wheel would be in the FRONT LEFT, and REAR RIGHT, of your robot when viewed from above. All 4 wheels are required to make a Mecanum drive holonomic system work properly.

    Wheel Bores:

    • Nub Bore
      • Perfect for FTC robots
      • Compatible with Nubs as an attachment point to shafts and motors
      • A 6-32 screw is perfect for attaching to a Nub:
        • (am-1567) 1.5 in. for a standard HD Nub or Servo Nub
        • (am-1568) 1.5 in.-1.75" for an XL HD Nub
    • 1/2 in. Hex and 3/8 in. Hex Bore
      • Bore molded directly into polycarbonate center body
      • BE AWARE: these have a limited torque capacity. Recommended use in light duty applications (FTC robots or non-drive train FRC items such as an intake)

    Roller and Axle Design:

    The black TPU rubber roller has a durometer rating of 60A. The roller has a Polycarbonate core, and rides on a stationary brass tube.

    Wheel Structure:

    12 rubber rollers are sandwiched between 2 steel plates. The two plates are held together by bolting the rollers in place.

    These wheels can be purchased individually as Left or Right wheels.

    Included Items:

    Individual Hardware within Each Wheel:
    • 2 - BB Mecanum Plates
    • 1 - Hub
    • 12 - Individual 4 in. Wheel Rollers
    • 24 - Axle Bearings
    • 12 - Brass Inner Sleeves
    • 12 - M3 x 0.5 in Nylock Nuts
    • 12 - M3 x 0.5 45 mm SHCS Screws
    ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    Usage:

    • Nub Bore Wheels
      • For FTC Robots: If attached to a shaft or NeveRest motor, these parts are needed for each wheel.
      • Attach an AndyMark Nub or Tetrix Motor Hub directly to the Nub Bore version of this wheel.
        • Four 1.5 in long 6-32 screws such as am-1567 are required per wheel for this method.
    • 1/2 in. Hex Bore : Direct Drive
      • Simple! with a 1/2 in. hex shaft
    • 3/8 in. Hex Bore : Direct Drive
      • Simple! with a 3/8 in. hex shaft

    Learn how to position these wheels by watching this video.

    • Body Material: Outer
    • Bolt Pattern: 6 holes (0.159 in. diameter) on a 1.875 in. diameter circle
    • Bore: Nub Bore, 3/8 in. Hex, 1/2 in. Hex
    • Diameter: 4 in. [100 mm]
    • Number of Rollers: 12
    • Roller Axle: Brass Tube
    • Roller Bearing Material: Steel Ball Bearings
    • Roller Durometer: 60A
    • Roller Material: Outside
    • Total Width: 1.52 in.
    • Weight: Single wheel: 0.84 lbs.
    • Weight Capacity: 40 lbs. per set of 4
    • Width Inset: 1.23 in.

title: 4 in. HD Mecanum Wheels
body_html:
Mecanum wheels provide easy and efficient omni-directional motion for robots.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • The 4 in. HD Mecanum wheel comes fully assembled and ready to go and comes in three different bore sizes.

    A full set consists of 2 "right" wheels and 2 "left" wheels. The "right" and "left" refer to the direction the rollers are pointing when viewing the wheel as if your about to get run over by the wheel itself. If the roller in the middle of the wheel points up and to the right, it's a "right" wheel, and up and to the left would be a "left" wheel.

    The configuration of these "right" and "left" wheels is important to a mecanum drive system! Be aware that the "right" wheel should not mean that it goes on the right side of your robot. The proper configuration would be to have the wheels create an "X" pattern when viewing your robot from above and drawing lines parallel to the rollers as viewed.
    This means that a "right" wheel would be the FRONT RIGHT, and the REAR LEFT position, while the "left" wheel would be in the FRONT LEFT, and REAR RIGHT, of your robot when viewed from above. All 4 wheels are required to make a Mecanum drive holonomic system to work properly.
    Using these for an intake? This has been a great use of these wheels as well! The angle of these wheels help drive the object in one direction, so you can pull in the object at the same time as pushing at an angle from the intake.
    This version of the wheel can handle a 200 pound load per wheel for a total 800 pound load if using as drive wheels! The interior body of this wheel is made of molded black polycarbonate, while the perimeter side plate is made of 1/8 inch thick steel, zinc plated. The perimeter plate is riveted to the interior body, and each perimeter bent tab rests on the interior body rim. This support allows for the wheel to handle more load.

    Wheel Bores:

    • Bearing Bore
      • the Original 4 in. HD Mecanum wheel
      • Use with a 1/2 in. hex hub for Heavy Duty and hex applications
    • Nub Bore
      • Perfect for FTC robots
    • 1/2 in. Hex
      • Bore molded directly into polycarbonate center body
      • While still being able to handle 200lbs of load, BE AWARE: these have a limited torque capacity. Recommended use in light duty applications (FTC robots or non-drive train FRC items such as an intake)
    • 3/8 in. Hex
      • Bore molded directly into polycarbonate center body
      • While still being able to handle 200lbs of load, BE AWARE: these have a limited torque capacity. Recommended use in light duty applications (FTC robots or non-drive train FRC items such as an intake)

    Roller and Axle Design:

    The gray urethane rubber roller (am-3027) has a durometer rating of 80A. The roller has a Nylon core, and rides on a stationary brass tube.

    Wheel Structure:

    9 rubber rollers are sandwiched between 2 steel plates. The steel plates are riveted to two interior polycarbonate hubs, which form the interior of the wheel. The two interior pieces are held together by the fastening technique of the rollers being attached.

    These wheels can be purchased individually as Left or Right wheels. They are sold without hubs, sprockets, or bearings.

    Included Items:

    Individual Hardware within Each Wheel:
    • 2 - HD Mecanum Plates
    • 2 - Hubs
    • 9 - Individual 4 in. Wheel Rollers
    • 9 - Brass Axle Tubes
    • 9 - M3 x 55 mm SHCS
    • 9 - M3 x 0.5 in Nylock Nut
    • 18 - 0.125 in diameter Rivets
    ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    Usage:

    Nub Bore Wheels

    For FTC Robots: If attached to a shaft or NeveRest motor, these parts are needed for each wheel.

    • Attach an AndyMark Nub or Tetrix Motor Hub directly to the Nub Bore version of this wheel.
      • Four 2in long 6-32 screws such as am-1499 are required per wheel for this method.
    Bearing Bore Wheels
    With Axle and Hub    : If driven by a shaft, these parts are needed for each wheel
    • A hub that matches the size of the drive shaft.
    • #10-24 thread-forming screws are used to fasten a hub to the wheel (we suggest 6).
    • 1/8 x 1/8 x 3/4 steel machine key (am-1043) is needed, one per wheel
    With Sprocket: If driven by a sprocket, these parts are needed for each wheel
    • Flanged ball bearings (qty. 2) with 1.125 in. od: either 3/8 in. inside diameter (am-0209), or 1/2 in. i.d.
    • A sprocket (type A) with a bolt hole circle of 1.875 in. diameter mounts to the wheels' interior bolt pattern.
    • #10-24 thread-forming screws are used to fasten a hub to the wheel (we suggest 6).

    Hex Bore
    Direct Drive:
    • Simple! with a hex shaft

    Learn how to position these wheels by watching this video.

    • Body Material: Outer
    • Bolt Pattern: 6 holes (0.2 in. diameter) on a 1.875 in. diameter circle
    • Bore: Bearing Bore, Nub Bore, 1/2 in. Hex, 3/8 in. Hex
    • Diameter: 4 in. [100 mm]
    • Forward / Reverse Coefficient of Friction: 0.7 (on tight pile carpet)
    • Load Capacity: 200 lbs. per wheel
    • Number of Rollers: 9
    • Roller Axle: Brass Tube
    • Roller Bearing Material: Nylon spinning over brass tube
    • Roller Durometer: 80A
    • Roller Material: Outside
    • Sideways Coefficient of Friction: 0.6 (on tight pile carpet)
    • Weight: 0.9 lbs. per wheel
    • Width Across Middle: 2.18 in.

body_html:

  • Specifications

  • These custom designed collar clamps have been designed specifically with FIRST Robotics Competition teams in mind. The one-piece collar clamp is a nice fractional width to make shaft stackups easy. The clamping force is provided by a socket head screw, 10-32 for the HD which is bigger than most used in the competition marketplace, and 4-40 for the thin versions for fitting in tight spots. This provides a high-strength clamping solution that shouldn't strip out when you need it most. You can even replace the 10-32 screw if it becomes lost with the screws historically used in the AM14U family of chassis. These thoughtfully designed collar clamps also have small bosses on each side. This allows these collar clamps to be installed directly adjacent to bearings without rubbing on the outer races for smooth operation.

title: Robits Pass Through Gearbox
body_html:
The Robits Pass Through Gearbox is a great way of transforming motion on your robot.
  • Description
  • What's in the Box?
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • The ability to have the shaft go beside the motor allows users to save space and opens up options when space is a concern. This gearbox accepts any length of our 3/8 in. hex shaft or Robits Hex Shafts allowing you to potentially drive a mechanism all the way across your robot.

    Additionally, the integrated nut pockets in the gearbox plates removes the need for a 3/8 wrench when attaching this gearbox to your structure.

    Note: When mounting this gearbox, we recommend a #10 washer under the fastener heads to provide adequate clearance with the gears.

    Compatibility:

    NeveRest Orbitals -> The input has our traditional NeveRest mounting pattern so you can orient your motor in 45° increments. Pair this with any of our 6 mm D to 3/8 Hex Adapters (not included).

    NeveRest Hex -> The input has both the traditional NeveRest M3 mounting pattern as well as the 10-32 mounting pattern. Retain the gear on the shaft using a #10 washer (not included) and a 10-32 x 1/2IN screw (not included) .


  • Included Components:

    • 2 - Robits Motion Bushing for 375IN Hex (am-5021)
    • 2 - 30 Tooth 20DP 0.375 in. Hex Bore Plastic Gear (am-5020_30)
    • 1 - Robits 0.375 in. Hex Shaft 4 in. Long (am-5003-0400)
    • 2 - Robits Pass Through Plate (am-5023)
    • 4 - Spacer, 0.375 OD x 0.194 ID x 1.00 Long Nylon (am-1696)
    • 2 - Spacer, 0.430 ID x 0.500 OD x 0.250 Long Aluminum (am-1698)
    • 2 - Screw, SHCS, 10-32 x 0500 (am-1002)
    • 4 - Screw, SHCS, 10-32 x 1750 (am-1048)
    • 2 - #10 Steel Washer (am-1026)
    • 4 - 10-32 Nylock Jam Nut (am-1063)
    • 4 - M3-0.5 x 12 mm Socket Head Cap Screw with Thread Patch (am-1706)

    Note: Kits after March 5th have (2) 1/4IN long spacers in lieu of (1) 1/2IN long spacer.

    • Motor Input: NeveRest Orbital Motor
    • Output Shaft: 0.375 Hex Shaft
    • Ratio: 1:01
    • Weight: 0.39 lbs.

title: Servo Range Extender Wire
body_html:
This Servo Range Extender is primarily suggested when using a standard RC transmitter with a SPARKmini Brushed DC Motor Controller.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • This Servo Range Extender is primarily suggested when using a standard RC transmitter with a SPARKmini Brushed DC Motor Controller. It converts the typical PWM signal output of 1000μs to 2000μs to the SPARKmini's expected input PWM signal of 500μs - 2500μs.

title: 10 ft Black Polybelt Roll
body_html:
This is a 10' length of flat, black, 1 in wide polyurethane belt.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • Polybelt is particularly useful in FRC for a myriad of applications. This 1 in. wide belt comes in a 10 foot roll. Cut it into custom lengths to suit your needs.

    To form a continuous belt, cut the polybelt to length, ensuring the end is square. Next heat both ends of the belt until they start to melt and press the melted ends together. Be sure to keep the belt ends aligned when welding them together to help the belt run straight. When the belt cools, extra melted polyurethane can be trimmed back if desired and it's ready to be used.

    We recommend the use of a Belt Welding Hot Knife (am-5284) and our Belt Welder Clamp (am-5285) for ease of polybelt welding.

    Watch this video for more detailed instructions on the use of Polybelt and its welding tools:

title: 12V Individually Addressable LED Light Strip 16.4 ft
body_html:
This 12V flexible color-changing LED strip can be programed with a variety of colors and patterns.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • This 12V flexible color-changing LED strip is perfect for robot lighting whether it's for fun or feedback. When used with an RGB controller such as the roboRIO (sold separately) one can control the color output including solid colors (red, green, blue, etc.) gradient fading, and blinking. Each LED is individually addressable, allowing for the display of multiple colors simultaneously. This light strip features a signal break-point continuous transmission, meaning that when one LED gets damaged, the others will keep working. It accepts 5V or 6V data input and is compatible with our 4pin LED Connector.

    NOTE: This strip's color pattern is actually GRB, rather than RGB. When controlling it, you may have to flip the values of red and green to produce the desired color.

title: 4pin LED Connector
body_html:
This solderless, clamping connector is intended to be used with our 12V Addressable LED Light Strip.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • This solderless, clamping connector is intended to be used with our 12V Addressable LED Light Strip. To use, simply cut off some of the clear insulation on the LED strip to reveal the gold contacts, insert into the connector, and pinch to close. The connector will pierce each contact, providing a robust and long lasting connection. The wires on the other side can be swapped around by prying up that side of the connector and simply sliding out each wire and sliding them back in to the desired channels. That way you can keep your power & ground colors consistent and remove the redundant data line if you choose not to use it!

title: Robot Parts Cart
body_html:
This cart holds storage containers or battery shelves for a portable work area.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • Looking for a "Super Pit" without the enormous cost and transport size? This Parts Cart is for you! It's a modular solution for a pit or workshop storage and work area. It is compact enough to fit three in a Prius with the seats down for easy transport to and from events, but large enough to hold a good portion of your well organized supplies needed to build and service a robot. The carts have latches hidden under the worktop that allow you to latch them side-to-side to form one long workstation in a pit, or back-to-back for an island work area in a shop.

    Each Parts Cart comes included with 8 storage containers and 3 battery shelves that you can mix and match to fill the 8 slots in the cart. The battery shelves do best on the lowest spots to keep the center of gravity low. If using the cart for batteries, there are handy-dandy mounting holes for the NOCO 3 Bank Battery Chargers up the side.

    The four swivel casters make for an incredibly easy-to-transport cart. Two of the casters have locks on them to secure the cart when at rest. A black HDPE top, makes for a perfect work surface once locked down.

    Prototypes for this cart were developed in partnership with FRC Team 3940 CyberTooth over the past several years and taken to dozens of events to refine the design to what you see here today.

    A 3D file is available at the bottom of the page if you wish to customize the handles of the totes as seen in one of the product photos.

    The cart ships unassembled.

    For more information about Pit Organization, watch our video about the subject!

title: Polybelt Welder Clamp Tool
body_html:
This assembly is used to easily make custom lengths of Polybelt loops.
  • Description

  • This assembly is used to easily make custom lengths of Polybelt loops. A set of thumb screws are included to make clamping belt ends simple. The over-center linkage makes it easy to bring the melted belt ends together and hold in place while the belt cools. This makes installing a custom-length polybelt loop on your mechanism easier than ever. This tool can accept polyurethane belts up to 2 inches wide.
    Usage:
    1.) Place cut belt ends under the clamping plates with about 1/16 inch hanging toward the inside. If using 1 or 2 inch wide belt, align the sides to the alignment notches.
    2.) Tighten the thumb screws on both sides until the belt is snug.
    3.) Using a heat source like our Belt Welding Hot Knife (am-5284) heat up the belt ends until they start to melt.
    4.) Once the ends start to melt, immediately close the clamp to press the melted ends together.
    5.) When cool, loosen the thumb screws on the slotted sides of the clamp (note indicator holes for reference) and remove clamp from belt.

title: Arduino Mega 2560 Rev3
body_html:
The Arduino Mega 2560 is a microcontroller board based on the ATmega2560.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • It has 54 digital input/output pins (of which 15 can be used as PWM outputs), 16 analog inputs, 4 UARTs (hardware serial ports), a 16 MHz crystal oscillator, a USB connection, a power jack, an ICSP header, and a reset button. It contains everything needed to support the microcontroller; simply connect it to a computer with a USB cable or power it with a AC-to-DC adapter or battery to get started. The Mega 2560 board is compatible with most shields designed for the Uno and the former boards Duemilanove or Diecimila.

    Programming

    The Mega 2560 board can be programmed with the Arduino Software (IDE). For details, see the reference and tutorials.

    The ATmega2560 on the Mega 2560 comes preprogrammed with a bootloader that allows you to upload new code to it without the use of an external hardware programmer. It communicates using the original STK500 protocol.

    You can also bypass the bootloader and program the microcontroller through the ICSP (In-Circuit Serial Programming) header using Arduino ISP or similar.

    The ATmega16U2 (or 8U2 in the rev1 and rev2 boards) firmware source code is available in the Arduino repository. The ATmega16U2/8U2 is loaded with a DFU bootloader, which can be activated by:

    On Rev1 boards: connecting the solder jumper on the back of the board (near the map of Italy) and then resetting the 8U2.
    On Rev2 or later boards: there is a resistor that pulling the 8U2/16U2 HWB line to ground, making it easier to put into DFU mode. You can then use Atmel's FLIP software (Windows) or the DFU programmer (Mac OS X and Linux) to load a new firmware. Or you can use the ISP header with an external programmer (overwriting the DFU bootloader).

    Warnings

    The Mega 2560 has a resettable polyfuse that protects your computer's USB ports from shorts and overcurrent. Although most computers provide their own internal protection, the fuse provides an extra layer of protection. If more than 500 mA is applied to the USB port, the fuse will automatically break the connection until the short or overload is removed.

    Power

    The Mega 2560 can be powered via the USB connection or with an external power supply. The power source is selected automatically.

    External (non-USB) power can come either from an AC-to-DC adapter (wall-wart) or battery. The adapter can be connected by plugging a 2.1mm center-positive plug into the board's power jack. Leads from a battery can be inserted in the GND and Vin pin headers of the POWER connector.

    The board can operate on an external supply of 6 to 20 volts. If supplied with less than 7V, however, the 5V pin may supply less than five volts and the board may become unstable. If using more than 12V, the voltage regulator may overheat and damage the board. The recommended range is 7 to 12 volts.

    The power pins are as follows:
    • Vin. The input voltage to the board when it's using an external power source (as opposed to 5 volts from the USB connection or other regulated power source). You can supply voltage through this pin, or, if supplying voltage via the power jack, access it through this pin.
    • 5V. This pin outputs a regulated 5V from the regulator on the board. The board can be supplied with power either from the DC power jack (7 - 12V), the USB connector (5V), or the VIN pin of the board (7-12V). Supplying voltage via the 5V or 3.3V pins bypasses the regulator, and can damage your board. We don't advise it.
    • 3V3. A 3.3 volt supply generated by the on-board regulator. Maximum current draw is 50 mA.
    • GND. Ground pins.
    • IOREF. This pin on the board provides the voltage reference with which the microcontroller operates. A properly configured shield can read the IOREF pin voltage and select the appropriate power source or enable voltage translators on the outputs for working with the 5V or 3.3V.

    Memory

    The ATmega2560 has 256 KB of flash memory for storing code (of which 8 KB is used for the bootloader), 8 KB of SRAM and 4 KB of EEPROM (which can be read and written with the EEPROM library).

    Input and Output

    Each of the 54 digital pins on the Mega can be used as an input or output, using pinMode(),digitalWrite(), and digitalRead() functions. They operate at 5 volts. Each pin can provide or receive 20 mA as recommended operating condition and has an internal pull-up resistor (disconnected by default) of 20-50 k ohm. A maximum of 40mA is the value that must not be exceeded to avoid permanent damage to the microcontroller.

    In addition, some pins have specialized functions:
    • Serial: 0 (RX) and 1 (TX); Serial 1: 19 (RX) and 18 (TX); Serial 2: 17 (RX) and 16 (TX); Serial 3: 15 (RX) and 14 (TX). Used to receive (RX) and transmit (TX) TTL serial data. Pins 0 and 1 are also connected to the corresponding pins of the ATmega16U2 USB-to-TTL Serial chip.
    • External Interrupts: 2 (interrupt 0), 3 (interrupt 1), 18 (interrupt 5), 19 (interrupt 4), 20 (interrupt 3), and 21 (interrupt 2). These pins can be configured to trigger an interrupt on a low level, a rising or falling edge, or a change in level. See the attachInterrupt() function for details.
    • PWM: 2 to 13 and 44 to 46. Provide 8-bit PWM output with the analogWrite() function.
    • SPI: 50 (MISO), 51 (MOSI), 52 (SCK), 53 (SS). These pins support SPI communication using theSPI library. The SPI pins are also broken out on the ICSP header, which is physically compatible with the Arduino /Genuino Uno and the old Duemilanove and Diecimila Arduino boards.
    • LED: 13. There is a built-in LED connected to digital pin 13. When the pin is HIGH value, the LED is on, when the pin is LOW, it's off.
    • TWI: 20 (SDA) and 21 (SCL). Support TWI communication using the Wire library. Note that these pins are not in the same location as the TWI pins on the old Duemilanove or Diecimila Arduino boards.
    The Mega 2560 has 16 analog inputs, each of which provide 10 bits of resolution (i.e. 1024 different values). By default they measure from ground to 5 volts, though is it possible to change the upper end of their range using the AREF pin and analogReference() function.
    There are a couple of other pins on the board:
    • AREF. Reference voltage for the analog inputs. Used with analogReference().
    • Reset. Bring this line LOW to reset the microcontroller. Typically used to add a reset button to shields which block the one on the board.

    Communication

    The Mega 2560 board has a number of facilities for communicating with a computer, another board, or other microcontrollers. The ATmega2560 provides four hardware UARTs for TTL (5V) serial communication. An ATmega16U2 (ATmega 8U2 on the revision 1 and revision 2 boards) on the board channels one of these over USB and provides a virtual com port to software on the computer (Windows machines will need a .inf file, but OSX and Linux machines will recognize the board as a COM port automatically. The Arduino Software (IDE) includes a serial monitor which allows simple textual data to be sent to and from the board. The RX and TX LEDs on the board will flash when data is being transmitted via the ATmega8U2/ATmega16U2 chip and USB connection to the computer (but not for serial communication on pins 0 and 1).

    A SoftwareSerial library allows for serial communication on any of the Mega 2560's digital pins.

    The Mega 2560 also supports TWI and SPI communication. The Arduino Software (IDE) includes a Wire library to simplify use of the TWI bus; see the documentation for details. For SPI communication, use the SPI library.

    Physical Characteristics and Shield Compatibility

    The maximum length and width of the Mega 2560 PCB are 4 and 2.1 inches respectively, with the USB connector and power jack extending beyond the former dimension. Three screw holes allow the board to be attached to a surface or case. Note that the distance between digital pins 7 and 8 is 160 mil (0.16 in.), not an even multiple of the 100 mil spacing of the other pins.

    The Mega 2560 is designed to be compatible with most shields designed for the Uno and the older Diecimila or Duemilanove Arduino boards. Digital pins 0 to 13 (and the adjacent AREF and GND pins), analog inputs 0 to 5, the power header, and ICSP header are all in equivalent locations. Furthermore, the main UART (serial port) is located on the same pins (0 and 1), as are external interrupts 0 and 1 (pins 2 and 3 respectively). SPI is available through the ICSP header on both the Mega 2560 and Duemilanove / Diecimila boards. Please note that I2C is not located on the same pins on the Mega 2560 board (20 and 21) as the Duemilanove / Diecimila boards (analog inputs 4 and 5).

    Automatic (Software) Reset

    Rather then requiring a physical press of the reset button before an upload, the Mega 2560 is designed in a way that allows it to be reset by software running on a connected computer. One of the hardware flow control lines (DTR) of the ATmega8U2 is connected to the reset line of the ATmega2560 via a 100 nanofarad capacitor. When this line is asserted (taken low), the reset line drops long enough to reset the chip. The Arduino Software (IDE) uses this capability to allow you to upload code by simply pressing the upload button in the Arduino environment. This means that the bootloader can have a shorter timeout, as the lowering of DTR can be well-coordinated with the start of the upload.

    This setup has other implications. When the Mega 2560 board is connected to either a computer running Mac OS X or Linux, it resets each time a connection is made to it from software (via USB). For the following half-second or so, the bootloader is running on the ATMega2560. While it is programmed to ignore malformed data (i.e. anything besides an upload of new code), it will intercept the first few bytes of data sent to the board after a connection is opened. If a sketch running on the board receives one-time configuration or other data when it first starts, make sure that the software with which it communicates waits a second after opening the connection and before sending this data.

    The Mega 2560 board contains a trace that can be cut to disable the auto-reset. The pads on either side of the trace can be soldered together to re-enable it. It's labeled "RESET-EN". You may also be able to disable the auto-reset by connecting a 110 ohm resistor from 5V to the reset line.
    • Analog Input Pins: 16
    • Clock Speed: 16 MHz
    • DC Current for 3.3V Pin: 50 mA
    • DC Current per I/O Pin: 20 mA
    • Digital I/O Pins: 54 (of which 15 provide PWM output)
    • EEPROM: 4 KB
    • Flash Memory: 256 KB of which 8 KB used by bootloader

title: 8 mm to 1/2 in Grid Gusset
body_html:
This Plate can be used to easily integrate an 8mm grid hole pattern with the 0.5 inch pitch Robits hole pattern.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • This Plate can be used to easily integrate the 8mm grid hole pattern commonly found in FTC with the 0.5 inch pitch Robits hole pattern. Use this to easily mount Robits components to other common FTC build systems and vice-versa.

    When using this gusset we recommend using them in pairs.

    Typical Method Converting to Robits

    1. Align one gusset on existing structure component and fasten it using the M4 holes.
    2. Attach your Robits components to the gusset using the #10 holes.
    3. Attach a second conversion gusset to the Robits component using the #10 holes.
    4. Align the second gusset to the existing structure component and fasten it using the M4 slots.

    Depending on the design, some #10 screw spacers can be used between the Robits components and the conversion gusset to provide adequate alignment when converting in a direction perpendicular to the gusset.

    • Additional Mounting Pattern: M4 holes on an 8mm grid
    • Length: 2.89 in.

title: Robits 5.5 in. ID Turntable Assembly
body_html:
The Robits 5.5 in. ID Turntable Assembly can add a new spin to your next robot project.

  • Description
  • What's in the Box?
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • This assembly eliminates the difficulty of the past by providing a robust power transmission option with an assortment of easy to use mounting features. This system is designed to natively accept one of our Programmable Servos or NeveRest Gearmotors giving you plenty of flexibility on speed/torque options. Due to the input mounting locations, multiple motors or servos (up to 8!) can be added to increase the load this turntable can move. The turret gear when paired with the included input gear creates a 4 to 1 reduction. When used with one of our 5-turn servos, this gives over a full rotation of travel. The added gear reduction can also be a great way to create a higher ratio for arm joints. Finally, the large hole in the mounting plate is great for allowing components to pass through the center.

    **Note** The following components are NOT included with this kit.

    Servo Drive Components

    • 1 - Programmable Servo and
    • 1 - 5mm Hex to 375IN Hex Adapter (am-4957) or
    • 1 - 5mm Hex Servo Hub (am-5439)
    Motor Drive Components
    • 1 - NeveRest Hex Motor or
    • 1 - NeveRest Orbital Motor and
    • 1 - 6mm D to 375IN Hex Adapter (am-3444)

    Use the above components to add power transmission to the Turntable mechanism. There are examples of power transmission assemblies in the CAD Files found in the Documentation tab.

  • Included Items:

    • 1 - 200T 20DP Turntable Gear (am-5038)

title: 0.375 in Hex Pass Through Bevel Box
body_html:
The Pass Through Bevel Box was designed to save as much space inside a robot as possible.

  • Description
  • What's in the Box?
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • On many robots, space is a premium. The Pass Through Bevel Box allows you to align your input 90° from your output. With a pass-through design in mind, any 3/8 inch hex shaft can be used as either an input or an output. This bevel box features durable bevel gears for low to high-load applications. The housing features a NeveRest mounting pattern, making for easy installation. When used with an Adapter Mount (am-5462), the Bevel Box can be mounted directly to Robits Tubes. One interesting feature of this gearbox is that it can accept up to two motors for even greater power input. Additionally, this gearbox is fully backwards compatible with both NeveRest Hex and NeveRest Orbital motors.

title: Robits #25 Series Chain Bundle
body_html:
This chain kit includes everything you need to integrate chain with your Robits system.
  • Description
  • What's in the Box?
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • Chain can be used to transfer motion from a motor to an object and is able to handle higher load situations than belts. Use the different sprocket sizes to change the output ratio and alter the speed/torque of rotation. The Dark Soul Chain Break is our preferred tool for breaking chain. Use the connecting links to rejoin loops of chain and the attachment links to add components to your chain loops. Got a loop that's too loose? The inline chain tensioner is a great way to remove that gap if your chain doesn't need to move all the way around the path. The included spacers will properly align the plate sprockets away from tubes to help you keep everything on grid making this a seamless integration into the Robits Build System.

title: DIY Orbit Odyssey Field Kit
body_html:
This DIY Kit is everything that is needed for the Orbit Odyssey field, excluding the 3D printed parts.
  • Description
  • What's in the Box?
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • This DIY Kit is everything needed for a Field (not including 3D printed components). No robotics parts are included in this set.

    Summer camps and STEM programs provide an incredible opportunity to inspire students through hands-on learning. Orbit Odyssey challenges students to design, program, and optimize their own autonomous and remote-controlled robots to navigate unpredictable space environments. title: 8 in. MK Mecanum Wheels
body_html:
These 8 in. mecanum wheels have an inproved capacity, better interfacing ability and are less expensive than the previous version.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • Product Overview:
    This wheel has improved capacity, lower cost, and better interfacing ability than our older 8 in. Mecanum wheels. This version is named 8 in. MK Mecanum in honor and memory of AndyMark co-founder Mark Koors (MK).

    This is a set of 4 wheels, consisting of 2 "right" wheels and 2 "left" wheels. All 4 wheels are required to make a Mecanum drive holonomic system to work properly.

    Strong, steel side plates are riveted to a black polycarbonate core. This core has a common AndyMark hub, designed for mounting aluminum hubs, sprockets, or bearings easily. The standard 6-hole mounting pattern and bearing bore are utilized here on the wheel. The rollers are molded with a nylon core and a 80A durometer TPU overmold in a special way which adheres the roller core to the skin for high durability. These rollers spin on a captured brass axle tube, contained by a #10 machine screw.

    We have been able to drive cost out of these wheels, so they are less expensive than our previous 8 in. Mecanum wheels, while still having a very high capacity and a smooth roll.

    These wheels are ASSEMBLED and shipped ready to roll!


    Individual Hardware within Wheel Set Assembly:

    • 4 - Left MK Mecanum Ring Plates
    • 4 - Right MK Mecanum Ring Plates
    • 8 - Polycarbonate MK Mecanum Hub Halves
    • 48 - MK Mecanum Rollers
    • 48 - Brass Tube Axles
    • 48 - #10-32 x 3.50 in. SHCS
    • 48 - #10-32 Nylock Jam Nuts
    • 48 - #10-24 x 3/4 Thread Forming Screw
    • 96 - 3/16 in. Rivets
    These wheels were designed by Mark Koors, co-founder of AndyMark. The "MK" in 8 in. MK Mecanum stands for Mark's name.

    Mark co-founded AndyMark with Andy Baker in 2004 and designed numerous products - including mecanum wheels until his retirement in 2016.     AndyMark is known for being the first company who made Mecanum wheels commercially available to all robot builders in 2006. He and Andy were inspired by FIRST Robotics Team 357, Royal Assault, after they introduced Mecanum wheels to FIRST during the 2005 competition season. Mark passed away in 2020.

    Learn how to position these wheels by watching this video.

title: Computerized Battery Analyzer
body_html:
This computerized Battery Analyzer will test any type or size of battery, any chemistry or number of cells, up to 55 volts.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • The computerized Battery Analyzer is much more than a simple battery voltage tester or a battery load tester. It will test virtually any type or size of battery, any chemistry or number of cells, up to 55 volts. We are making this tester available with accessories intended for FIRST legal batteries, although teams may purchase the CBA without accessories and create their own cables for testing other battery types.
    The CBA not only tests the total amount of energy stored within a battery (capacity in amp-hours), but also graphically displays and charts the voltage versus time under a constant current load. Graphs may be displayed, saved and printed, and the axis parameters can be changed at any time. Multiple test graphs of the same battery, or multiple batteries, may be compared or overlaid; a very useful feature for teams looking to test capacity and performance of their batteries as they age.

    Included Items:

    • 1 - Computerized Battery Analyzer (am-3158a)
    • 1 - SB50 to PP45 XT30 and XT60 Adapter Cable (am-2070b)
    • 1 - USB A to USB B 2.0 Cable (am-3579)
    ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    To run a test:

    • Install the CBA V software
      • You can find the latest version of the software, drivers, and the full owner's manual for your CBA V here.
    • Connect the battery tester to your computer
    • Connect a fully charged battery to the battery tester
    • Click the "New Test File" Button
      • If you wish to add an additional test to an existing file chose "Append Test" instead.
    • In the New Test window do the following.
      • Select "Discharge" on the left
      • In the blue box on the right click the "Detect" button
        • For an FRC Battery fill in the following settings: Lead Acid, 13.2V, 6 Cells
        • Enter the Ah of the battery
          • Usually 18 for FRC batteries
      • Enter a name for the battery at the top under "Test Name:" and label the battery with this name for future comparison
      • In the center of the screen set "Cutoff V:"
        • This is the voltage that the battery will be depleted to.
        • For an FRC Battery we recommend 10.5
      • In the center of the screen set "Test Amps:"
        • This is the load that the tester will apply to the battery for the duration of the test.
        • For an FRC Battery we recommend 7.5
          • This is the highest the tester can do on an FRC battery and will result in the fastest test.
      • Click "Start"
    • The test will now run for anywhere between a few minutes to a few hours
      • Do not move or touch the battery at all during the test
      • Pausing the test will result in a bad portion of data around the pause and is not recommended
    • When the test is complete a dialogue box will appear informing you of the result and the graph will be complete
      • Click "OK" and repeat the test for another battery.

    The critical number to look for is amp hours (Ah) after the test. If the graph crosses the 10.5V at less than 12Ah after 2 consecutive tests from a fully charged state we recommend not using this battery in competition due to the increased risk of brownouts, especially near the end of a match. Such batteries should be marked and only used for things like practice, demos, or testing.

    Further Reading:

    FRC 1640 has published their procedures and best practices regarding this tester.

    For further instruction and explanation, watch our video about preparing batteries for competition:

title: NR Bevel Box
body_html:
To optimize space, the output shaft of this Bevel Box is at right angle to the NeveRest motor.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • The NR Bevel Box was created to help optimize space inside of a robot. This gearbox can be mounted along the side of the robot structure because the output shaft of the Bevel Box is at a right angle to a NeveRest Orbital Motor, therefore taking up less space. The NR Bevel Box has a similar mounting pattern as our NeveRest Orbital Motors, allowing it to be a drop in replacement wherever you would install one of our orbital motors. The output shaft is adjustable, allowing you to optimize the length and position for every application.

    A 3D printable file of a protective cover is hosted in the Documents section below. This helps prevent anything from being pinched in the gears, such as wires or fingers. Additionally, it allows users to install a 6 mm x 8 mm bushing (am-1289) in the back to further support the 6 mm D shaft.

    Motor Options

    • NeveRest Orbital 3.7 to 1 (~1784 RPM)
    • NeveRest Orbital 13.7 to 1 (~482 RPM)
    • NeveRest Orbital 19.2 to 1 (~344 RPM)
    • NeveRest Orbital 50.9 to 1 (~130 RPM)
    • NeveRest Orbital 263.7 to 1 (~25RPM)

    Shaft Length

body_html:
The LJ Bevel Box is a right angle gearbox using steel bevel gears, designed to integrate with a motor.
  • Description

  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • The LJ Bevel Box is a right angle gearbox using steel bevel gears, designed to integrate with a CIM Motor (am-0255), CIM-Sim (am-0932), 57 Sport, NEO, or CIM Sport. This setup allows for the use of a gearbox or CIM motor in locations where you may not have the space available for an assembly in a straight line. We recommend using this gearbox in low torque setups. An E4T encoder can be added to the side of this gearbox, but is not included.


    LJ: Larry Jones


    This product is named after Larry Jones, the uncle of AndyMark president Andy Baker. He passed away during the fall of 2013. He was the main inspiration to Andy in becoming an engineer, and is one of Andy's heroes. Larry grew up in Indiana and was a graduate of Purdue University and worked on many projects during his lifetime, including designing lawn tractors and military training devices. He enjoyed his profession, working as an engineering manager at Wheelhorse, Jet Propulsion Laboratory and Caltech. For the past two decades, Larry worked on the LIGO project as a mechanical engineer. This project includes very large installations of lasers, mirrors and detection equipment which culminate in the goal of detecting gravity waves.

    Larry was gifted in not only being a technically sound engineer, but also was a master communicator. He could easily explain the most complex systems and theories so that a child could understand what he was explaining. He would tell stories in a way which would capture the attention of his grandchildren, nieces and nephews, all while displaying his charismatic smile.

    Most importantly, Larry was a devoted and faithful husband, father, and leader. His community involvement, church leadership, and care for his family was inspirational to all who had the pleasure to know Larry. Naming this gearbox after Larry is a small token to pay tribute to a great man. Rest in peace, Uncle Larry.

title: 1/2 in. Churro Different Lengths
body_html:
Churro is a versatile extruded aluminum hex profile.

  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • The outside of this part is a 1/2 in. hex with small concave dimples which act as weight savings. There is an inside hole is sized at 0.2 in. in order to fit 1/4-20 thread forming screws. No tapping or threading is needed, as long as a thread forming screw is used. The outside hex size fits a 1/2 in. wrench or socket. You can use am-1182 to secure components to churro. Longer thread forming screws are available if you need to attach larger items to churro.

    The 3-foot churro, our most popular length and the best value on shipping, is available anodized in red, blue, purple, gold and black to dress up your robot. Anodized finish is hardy and doesn't flake off or add thickness like paint, but it is possible for a scratch to expose the bare metal beneath. Take basic precautions in your shop like watching for sharp tools or overtightening this churro in a vise.
    The anodizing process may result in colors that are not exact to the reference photo. FED-STD-595 is a color description system. These anodized products can be described by this system as follows:
    Red: 31310-31136
    Green: 24449-24272
    Violet: 27142-27144
    Blue: 35183-35180
    Gold: 10260-10371

title: Robits Compact Linear Slide
body_html:
The Compact Linear Slide system is a quick way to execute a controlled extension.

  • Description
  • What's in the Box?
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • Specifically designed for FTC, (though not limited to FTC), this remarkable system is a quick way to execute a controlled extension. Each stage of the Compact Linear Slide is controlled by a pulley system that can be rigged to power both extension and retraction. This is the latest version of the AM Compact Linear slide, with Robits design ideals integrated. The inline stringing removes any tensioning spring requirement. The slide to pully holder attachment has been redesigned and improved.

    Options:

    • 1 Stage has 12.18 inches of stroke
    • 2 Stage has 24.37 inches of stroke
    • 3 Stage has 36.56 inches of stroke
    • Additional Stages
      • AndyMark officially supports a 3 stage system however teams may elect to add additional stages to increase reach.
      • Load limit of 25 lbs

    Suggested Rigging:

    • Continuous
      • One string per direction that connects through each stage
      • For more details, see the assembly guide and video

    Included Powering/Gearing:

    • NeveRest Hex 13.7 to 1:
      • Speedy, approximately 1 second per stage at full speed.
      • Enough torque to easily lift multiple stages with a manipulator and game pieces
    • No Motor Options have no motor included. They are compatible with NeveRest Hex Gearmotors.
      • For lower load applications, a lower ratio gearmotor like a 3.7 or 13.7 is ideal.
      • For higher load applications, a larger ratio gearmotor like a 19.2 or 50.9 is ideal.

title: Compliant Stars
body_html:
Compliant Stars are very effective intake manipulators.

  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • Compliant Stars are the perfect thing for intake mechanisms. The soft material gives way to allow rigid objects to be manipulated easily. A line of multiple stars on a driven hex shaft creates a very effective roller that ignores variations in the objects being driven. The multiple-spoke design allows the star to act as a brush, creating more surface area to interact with and grab objects. This makes for high-performance intakes and internal conveyors. A shaft collar may be used to make absolutely sure the wheels stay clear of other mechanisms or maintain consistent spacing. Molded into the star are several guidelines. Cut the star at the lines (or elsewhere) to create more compact mechanisms.

    Different durometer ratings give each Compliant Star unique characteristics. Green stars (35A durometer) are the softest and most compliant around objects, while orange (40A), maroon (45A), and blue (50A) wheels are increasingly firm. Black (60A) is quite firm, while the Gray (80A) is nearly rigid. The increased firmness also allows the latter wheels to carry a higher RPM rating.

    • Bore: 0.500 in. [12.7 mm] (1/2) Hex, 3/8 in. Hex
    • Diameter: 3 in., 5 in.
    • Durometer: 35A (Green), 40A (Orange), 50A (Blue), 60A (Black), 80A (Gray)
    • Material: TPU
    • Maximum RPM: 6000 - 9000 RPM
    • Weight: 0.085 lbs.
    • Width: 0.4 in.
