title: DuraOmni Wheel
body_html:
This Heavy Duty DURAble omni wheel has been totally redesigned with durability and mobility in mind.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • This Heavy Duty DURAble omni wheel is a vast improvement over our older 6 in. omni wheels and other wheels on the market. The body has been totally redesigned with durability and mobility in mind. The design intent is to provide a smooth roll along with the ability to handle impacts very well.

    The body is made from black polycarbonate, while the rollers are each molded with a nylon core and TPU tread. These rollers spin smoothly on a captured dowel pin.

    Usage With Axle and Hub:
    • If you wish to drive this wheel with an axle and hub, you can pick your hub by fitting any of the AndyMark hubs to this wheel. Hubs are not included with this wheel. If this is your choice, then no bearing is needed. To install a hub onto this wheel, use #10-24x3/4 thread forming screws.

    Usage With Sprockets and Bearings:

    • If you wish to drive this wheel with a sprocket, then the sprocket needs to be attached to the side of the wheel with #10-24x3/4 thread forming screws. You will also need to press ball bearings into the wheel so that it may spin on a shaft or bolt. The ball bearing must have a 1.125 in. od. For a 1/2 in. shafts, use am-0181. For a 3/8 in. shafts use am-0209.
    • Bolt Pattern: 6 holes (0.157 in.) on a 1.875 in. bolt circle
    • Bore: 0.96 in. diameter through hole, with two 1.125 in. diameter bearing pockets
    • Diameter: 4 in. [100 mm], 6 in.

title: Robot Competition Table
body_html:
This table is suitable for use in the FIRST LEGO League Robot Game.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • Warranty

  • The AndyMark Robot Competition Table is finally here. Since 2004, AndyMark has provided innovative products and services for the competition robotics community. With our staff's decades of experience participating in and volunteering for the FIRST® LEGO® League Program, combined with our engineering expertise, AndyMark has designed and manufactured a 3-piece table design that can be easily stored and transported while maintaining the robustness found in many DIY plywood designs.

    This table is suitable for use in the FIRST LEGO League Robot Game.

    This table was designed in collaboration with Jay Kinzie.

    Design Features:

    New and improved version includes smooth black laminated playing surface. No painting required!

    The AndyMark Table meets all of the core design requirements of an Official Table to be used in the FIRST LEGO League Challenge program.

    • Safe for adults and students to compete and practice
    • Robust enough for students and small robots to interact with surfaces without damage
    • Sizing matches current 4ft x 8ft FIRST LEGO League Challenge table specifications and plywood design
    • Provides a flat, black surface for robots to drive on
    • Provides a uniform wall profile for robots to interact with that matches current FLL Challenge specifications
    • Works well as a single table for practice and also side-by-side for tournaments

    In addition to the core design requirements, the AndyMark Table has additional features that have been developed through listening to input from the robotics community that makes this a great improvement over the plywood DIY tables.

    • Quickly disassembles into three sections for easy storage at home, in a classroom, or between tournaments
    • Sections fit into small vehicles for transportation
    • Sections are able to be carried by one adult or two students (each section weighs about 22lb)
    • Critical parts stay together after initial assembly to ensure a consistent playing surface
    • One Phillips head screwdriver (four screws) needed to reassemble sections for use
    • The bolted design allows for walls to be adjusted to ensure they are always in the correct location

    For Tournament Play:

    • Designed for use on a standard 8ft banquet table (for one Robot Competition Table)
    • Integrated latches securely hold two tables together in all directions
    • If using two tables together, it is recommended to use 3 banquet tables for more stability underneath

    Design Specifications:

    • Extruded black ABS (plastic) sidewalls
      • Robust and lightweight
      • Maintains color when scratched or dented
    • Lightweight MDF playing surface
      • Rigid and flat
      • Smooth surface
      • Black laminate top surface
    • Utilizes common easy-to-find hardware
    • CNC manufactured at AndyMark HQ in Indiana, USA
    • Fully assembled size: 102 in. x 50 in. x 3 in.
    • Section size: 50 in. x 34 in. x 3 in.
    • Weight: 62 lbs

    Individual Components:

    If you've damaged a component, or it's just taken years of wear and isn't working anymore, you can get the individual components.

    Shipping Options:

    The AndyMark Robot Competition Table is shipped disassembled in a 51 in.x34"x4" box, typically via FedEx ground. For bulk orders and options for shipping alternatives please contact us directly for a shipping quote.

    Assembly Video Guides

    The assembly video can be found by clicking here.

    Not officially endorsed by FIRST or the LEGO Group. FIRST® is a trademark of For Inspiration and Recognition of Science and Technology (FIRST). LEGO® is a registered trademark of the LEGO Group. FIRST ® LEGO® League is a jointly held trademark of FIRST and the LEGO Group.

    US Patent 20220152473

  • Warranty Information:

    AndyMark, Inc. warrants its products to be free of defects in material and workmanship, provided any issues are reported in writing or the product is returned within 30 days after the date of receipt. This warranty does not cover damage or defects caused by or resulting from repairs, service, or alterations to the product or any of its parts, or damage or defects caused by negligence, accident, abuse, misuse, improper or abnormal usage, or maintenance of this product or its parts.

    When not in use, AndyMark recommends that the Robot Competition Table be stored flat in a cool (60-80F), dry (>50% humidity), area. The boards must be protected from any direct contact with water. They must be stacked flat - boards should not be stored vertically, unless ground contact can be avoided. The board will expand or shrink under variable humidity conditions. Tables that are improperly stored, exposed to water, or stored in areas with high fluctuations in temperature or humidity may warp over time and will not be covered under AndyMark's warranty.

    The perimeter attachment method allows for the perimeter to be loosened, and readjusted to accommodate any natural warpage in the MDF due to changes in temperature and humidity.

title: REEFSCAPE℠ Game Pieces
body_html:
There are multiple Game Pieces for the 2025 FIRST® Robotics Competition REEFSCAPE℠ presented by Haas.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • There are multiple Game Pieces for the 2025 FIRST® Robotics Competition REEFSCAPE℠ presented by Haas.

    Coral (also known as Game Piece 1) is a 11 ⅞ in. long (~30 cm) piece of 4 in. diameter Schedule 40 Cellular (Foam) Core PVC pipe. Coral has a 4-in. (~102 mm) inside diameter and a 4½-in. (~11 cm) outside diameter. The Coral sold here is from the same batch and manufacturer used on official fields. For optimal shipping price, buy Coral in multiples of 14.

    Algae (also known as Game Piece 2) was available as a preorder for this season, and each team has received two of Game Piece 2 in the Season-Specific box from FIRST. Each Algae is a 16 in. (41 cm) ±½ in. (~12 mm) diameter rubber playground ball. While similar items are available from other sources, the only place to get the official Algae is in the Kit of Parts or from AndyMark. Algae are being offered as single items with quantity discounts, with a maximum discount for a box of 20, which is two more than a full field.

    Algae Measuring Jig V2 This is a FIRST Approved Alternative for checking ball inflation using the same procedure that will be used on competition fields. This Jig has been cost and production time optimized without losing functionality. Ignore the instructions on the ball in favor of this jig for accurate sized Algae.

    REEFSCAPE℠ game piece pre-orders are not eligible for a return.

    See how to use the old measuring jig to achieve the new specifications for Algae by watching this video:

title: Official Individual FRC AprilTag Stickers
body_html:
These April Tags are the same ones that are used on the FIRST® Robotics Competition Game Field.

  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • The AprilTags sold here are identical to the ones found on the real field, sourced from the same vendors that FIRST uses. FIRST is using a new vendor this year, so in these kits if that tag ID was used in the past it may be from either vendor, but tag IDs that were not used in the past will be from the new vendor.

    AprilTags are a part of the Field, used by vision systems to generate positioning data. AprilTag resources are available through FIRST for use with the roboRIO. FIRST also expects that many community solutions will likely be able to detect these tags as well.

    The image on the sticker is 6.5 in. square, and the stickers are 10.5 in. square with notched corners to accommodate bolt heads. On a competition field these tags are affixed to a plastic plate.

title: Spur Gear Stock
body_html:
Gear stock is perfect for creating custom sized gears.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • Gear stock is perfect for creating custom sized gears, or up-integrating shaft features to reduce part count in assemblies. It can be loaded into a lathe or mill and machined to any number of shapes and given any number of bores to meet your specific needs.

    Some examples of what you can do when designing with gear stock as opposed to off the shelf gears include am-3013b and am-3018b.

    All the gear stock that AndyMark utilizes to create our fully machined gears are listed and available here. These are sold in 1 foot (12 inch) sections, but if you require a longer section or a gear profile we do not currently offer, please contact us at Support@AndyMark.com.

    Selecting a Gear Stock

    Tooth Profile

    First, and most importantly, the tooth profile. If you are interfacing with another gear you need to know its Diametral Pitch (DP, for imperial gears) or Module (MOD, for metric gears). This number governs the size of the tooth, and meshing gears must have the same size tooth. Within these sizes there can be various pressure angles. These also need to match for meshing gears. To avoid confusion we do not sell gear stocks with the same "tooth size" and different pressure angles and for this reason we have combined these 2 parameters into one dropdown. In FRC 20 DP, 14.5° PA is the most common, followed by 32 DP, 20° PA. The rest of our gear stocks are used in specialty applications.

    Tooth Count

    Next, you will want to select tooth count. We have many options here and this is usually dictated by your design and what gear ratio you want to achieve, or which gear you may be trying to replace. Note that tooth count directly affects gear diameter, so if you need to put a specific size shaft through the gear you are picking make sure the gear is going to be large enough. All the CAD files for all these gear profiles are available at the bottom of this page.

    Material

    After specifying the above parameters you will be presented with a list of available materials available for those options. If you require your gear to be a specific material specify this first and the other options will narrow to ones that are available in this material. If you are curious about the specific alloy number of the material selected (for example 6061 Aluminum or 4140 Steel) check the part number that is generated below the last dropdown. The 4 digit number near the end is the alloy number.

    Part Number

    Once you have made a selection in each of the options you will be given a part number. This number contains all the information you selected above and can be used to locate the appropriate CAD file below. If you would like to interpret the number, it is set up as follows:

    gs-P-S-T-A-1
    gs - indicates Gear Stock
    P - indicates the Pressure Angle
    S - indicates Diametral Pitch or Module
    T - indicates Tooth Count
    A - indicates Alloy Number of the Material
    1 - indicates the length (in feet) of your piece of stock

title: HD Nubs
body_html:
The nub is a specific hub intended to connect motion components to spinning shafts, like sprockets gears, pulleys and wheels.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • Looking to upgrade your nub game? This brand new series of Nubs feature pre-threaded attachment points for a high-strength connection.

    We carry several body profiles of the Nub too! Their use cases are:

    • Single Boss for installing an individual Nub Bore item on a shaft
    • Double Boss for locating two Nub Bore items on a shaft
    • Double Boss XL for high-torque applications or connecting two shafts together
    • Single Boss Bearing for making free-spinning motion components
    • Single Boss Servo for interfacing with 24T spline-based servos

    Note:
    The flat sides on all of the D-bore Nubs are timed and parallel to the side with the setscrew. The flat is positioned opposite from the set screw so that the set screw can press the flat of the shaft into the flat of the nub for optimal torque transfer.

title: KitBot 2024 CRESCENDO℠
body_html:
Designed to integrate with the am-14U5 chassis, this kit can be used to build the 2024 FRC Kitbot.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • THIS GAME IS A PAST SEASON, be sure that this item is for the correct game you are looking for.

    This kit is equivalent to the FRC Kit of Parts KitBot. In conjunction with an AM14U5 drive train, and two additional motor controllers, these items can create a robot that can play some aspects of CRESCENDO℠. It’s also been designed so teams can build the KitBot and then further iterate on it to add additional features if they choose. Teams will still need basic power tools (drills, saws, etc.) in order to build this robot.

    The options here are configured per what teams can opt in or out of in the KOP. KitBot documentation will be available to all teams, and many of the items from the Black Tote that are used to build the KitBot are components that Veteran teams likely already have on hand or can easily replicate.

    NOTE: While the Black Tote does include two motor controllers we opted to not include them in either of our bundles due to the high cost, and high likelihood that teams will have extra brushed speed controllers available to use.

    Resources that will be made available by FIRST include:

    • Build instructions for the KitBot with photos
    • Basic code to operate the KitBot as designed in LabVIEW, Java, C++, and Python
      • Software guide for each language exploring the code and possible controls modifications

title: nOOds 3V 300mm Flexible LED Filament
body_html:
These LED filaments are colorful, flexible, and about the size of a spaghetti noodle, hence the name.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • These adorable little noodles are the perfect thing to brighten up your day. Super flexible, nOOds can be lit with only 3V - we recommend current limiting with a resistor to a max of 50mA. These can be folded into wonky shapes that can't be easily achieved with other light sources. To use, connect both ends to a power source. The anode should be the metal end with a little hole in it. If it doesn't immediately light up, switch the connection around.

    If you're looking for a simple and easy way to connect your nOOds, you may want to consider pairing this product with the am-4728 WAGO connector. However, we would highly recommend soldering as the most reliable and secure option for long-term use.

    • Dimmable: Yes
    • Input Voltage: 3 VDC
    • Length: 300 mm

title: SDS MK4 Pinion Kits
body_html:
These Pinion Kits are used to allow NEO and Falcon Motors to interface with the SDS MK4 Modules.

  • Description
  • What's in the Box?
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • These Pinion Kits are used to allow NEO and Falcon Motors to interface with the SDS MK4 Modules.

    -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    Pinion Installation:
    The 15 Tooth 32 DP pinion gear for the NEO gear does not use a key for torque transfer. There are two possible methods of installation of this pinion on a CIM or NEO style motor.

    • If the tolerances of both the motor shaft and the pinion are in your favor an arbor press (possibly up to 3 tons) is required to install this pinion due to the intended interference fit (0.001 - 0.002 in.)
      • If using an original NEO motor, please follow the NEO Press Fit Pinion Guide.
      • If using a NEO 1.1 Motor insert a #10-32 x 3/8in long socket head screw into the hole in the back of the motor to support the internal shaft while pressing pinions.
    • If the tolerances are not in your favor and the pinions slip on the shaft, or you feel that the press fit it too weak, an adhesive is required to transfer torque. The procedure is the same for all motors.
      • Apply a few rings of red Loctite to the shaft, and the bore of the pinion, then slip the pinion onto the shaft down the the desired location.
      • Red Loctite has been tested to a factor of safety of 4x the stall torque of a CIM when let to cure for 24 hours.

    If you are are unable or uncomfortable performing these procedures, we recommend purchasing a motor with the pinion pre-installed. They are available as am-4258a_15T for the NEO.

title: MecanAM FTC Chassis
body_html:
The MecanAM Chassis is designed to be a very maneuverable robot for FTC teams.

  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • The MecanAM Chassis is designed to be a very maneuverable robot for FTC teams to enjoy. The omnidirectional movement capabilities of the mecanum wheels can help drivers smoothly avoid obstacles and quickly change drive direction.

    There are many configurations available, but if you are not sure what to get, we recommend the BTHMB2N. It features our best mecanum wheels for FTC along with the standard in FTC drive motors.

    Wheels

    • 4 in. BB Mecanum Wheels
      • This wheel is optimized for FTC, with a lightweight, slim profile
      • The ball bearings inside of the rollers make for a smoother ride
    • 4 in. HD Mecanum Wheels
      • These mecanums are designed to be hardy wheels that can handle a lot of weight

    Motors

    • NeveRest Orbital 14:1
      • for a faster drive train, the 14:1 output of these motors is preferred
    • NeveRest Orbital 20:1
      • These motors can handle moving around more weight at a more consistent speed
    • NeveRest Hex 14:1
      • for a faster drive train, the 14:1 output of these motors is preferred
      • Hex output shaft for easy integration
      • NOTE: due to sizing, the encoder is not accessible on the hex version of this chassis 
    • NeveRest Hex 20:1
      • These motors can handle moving around more weight at a more consistent speed
      • Hex output shaft for easy integration
      • NOTE: due to sizing, the encoder is not accessible on the hex version of this chassis 

    Understanding Part Numbers

    FIRST Tech Challenge Chassis Configurator

    Structure & Usage

    The foundation of this drive base is a set of aluminum plates, brackets, and struts that provide a sturdy frame to build upon. All of the holes in the sheet metal are on a global 16 mm pattern, which integrates with numerous structure components across several vendors.
    The cross plate can also be moved into a number of alternate locations to best suit your robot's configuration needs. Without motors and wheels, the chassis is about 4 pounds.

    Performance, Rugged, Configurable

    The MecanAM Chassis was designed with the FIRST Tech Challenge community in mind. The usage doesn't stop there, however, it can work well for many other robotic competition platforms of similar size. Years of lessons from designing, building, and competing with championship-winning drive systems have gone into this robust drive system that integrates well with teams' existing FTC parts.

    Upgrade Instructions

    If using a kit with the NeveRest Hex motors, the installation hardware of the motors will be slightly different than noted in the kit instructions. Use this image as guidance instead.

title: Sport Gearbox Motor Blocks
body_html:
These components are used to interface between motors and the Sport Gearbox.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • If you are looking for complete kits to attach your motors please see Sport Gearbox Motor Mount Kits.

    am-3770 CIM & NEO with Standard Shaft

    This component attaches to a CIM Motor (am-0255) or a NEO Motor (am-4258a) with 1 in. long 10-32 Screws (am-1056) and secures to Sport Gearbox using the long screws that run down the corners of the gearbox. This motor block does not require modification of the motor shaft.

    am-3769a CIM & NEO with Cut Shaft

    This component allows either a CIM Motor (am-0255) or a NEO Motor (am-4258a) to be used with a Sport Gearbox. Use this motor block if you are looking to save on space and weight. To use this motor block, the motor shaft must be cut ~7/8 in. shorter. No additional screws are needed to use this block, it sandwiches between the motor and the gearbox and the motor is attached with the long screws that run down the corners of the gearbox.

    am-3765 550 & 775

    This motor block is used to hold an RS-500 or RS-700 motor such as the AndyMark 775 RedLine (am-3775) or the NEO Motor (am-4258a) to the Sport gearbox. 550 motors attach to the block with M3 screws, and 775 motors attach to the block with M4 screws, then the block attaches to the Sport Gearbox using the long screws that run down the corners of the gearbox.

    am-3770 CIM & NEO & Kraken with Standard Shaft

    This component attaches to a CIM Motor (am-0255) a NEO Motor (am-4258a), a Kraken X60, or a Kraken X44 with 5/8 in. long 10-32 Screws (am-1549) and secures to Sport Gearbox using the long screws that run down the corners of the gearbox. This motor block does not require modification of the motor shaft.

    am-5587 CIM & NEO & Kraken with Cut Shaft

    This component allows either a CIM Motor (am-0255), a NEO Motor (am-4258a), a Kraken X60 or a Kraken X44 to be used with a Sport Gearbox. Use this motor block if you are looking to save on space and weight. To use this motor block, the motor shaft must be cut ~7/8 in. shorter. No additional screws are needed to use this block, except with the Kraken X44 that requires 3/8 in. long 10-32 BHCS (am-1588) to mount. It sandwiches between the motor and the gearbox and the motor is attached with the long screws that run down the corners of the gearbox.

    am-5615 Minion

    This component allow a Minion Brushless Motor to be used with a Sport Gearbox. Minion motors attach to the block with 10-32 screws, then the block attaches to the Sport Gearbox using the long screws that run down the corners of the gearbox.

    • Material: 6061-T6 Aluminum

title: NeveRest Hex Gearmotors
body_html:
The NeveRest Hex gearmotor is our newest planetary gearmotor designed for FTC.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • The NeveRest Hex line of gearmotors continues to offer a wide range of ratios making it easy to select the right one for the right application. The NeveRest Hex is backwards compatible and can be installed everywhere the previous NeveRest Orbital could be mounted. They have a pre-installed encoder and an output shaft directly in the center of the output face. The shaft is a 3/8 inch hex and is available in three different lengths based on application.

    New to our NeveRest Hex line of motors is a detachable power cable. All Hex gearmotors will come with a twelve inch power cable that can be removed and replaced as required. This allows users to select an appropriate length of cable as well as allows the motor to be adaptable to other control systems.
    JST-VH-2 connectors: this option comes standard and plugs directly into the FIRST Tech Challenge REV Controller

    Shafts: 3/8 inch hex with a 10-32 tapped end in 1, 2, and 3 inch options

    Part Number: this gearmotor assembly uses the following part numbering scheme

    am-5550_xxxx_yyy

    am-5550 (base number for NeveRest Hex Gearmotors)

    xxxx denotes the shaft length (example 0100 is 1 inch)

    yyy denotes the gearbox ratio (example 019 is 19.2:1)

    FIRST Legality:

    • According to the FIRST Tech Challenge Competition Manual, all versions of the NeveRest motor are legal in FTC.
    • According to the FIRST Robotics Competition Game Manual, all versions of the NeveRest motor are legal in FRC as it uses the NeveRest am-3104 motor.

    Encoder:

    There is an encoder mounted to the backside of this motor. It is a 7 pulse per revolution (PPR), hall effect encoder. Multiply the ratio by 7 to get the PPR of the output shaft. For example the NeverRest Hex 3.7 output shaft provides 25.9 PPR.

    Encoder Cable Options:
    NeveRest motors do not come with an encoder cable as we offer multiple cable options:

    am-3926a allows you to connect the encoder directly to the FIRST Tech Challenge REV Controller with various lengths.
    am-2992 has the 4 encoder pins joined in one housing using standard 0.1 in. spacing.
    am-2993 allows you to break out the 4 pins separately if you need them in a different order.

    Working with the Encoders:
    • https://youtu.be/d0liBxZCtrA?t=95
    • Connector Type: JST-VH-2
    • Gauge: 18 AWG
    • Material: Steel and Plastic
    • Maximum Diameter: 1.5 in. [38 mm]
    • Maximum Power: 14 W
    • Mounting Geometry: 4x M3 x 0.5 on a 28 mm Bolt Circle, 4x 10-32 (1.5 in. by 0.5 in.)
    • Output Shaft Size: 0.375 in. Hex Shaft
    • Poles Per Magnet: 7
    • Stall Current: 11 A
    • Voltage: 12 VDC

title: NeveRest Orbital Gearmotors
body_html:
The NeveRest Orbital gearmotor is a robust planetary gearmotor designed for FTC.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • With many ratios to choose from you can find the right motor for you, from a fast spinning intake to a high reduction arm, all are possible with NeveRest Orbitals. They have a pre-installed encoder and an output shaft directly in the center of the output face. The shaft is a 6 mm D and the gearbox housing is 37 mm in diameter.

    The power cable which feeds into the black encoder housing has two different options that are already crimped to the end of the cable.
    1. JST-VH-2 connectors: this option plugs directly into the FIRST Tech Challenge REV Controller
    2. Anderson Powerpole 15A connectors: This is another popular connector with FTC and FRC teams.

    FIRST Legality:

    • According to the FIRST Tech Challenge Game Manual, all versions of the NeveRest motor are legal in FTC.
    • According to the FIRST Robotics Competition Game Manual, all versions of the NeveRest motor are legal in FRC as it uses the NeveRest am-3104 motor.
    Usage:
    • PicoBox LEO (am-3614). This gearbox is used for creating chain drives for mechanisms like arms.
    • PicoBox GEO (am-3616). This gearbox combines two NeveRest Orbital motors into a single output shaft allowing for combined power at a low ratio.
    • PicoBox MEO (am-3615). This gearbox accepts one NeveRest motor and allows for gear changing through PicoBox gearing.

    Encoder:
    There is an encoder mounted to the backside of this motor. It is a 7 pulse per revolution (PPR), hall effect encoder. Multiply the ratio by 7 to get the PPR of the output shaft. For example the NeverRest 3.7 output shaft provides 25.9 PPR.

    Encoder Cable Options:
    NeveRest motors do not come with an encoder cable as we offer 3 cable options:

    am-3926a allows you to connect the encoder directly to the FIRST Tech Challenge REV Controller.

title: NeveRest Sport Gearbox
body_html:
The NeveRest Sport gearboxes are ideal for applications where more shock loading, dynamic loading, and torque is needed
  • Description
  • Gearbox Ratios
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • Hey, FTC teams, this is for you!

    NeveRest Sport planetary gearboxes are created with FIRST Tech Challenge teams in mind. Designed in collaboration with BaneBots, these gearboxes have a Nub-shaped output shaft, and all the mounting features are designed around common FTC hole spacing for maximum compatibility. The shaft and gears are robust, machined steel components designed to withstand many times more power than a NeveRest motor will supply. With seven ratios up to 256:1, you're sure to find a ratio that fits your application.

    These gearboxes accept one NeveRest Motor (am-3104), sold separately. We include a packet of Red Tacky Grease (am-2768) with each NeveRest Sport gearbox order; a pea-sized amount on each stage of reduction before running it will ensure smooth, trouble-free operation.

    These gearboxes are more expensive and more robust than the small gearboxes usually mounted on the face of NeveRest gearmotors. than what a standard NeveRest gearbox (or its mount) can handle. The NeveRest Sports have a max loading of 6700 oz-in, or 35 ft-lbs.

    Mounting Features

    • 6-32 tapped holes on two faces, on a 16 mm hole spacing
    • 6-32 tapped holes on a 28 mm bolt circle for face mounting, same as our NeveRest Orbital gearmotor.

    Output Geometry

    • Nub shaped output shaft with 6-32 tapped holes on a 16 mm bolt circle
    • 6 mm hole and set screw for any length 6 mm D shaft or 5 mm hex shaft

    Gearing

    • The 15 tooth pinion and all internal gears are 0.6 module
    • All first stage gear sets have 4 planet gears

    Included Hardware

    • 1 - NeveRest Sport gearbox assembly (depending on which gearbox selected)
    • 1 - NeveRest Sport Motor Mounting Kit (am-2890)

  • Please contact support@andymark.com if you do not see a Ratio Table
    • Motor Input: NeveRest
    • Motor Quantity: 1
    • Ratio: 4:1, 16:1, 20:1, 64:1, 81:1, 104:1, 256:1

title: Plaction Wheels
body_html:
• Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • Usage:
    There are two ways to drive these wheels. One way is with an Axle and Hub, and the other is with a Sprocket. To install a sprocket or hub onto a Plaction wheel, use 10-32 x 1.75 in. socket head screw (qty. 3 or 6), and 10-32 nylock nuts. To use one sprocket on each side of a Plaction wheel (2 sprockets total) use 10-32 x 2.5 in. screws (3 or 6) and 10-32 nylock nuts.

    With Axle and Hub:
    • If you wish to drive this wheel with an Axle and Hub, you can pick your hub by fitting any of the AndyMark hubs to this wheel. Hubs are NOT included in the price of the wheel. If this is your choice, then no bearing is needed.
    With Plate Sprocket:
    • If you wish to drive a wheel with a plate sprocket, then the sprocket needs to be attached to the side of the wheel, and two ball bearings need to be pressed into the wheel (one on each side).
    With Bearing:
    • If your design needs this wheel to spin on a stationary axle (and possibly be driven by a sprocket), you will need 2 bearings with a 1.125 in. od pressed into this wheel. One bearing is pressed into each side of the wheel. Bearings are NOT included in the price of this wheel.
    With Tread:
    • These wheels are designed to capture 1 in wide conveyor belt tread (Roughtop or Wedgetop) between 2 wheel halves. The 6 perimeter screws can be loosened by 1/8 in. to install the desired tread. We recommend using Alligator Clips to hold the tread together on the wheel.
    For a Wider Wheel:
    These wheels are designed so that a Schedule 40 PVC pipe of the appropriate diameter can be inserted between the two wheel halves to create a wider wheel.

body_html:
• Description

  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • Extrusion is not included in these kits.

    This Elevator is designed to make building an elevator as simple as possible. With a detailed assembly guide and carefully designed components, the Powered Elevator makes some of the most difficult things about elevators for FIRST Robotics Competition easy by providing a simple string-driven solution to lift an assembly up and down. The Powered Elevator is easily customizable to your liking, allowing you to rig it as a continuous elevator or as a cascade elevator by adding additional stages to increase your travel. This Elevator is designed around the use of Pre-drilled tubing, the standard for FRC construction, and each stage stays on our classic 10-32 0.5 in. grid.

title: Programmable Servos
body_html:
The AndyMark Programmable Servos are adjustable metal-geared servos that are perfect for use in robot mechanisms.

  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • These servos can be programmed to include angular limits as well as continuous rotation mode, making them highly adaptable. Overall, these servos are designed to fuse many ease-of-use features into one package. The built in mounting tabs feature 10-32 sized holes on a 1/2 in. spacing making it easy to integrate into designs. Additionally, the hex output makes adding attachments a breeze.

    Default Mode

    This servo defaults to the standard angular mode and will respond to input pulses between 500μs – 2500μs.

    Programmable Features

    • Programming the servos can be done with the Programmable Servo Programmer (am-3218) sold separately.
    • Angular Mode
      • Angular limits and run to position commands can be modified to allow full or clipped positional range.
      • 1-turn Servos can be controlled up to ~300° in Angular mode
      • 5-turn Servos can be controlled up to 1800° in Angular mode
    • Continuous Rotation Mode
      • Continuous rotation mode can be set from the programmer and allow the output to spin indefinitely in either direction.

    • Analog Feedback

      • The analog feedback versions of these servos has a fourth wire that can be read to determine the position of the internal potentiometer. 

      • This lets you know the output of the servo at all times and pairs well with our analog breakout board (am-5681).

      am-4954 and am-4954a High Torque 1-Turn

      Specifications:
      • Default Angular Range: 280°
      • Input Pulse Range: 500μs – 2500μs
      • Size: 2.5 in. x 1.64 in. x 1.76 in.
      • Speed: 0.2 s/60° , ~50 RPM (at 6V)
      • Output Material: Steel
      • Output Profile: 5mm Hex with M3 threads
      • Stall Current: 1.7A max (at 6V)

title: Pronoun Pins
body_html:
The official Rainbow STEM Alliance Pronoun Pin is an emamel coated, steel lapel pin with a variety of pronoun options.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • From 2017-2019, The Rainbow STEM Alliance provided pronoun ribbons at the FIRST Championship events, in partnership with their earliest supporters, and The LGBTQ+ of FIRST student organization. In 2020, they made the decision to switch to a longer lasting lapel pin. This diestruck, enamel coated, steel pin is slightly larger than the LGBTQ+ of FIRST lapel pin, and will last for many competitions, without the need for a specific badge to hang it on. New for 2023 are 3 new pin options, She/They, He/They, and “Any Pronouns”, in addition to the original offerings of He/Him, She/Her, They/Them, and “Ask Me About My Pronouns” bringing the total to 7. Based on feedback from so many in the community, the RSA has also started transitioning the design to be higher contrast, in an effort to ease visibility, and the AndyMark pins will follow suit in time.

    We at AndyMark are proud to continue our support of the Rainbow STEM Alliance, and their mission to support LGBTQ+ youth pursuing STEM education. As a part of our partnership, a majority of the proceeds from these pin sales goes directly to The Rainbow STEM Alliance.

    Quantity Discounts on these products will show up after they are added to a cart. Discounts only apply to individual part numbers, ex: ordering 10 She/Her pins will get a discount, but ordering 5 She/Her and 5 They/Them will not. The quantity discounts on these products are as follows:

    1-9 : $9.00

    10-24 : $8.50

title: Raptor Track Drive
body_html:
The Raptor Track Drive is an efficient, low profile, tank track system utilizing timing belt treads.
  • Description
  • What's in the Box?
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • The Raptor Track Drive (am-4020) is an efficient, low profile tank track system utilizing timing belt treads. This product uses much of the same components from our popular Rhino Track Drive, with many improvements.

    Improvements compared to Rhino Track Drive:
    • Side plates are one continual piece of 1/8 inch thick aluminum, much like our popular AM14U series chassis structure.
    • A balanced, dual turnbuckle mechanism provides tension for each belt in a compact manner.
    • Timing belt tread choices are available. Depending on their application, users can choose either blue nitrile roughtop tread (am-3288) or black urethane flat tread (am-4017).
    • Low profile with flanges top and bottom allows for easier bumper mounting.
    • The tensioning method is contained within the plates, meaning the robot frame perimeter does not change when the belts are tensioned.
    Carryover features from Rhino Track Drive:
    • Tough polycarbonate pulleys (am-3298a) drive the treads, five (5) for each module. These are the same pulleys which have been tested on Rhino systems since 2016.
    • Various gearboxes can be mounted to the inside plate, as mounting holes will allow for a Toughbox Mini, EVO Shifter, EVO Slim for CIMs, or EVO Slim for 775s gearbox to drive the tread mechanism.
    Modules:
    Raptor Track Drive Modules ship in an un-assembled kits. They include the hardware, side plates, and one belt. Due to the design of the side plates, they are available in LEFT and RIGHT versions. Since they are offered with two tread choices, customers have a total of four (4) modules to choose from:
    • Raptor Track Drive Left Black Module (am-4020L_black)
    • Raptor Track Drive Right Black Module (am-4020R_black)
    • Raptor Track Drive Left Blue Module (am-4020L_blue)
    • Raptor Track Drive Right Blue Module (am-4020R_blue)
    Chassis:
    Customers can purchase an entire Raptor Track Drive chassis, which includes two (2) modules and connecting extrusions, Peanut and Walnut. Three (3) foot lengths of these extrusions ship with two modules so the user can cut them to length for their application in order to make a strong drive system structure.
    • Raptor Track Drive Chassis, Black (am-4020_black)
    • Raptor Track Drive Chassis, Blue (am-4020_blue)
    Please see the assembly instructions in the "Documents" section for any assembly assistance.

  • Included Items:

    Included Hardware for Modules:
    • Raptor Track Drive Left Module Common Hardware (qty. per module)
      • 1 - Bearing Kit
        • 10 - 1614ZZ Bearing (am-0209)
        • 1 - FR8ZZ Hex Bearing (am-2986)
      • 1- Motion Hardware Kit
        • 1 - 250 Sprocket/Pulley Spacer (am-0207a)
        • 2 - 22T #35 Sprocket (am-0216)
        • 1 - 500Hex Hub (am-2568)
        • 2 - Turnbuckle (am-1429)
        • 6 - 10-32 Nylock Nut (am-1042)
        • 6 - 10-32 x 750 SHCS (am-1047)
      • 1- Spacer Kit
        • 6 - AS62-18-34 AL Spacer (am-1514)
        • 4 - MAS16-10-5 AL Spacer (am-1515)
        • 4 - .125t x 443ID Nylon Spacer (am-2930)
        • 2 - 500Hex Molded Spacer x 1in (am-3948-1000)
        • 1 - 500Hex Molded Spacer x 0.188in (am-3948-188)
      • 1 - Axle Kit
        • 5 - 3/8-16 x 4.25 Bolt (am-1297)
        • 5 - 3/8-16 Nylock Jam Nut (am-1394)
        • 2 - 3/8 Washer (am-1393)
      • 40 - 1/4-20 x 750 Thread Forming Screw (am-1310)
      • 30 - 10-24 x 1.25 Thread Forming Screw (am-1266)
      • 10 - 3.375 in. Churro (am-2569)
      • 5 - 20T Track Drive Pulley Half, Rev 4 (am-3298a)
    • Side Plates (one pair for each module)
      • Left Module
        • 1 - Raptor Inside Plate, Left (am-4011L)
        • 1 - Raptor Outside Plate, Left (am-4012L)
      • Right Module
        • 1 - Raptor Inside Plate, Right (am-4011L)
        • 1 - Raptor Outside Plate, Right (am-4012R)
    • #35 Chain
      • 1 - #35 Roller Chain, 10 ft. (one per module, am-0367)
    • Belts (one provided per module)
      • 1 - Blue Nitrile Roughtop Belt (am-3288)
      • 1 - Black Urethane Flat Belt (am-4017)
    Included Hardware for Chassis:
    • Black Tread Version
      • 1 - Raptor Track Drive Left Module (am-4020L_black)
      • 1 - Raptor Track Drive Right Module (am-4020R_black)
      • 2 - Peanut Extrusion, 3 ft. (am-3090-3)
      • 2 - Walnut Extrusion, 3 ft. (am-3478-3)
      • 1 - #35 roller chain, 10 ft. (one per chassis, am-0367)
    • Blue Tread Version
      • 1 - Raptor Track Drive Left Module (am-4020L_blue)
      • 1 - Raptor Track Drive Right Module (am-4020R_blue)
      • 2 - Peanut Extrusion, 3 ft. (am-3090-3)
      • 2 - Walnut Extrusion, 3 ft. (am-3478-3)
      • 1 - #35 roller chain, 10 ft. (one per chassis, am-0367)

    Not Included: Drive train components such as gearboxes, transmissions, motors, bumper mounting systems are not included with Raptor Track Drive Modules or Chassis.

title: Power Cable, offset Black/Red, custom lengths up to 36 in.
body_html:
This is a customizable cable kit for the SB connector.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • This is the SB connector side of the custom length robot power cable kit. It is offered as an option to those who are looking to customize further and do not want the ring terminal ends to be the same overall distance from the SB connector, or who need a replacement cable.

    All wire connections are crimped with a 6-ton pneumatic crimping tool to ensure they are never the failure point.

    How to Customize:

    1. Select your Cable Gauge and Type
    2. Select the overall cable length, which does not included the SB connector
    3. Select the length of the Red Wire side, which is typically the length between the SB connector and the 120A Breaker

    Note: Lengths are +/- 0.5 in.

    Competition Tip: Remember, as the cable length increases, so does the internal resistance of the overall system. This creates a voltage drop that means less power going to your motors and control system. For best results, you'll want to keep this cable as short as your design allows safely.

title: Robot Power Cable Kit, custom lengths up to 36 in.
body_html:
• Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • Everyone's Robot is different, this lets you customize the wire gauge, jacket type and lengths of your Robot Side Power Cable designed to connect a Power Distribution Panel mounted on your robot to a battery via a battery cable (6AWG, 6AWG Custom, or 4AWG), It includes a 120A Breaker.

    All wire connections are crimped with a 6-ton pneumatic crimping tool to ensure they are never the failure point.

    How to Customize:

    1. Select your Cable Gauge, Type, and SB Connector
    2. Select the overall cable length, which does not included the SB Connector
    3. Select the length between the SB Connector and the 120A Breaker on the red wire side
    4. The length of the individual red cable will be calculated automatically to make the ring terminal connections the same distance from the APP.

    Note: Lengths are +/- 0.5 in.

    Competition Tip: Remember, as the cable length increases, so does the internal resistance of the overall system. This creates a voltage drop that means less power going to your motors and control system. For best results, you'll want to keep this cable as short as your design allows safely.

title: Red Power Wire, multiple lengths 5 in. to 29 in.
body_html:
These Power Wires are offered in 2 different guages and in lengths between 5 in. and 29 in.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • Used in the custom length robot power cable kit, this option is offered in different lengths between 5 in. and 29 in.

    All wire connections are crimped with a 6-ton pneumatic crimping tool to ensure they are never the failure point.

    How to Customize:

    1. Select your Cable Gauge and Cable Jacket type.
    2. Select the length of red wire needed.

    Note: Lengths are +/- 0.5 in.

    Competition Tip: Remember, as the cable length increases, so does the internal resistance of the overall system. This creates a voltage drop that means less power going to your motors and control system. For best results, you'll want to keep this cable as short as your design allows safely.

title: Robits Lift Kit
body_html:
Fully compatible with the Robits Build System, this lift offers a durable linear motion option to help teams reach their goals.
  • Description
  • What's in the Box?
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • In FTC, a simple lift can be a very powerful thing. Fully compatible with the Robits Build System, this lift offers a durable linear motion option to help teams reach their goals. Teams familiar with FRC-style elevators will find many key features that are now the gold standard for lifts. This kit is bearing-based, providing smooth extension and retraction with bearings reacting on perpendicular tube faces to prevent binding. The carriage section has plenty of mounting holes for teams to mount a wide range of mechanisms and components making it adaptable to any situation.

    Options:

    • 1 Stage has 9.5 inches of stroke
    • 2 Stages has 21 inches of stroke

    Suggested Rigging:

    • Continuous
      • One string per direction that connects through each stage
      • For more details, see the assembly guide

    Included Powering/Gearing:

    • NeveRest Hex 13.7 to 1
      • Speedy, approximately 1 second per stage at full speed.
      • Enough torque to easily lift multiple stages with a manipulator and game pieces
    • No Motor Included options do not have a motor. They are compatible with NeveRest Hex Gearmotors  
      • For lower load applications, a lower ratio gearmotor like a 13.7, is ideal.
      • For higher load applications, a larger ratio gear motor like a 19.2 or 50.9 is ideal.

    Further rigging assembly instructions can be found in the video:

title: Robits Angle Gussets
body_html:
These Gussets are used to connect components within the Robits platform.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • Robits Angle Gussets are used to quickly and easily mount to Robits structure at a precise angle. Featuring the standard Robits hole pattern of a clearance hole for 10-32 screws every 0.5 in., these gussets are a versatile addition to your Robits collection.

    Each Angle Gusset has a complimentary gusset, with their angle adding up to 180°. These pairs are often used together and are color-coded to match their partners.

    • 30° & 150° (White)
    • 45° & 135° (Black)
    • 60° & 120° (Gray)
    • Grid Hole Spacing: 0.50 in.
    • Hole Size: 0.201 in.
    • Material: Polycarbonate
    • Thickness: 0.25 in.

title: Robits Carriers
body_html:
Robits uses components we call carriers to assist in all sorts of motion applications.
  • Description
  • Specifications

  • Carriers come in two types: shaft and bushing.

    • Shaft carriers transfer torque using an integrated 3/8 hex feature and are made of durable polycarbonate plastic.
    • Bushing carriers allow hex shafts to spin smoothly due to their low surface friction material: acetal.
    • Hole Spacing: 0.50 in.
    • Material: Polycarbonate, Acetal
    • Mounting Hole Size: 0.201 in.

title: Robits Drop Brackets
body_html:
These drop brackets are motor mounting brackets for the Robits line of products.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • These Mounting Brackets are a part of the Robits Building System and can be used to fasten motors to get your robot moving.

    Drop Mount (am-5019):

    This bracket is most often used with the Gearbox Mount (am-5018_1) to provide a slight drop or rise to a motion component.

    80T or 100T Drop Motor Mount (am-5018_1):

    The 80T - 100T Motor Mount is primarily designed to integrate with our 1 in. Robits tube, providing a slight drop or rise to the output from the gearbox. This gusset is 1/8 in. thick 6061 aluminum making it resilient to bending even under heavy loads. It utilizes a unique slotted feature to allow users the option of making an 80 tooth or 100 tooth gearbox.

    80T Supported Gear Pairs

    • 20T (am-3820) & 60T (am-5020_60) [3:1]
    • 28T (am-3647) & 52T (am-4733) [1.9:1]
    • 30T (am-5020_30) & 50T (am-5020_50) [1.7:1]
    • 40T & 40T (am-5020_40) [1:1]

    100T Supported Gear Pairs

    • 40T (am-5020_40) & 60T (am-5020_60) [1.5:1]
    • 50T & 50T (am-5020_50) [1:1]
    • Gusset Mounting Hole Diameter: 0.201 in.
    • Motor Boss Hole Diameter: 0.8741 - 0.8749 in.
    • Motor Mounting Bolt Circle: 1.102 in. [28 mm]
    • Motor Mounting Hole Diameter: 0.125 in.

title: Robits Mounting Brackets
body_html:
These Mounting Brackets for the Robits Building System are to fasten motors to your robot.

  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • These Mounting Brackets are a part of the Robits Building System and can be used to fasten motors to get your robot moving.

    Motor Mount [Side 2 Hole] (am-5012):

    The Side 2 Hole Motor Mount is an excellent way of mounting a NeveRest motor to your Robits tubes. The mounting gusset is 1/8 in. thick 6061 aluminum for strength and features an 8 hole NeveRest hole pattern to allow users to mount a motor in 45° increments. The corners are notched to allow the mount to fit nicely against other Robits tubes and the 2 #10-32 holes are aligned on the bracket to allow it to be mounted centered on a tube. Additionally, this gusset is compatible with our 3/8 in. hex bearing (am-4489).

    Side Slotted Motor Mount (am-5033):

    The Side Slotted Motor Mount is comparable to our original Motor Mount (am-5012), but with some more flexibility on placement. The mounting gusset is 1/8 in. thick 6061 aluminum for strength and features an 8 hole NeveRest hole pattern to allow users to mount a motor in 45° increments. The corners are notched to allow the mount to fit nicely against other Robits tubes and the 2 #10-32 holes are aligned on the bracket to allow it to be mounted centered on a tube. Additionally, this gusset is compatible with our 3/8 in. hex bearing (am-4489).

    80T or 100T Motor Mount (am-5017):

    The 80T - 100T Motor Mount is primarily designed to integrate with our 1 in. Robits tube. This gusset is 1/8 in. thick 6061 aluminum making it resilient to bending even under heavy loads. It utilizes a unique slotted feature to allow users the option of making an 80 tooth or 100 tooth gearbox.

    80T Supported Gear Pairs

    • 20T (am-3820) & 60T (am-5020_60) [3:1]
    • 28T (am-3647) & 52T (am-4733) [1.9:1]
    • 30T (am-5020_30) & 50T (am-5020_50) [1.7:1]
    • 40T & 40T (am-5020_40) [1:1]

    100T Supported Gear Pairs

    • 40T (am-5020_40) & 60T (am-5020_60) [1.5:1]
    • 50T & 50T (am-5020_50) [1:1]

    Double Motor Pass Through Plate (am-5045):

    This Bracket is primarily used in the Robits Multi Motor Pass Through Gearbox and can facilitate motor mounting or hold an 0.875 in. OD Bearing such as am-4489. It is made from polycarbonate and is shaped so that it can be braced around 1 x 1 in. Tubes.

    80T or 100T Double Motor Mount (am-5042):

    This Double Motor can integrate two motors into one system I order to take advantage of both of their Torque. It is primarily designed to integrate with our 1 in. Robits tube. This gusset is 1/8 in. thick 6061 aluminum making it resilient to bending even under heavy loads. It utilizes a unique slotted feature to allow users the option of making an 80 tooth or 100 tooth gearbox.

    80T Supported Gear Pairs

    • 20T (am-3820) & 60T (am-5020_60) [3:1]
    • 28T (am-3647) & 52T (am-4733) [1.9:1]
    • 30T (am-5020_30) & 50T (am-5020_50) [1.7:1]
    • 40T & 40T (am-5020_40) [1:1]
    100T Supported Gear Pairs
    • 40T (am-5020_40) & 60T (am-5020_60) [1.5:1]
    • 50T & 50T (am-5020_50) [1:1]

    Single Motor Bearing Mount (am-5022):

    This Bracket is primarily used in the Robits Solo Motor Bearing Assembly and can facilitate motor mounting or hold an 0.875 in. OD Bearing such as am-4489. It is made from polycarbonate and is shaped so that it can be braced around 1 x 1 in. Tubes.

    Pass Through Plate (am-5023):

    This Bracket is primarily used in the Robits Pass Through Gearbox and can facilitate motor mounting or hold an 0.875 in. OD Bearing such as am-4489. It is made from polycarbonate and is shaped so that it can be braced around 1 x 1 in. Tubes.

    Sport Gearbox Mount (am-5043):

    This Bracket allows a Sport Gearbox to be able to be mounted onto Robits! With a 0.5 inch hole spacing, this bracket is perfect for mounting on any Robits Tubes or Gussets. It's 1/8 in. thick 6061 aluminum making it quite tough.

    80T Sport Gearbox Mount (am-5044):

    This Sport Gearbox mount is compatible with our Robits 1x1 Tubes and features an 80 tooth gear spacing between the the Sport output and the Tube's bushing hole. It's made from 1/8 in. thick 6061 aluminum so it can allow users to create a rigid 80 tooth gearbox.

    • Gusset Mounting Hole Diameter: 0.201 in.
    • Motor Boss Hole Diameter: 0.8741 - 0.8749 in.
    • Motor Mounting Bolt Circle: 1.102 in. [28 mm]
    • Motor Mounting Hole Diameter: 0.125 in.

title: Robits Tubes
body_html:
The Robits building system uses Tubes as the main structural component.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • These tubes feature holes on a 1/2 inch grid, matching all Robits components.

    0.5 in. x 0.5 in. Tube Profile:

    This is the most basic building block of the Robits system. The Tube is 0.5 in. x 0.5 in., with a wall thickness of 0.063 in. Each side has holes every 0.5 inch for the length of the Tube making it easy to mount components in 90° increments. These are great for creating structure and motion components due to their small profile and easy to fasten to nature.

    These are currently available in 1.5, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, and 47 inch lengths.

    1 in. x 1 in. Tube Profile:

    This Tube profile allows motion components to be seamlessly integrated into a Robits structure. Two sides of this extrusion feature two rows of holes, 0.5 inches from each other. The other two faces have a pattern that includes holes for bushings, allowing gears, pulleys and sprockets to spin easily on a predefined spacing.

    These are currently available in 5, 8, 11.5, and 15.5 inch lengths.

    1 in. x 0.5 in. Tube Profile:

    These Tubes are like our 0.5 in. x 0.5 in Tubes but double wide. They feature two rows of holes on the 1 inch wide face and single row of holes on the 0.5 inch space, all spaced 0.5 inches apart. These are great for more robust connections as well as supporting linear motion.

    These are currently available in 14 inch lengths.

    • Material: 6061-T6 Aluminum
    • Screw Hole Size: 0.201 in.
    • Typical Screw Spacing: 0.50 in.

title: SDS Elevator Kit
body_html:
• Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • SDS Billet Bearing Blocks are the core of an incredibly efficient and smooth elevator mechanism. Select the desired number of stages, tube thickness, and extrusion inclusion to create your complete elevator mechanism.

    SDS Billet Elevator Bearing Blocks are designed to integrate with included tube plugs and commonly available pre-drilled or punched 2x1 tubing. Attach 1 or 2 tube plugs to a bearing block depending on where it is used on an elevator. These allow the connection between the box tube and the Bearing Blocks to be primarily inside of the box tube, resulting in an incredibly low profile.

    These premium bearings blocks utilize cam followers for the primary load direction. Cam followers are designed for the line contact loading present in FRC elevators and have a higher load rating when compared to similarly sized ball bearings. Cam followers also have a much larger face width than typical bearings, allowing for more overlap to prevent elevator stages from becoming dislodged.

    SDS bearing blocks come with 2 sets of spacers for the cam followers. Users can decide if they would like to use the long spacers for maximum bearing overlap, or the short spacers if needed for screw head clearance.

title: SDS Gear Ratio Kits
body_html:
These gears are the controlling factor for the SDS modules' drive gear ratios.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • The MK4 is compatible with all 4 drive gear ratios. The MK4c, MK4i, MK4n are available in ratios L1-L3. The L2 ratio is the most popular ratio and are suitable for standard full-weight competition robots. The L3 ratio is more aggressive and is recommended for lightweight robots. The L4 ratio is very aggressive and is only recommended for very lightweight mini bots.

    The "L" followed by a number indicates the specific gear ratio. The "+" designator after L# indicates that the pinion gear on the drive motor is a 16T, instead of a 14T. The L# and L#+ therefore refer to the overall gear ratio of the swerve module. The pinion gear size is specific to each swerve module, and it is not included in the L Gearset.

    The swerve module product pages (MK4, MK4c, MK4i, MK4n) detail the drivetrain free speeds based on the motor and gear ratios.

    Please refer to following table and Notes below for what is included and what gear ratios are applicable to each swerve module:



    Notes:

    • The standard MK4i is offered with L1, L2, and L3. It can be converted to the "+" version of the gear ratio via the 16T Drive Pinion Gear Adapter Kit. That kit replaces the standard 14T drive motor pinion gear with a 16T.
    • Matching L gear ratio kits will result in the same drivetrain free speed across the entire MK4 family of swerve modules, so different swerve modules can be used on the same drivetrain. For instance:

      • L2 MK4 and L2 MK4i have the same drivetrain free speed.
      • L3+ MK4i (L3 Gearset + 16T Drive Pinion Gear Adapter Kit) and L3+ MK4n have the same drivetrain free speed.


    L1 Gear Ratio 8.14:1 (MK4/4i):

    • 25T-50T 20DP Double Gear
    • 19T 20DP 3/8 Hex Bore Gear

    L2 Gear Ratio 6.75:1 (MK4/4i):

    • 27T-50T 20DP Double Gear
    • 17T 20DP 3/8 Hex Bore Gear

    L3 Gear Ratio 6.12:1 (MK4/4i):

    • 28T-50T 20DP Double Gear
    • 16T 20DP 3/8 Hex Bore Gear

    L4 Gear Ratio 5.14:1 (MK4):

    • 28T-48T 20DP Double Gear
    • 16T 20DP 3/8 Hex Bore Gear
    • Finish: Black Oxide
    • Material: Steel

body_html:
This robot is intended for use as a programming test platform for university and high school classrooms.
  • Description

  • This two-wheel tabletop robot was developed in collaboration with Purdue University.

    The Skitter Robot is intended for use as a programming test platform for university and high school classrooms. Additionally, it can be used for custom tabletop robotics projects. Skitter can handle several sensor inputs and has robust drive motors with encoder feedback. The frame is a strong sheet metal construction with a hard-anodized finish. This robot can be used on classroom tabletops and floors and is small enough to be transported in a backpack.

    Skitter Arduino Classroom Robot: This version was designed with Purdue University for use in their ME375 class. It utilizes the Arduino Mega to teach control systems in the classroom.

    Purdue Students: This unit is sold as a disassembled kit with tools. Purdue students looking to purchase this robot for classes can get a discounted price with the use of a coupon code provided by your instructor.

      • Max current draw: 0.95 amps
      • Max power output: 2.5 Watts at 45% efficiency
    • Motor Controller Output

title: Small Electronic Bundles Builder
body_html:
Configure your own control system with this Electronics Bundle Builder.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • Electronics are the power and brains behind every incredible robot and machine. Figuring out all the individual pieces needed to make a robot go can be tedious which is why we've made it easy with this electronic bundles builder page!
    This builder is focused on a smaller sized robot using SPARKmini brushed motor controllers. Think FTC sized robots, 1-2 foot cubed sized.

    Choose your processor, # of motors your working with, and power distribution option to create a complete electronics system to suit your needs.
    A Few Recommended Options:
    • BCLM4XU - This bundle utilizes the RadioLink with SparkMini brushed motor controllers and an unfused power distribution block making it incredibly easy to get a basic robot up and running. Combine this with a mecanum mixer (am-5212) and you're on your way to a functional mecanum drive.
    • BCNM4XU - This bundle is exactly like the one above, it's just without the RadioLink. This bundle is awesome for FTC teams hoping to add more motors to their robot without adding an Expansion hub. NOTE: you will get a Servo Range Extender (am-5164) for each motor, and these are NOT legal per FTC rules.
    Electronic bundles product numbers are built to identify components within the code. Below is the breakdown of how these part numbers are built.
    • The first two positions identifies the product number:
      • BC - Bundle for Controls
    • The third position identifies the controller and will come with components needed to hook it up (see link):
      • L - RadioLink - a simplistic approach of a simple Radio Control with limited programming capability in the controller
      • N - No Processor - so you'll need to have your own controller.
    • The fourth position identifies the motor controller and will come with the components needed to hook it up (see link):
      • M - SPARKmini Brushed DC Motor Controller is our only option for this bundle
    • The fifth position identifies the quantity of motors this bundle is designed to work with and includes the wires needed to hook them up:
      • 1 - One Motors
      • 2 - Two Motors
      • 3 - Three Motors
      • 4 - Four Motors
      • 5 - Five Motors
    • The sixth position identifies the type of motor:
      • X - As there is so many options of motors, we leave this up to you and this is always an X for this product, please be sure to use motors that are compatible with the SPARKmini Brushed DC Motor Controller.
      • Please note: You will also get a Servo Range Extender with these kits that are NOT legal for FTC.
    • The seventh position identifies the type of power distribution and will come with components needed to hook them up (see links):
      • F - XT30 Fused Power Distribution Board - replaceable fuses allow additional protection for changing robot requirements
      • U - Unfused XT30 Power Distribution Block - designed for FTC and simple robot construction with XT30 connections

title: SmoothGrip Wheels
body_html:
SmoothGrip wheels provide strong traction with a long life-span good for robot drive wheels or flywheels to propel game pieces.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • Looking or a flat profile wheel with plenty of grip? Look no further than our six or eight inch SmoothGrip wheels! Many are familiar with our flagship HiGrip wheels which feature an aggressive tread pattern great for biting hard into the ground. SmoothGrip wheels provide a strong level of traction with a longer life-span thanks to their smooth profile. They make great drive wheels on almost any surface as well as great flywheels to propel game pieces at high speed without damage. SmoothGrip wheels feature your favorite 1.125 in. bearing bore and 1.875 in. bolt circle, allowing you to mount a hub or bearing of your choice for live or dead axle setups.

    In 2010, the Gray 8 in. 80A Durometer SmoothGrip wheel was provided in the FRC Kit of Parts under the name "FIRST Wheel". No bearings are included.

    Usage With Axle and Hub:

    • If you wish to drive this wheel with an axle and hub, you can pick your hub by fitting any of the AndyMark hubs to this wheel. Hubs are not included with this wheel. If this is your choice, then no bearing is needed. To install a hub onto this wheel, use #10-24x3/4 thread forming screws.

    Usage With Sprockets and Bearings:

    • If you wish to drive this wheel with a sprocket, then the sprocket needs to be attached to the side of the wheel with #10-24x3/4 thread forming screws. You will also need to press ball bearings into the wheel so that it may spin on a shaft or bolt. The ball bearings must have a 1.125 in. od. For a 1/2 in. shafts, use am-0181. For a 3/8 in. shafts use am-0209.

    Please note: due to the way these wheels are molded, the outer profile may be tapered slightly to one side; this does not significantly affect performance as a drive wheel in most applications.

    • Bolt Pattern: Six holes (0.17 in. diameter) on a 1.875 in. diameter bolt circle
    • Bore: 0.95 in. diameter through hole, with two 1.125 in. diameter bearing pockets
    • CoF: 1.0 static (on tight pile carpet)
    • Diameter: 6 in., 8in.
    • Durometer: 50A, 60A, 80A
    • Material: Black Polycarbonate, urethane rubber
    • Weight: 0.58 lbs., 0.62 lbs.

title: FIRST Tech Challenge Field Soft Tiles
body_html:
Soft Tiles are 2' x 2' x 5/8 in. thick gray floor mats that are used on the FIRST Tech Challenge playing field.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • AndyMark’s FIRST Tech Challenge Field Soft Tiles (am-2499) have a size variance. Some tiles are slightly smaller than tiles used during previous years. The size range is anywhere from 24 ¼” to 24 ⅜” from outside to outside of each tile. Stacked 6 wide, this ⅛” variance can be up to ¾” across an FTC field. AndyMark recommends that teams assemble their perimeter on top of an assembled 6x6 grid of tiles before cutting off any tabs. More information is available in this document.

    Soft Tiles are 2' x 2' x 5/8 in. thick gray floor mats that are used on the FIRST Tech Challenge (am-0481a) playing field.
    • A full FTC field requires 36 tiles.
    • Tiles should be laid out smooth side up when setting up an FTC field.

    The interlocking edges of these tiles connect nicely for a quick setup and will stay firmly in place. The edges can be easily cut for a straight edge as required when used on an FTC playing field. The tiles are double-sided with both a textured and a smooth side to suit any need. Disassembly is simple and we suggest these Soft Tile Bags for storage and transport. Each bag can carry up to 18 tiles.

    These tiles are ideally suited for a variety of purposes and are perfect for exercise areas, playrooms, and workshops. The soft, durable mats would also work well anywhere that needs a bit more cushion - including camping or as an anti-fatigue standing mat. These mats are made from a non-toxic EVA (ethylene vinyl acetate) foam.

    Tiles can be purchased in single quantities, packs of 4, 18, or 36. Please note when purchasing quantities of less than 36 to interface with previously purchased tiles there may be some batch variance in the color, exact tooth shape and overall tile size resulting in small gaps or complete assemblies that are slightly smaller than the field perimeter.
    Information about ESD can be found here: https://www.alphalabinc.com/triboelectric-series/

    • Height: 5/8 in. [16 mm]

    • 2 - 10-32 x 1 in. Socket Head Cap Screw (am-1056)

    Sport Gearbox Kraken Uncut Shaft Pinion Kit (am-5582):

    • 1 - 1/4-20 x 0.5 in. Button Head Cap Screw (am-1739)
    • 1 - 16T Mod 0.7 SplineXS Kraken Motor Pinion (am-5434)
    • 2 - 10-32 x 0.625 in. Socket Head Cap Screw with Nylon Thread Lock Patch (am-1120)

    Sport Gearbox CIM & NEO Motor Pinion Kit (am-3771a):

    • 1 - 16 Tooth 0.7 Module 8 mm Round Bore Steel Pinion Gear for CIM Sport (am-3785)
    • 2 - 10-32 x 1 in. Socket Head Cap Screw (am-1056)

    Sport Gearbox Minion Pinion Kit (am-5616):

    • 1 - 8 mm ID 0.500 in. OD 0.500 in. Long Aluminum Spacer (am-1751)
    • 1 - Kraken/Minion Sport Gearbox Pinion (am-5434)
    • 5 - 10-32 x 0.500 in. Socket Head Cap Screw with Nylon Thread Lock Patch (am-1744)

    -------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

    CIM / NEO Pinion Installation:
    The 16 tooth pinion gear for the CIM / NEO does not use a key for torque transfer. There are two possible methods of installation of this pinion on a CIM or NEO style motor.

    • If the tolerances of both the motor shaft and the pinion are in your favor an arbor press (possibly up to 3 tons) is required to install this pinion due to the intended interference fit (0.001 - 0.002 in.). In the Sport gearbox these pinions are designed to press flush to the end of the shaft.
      • If using an original NEO motor Please follow the NEO Press Fit Pinion Guide.
      • If using a NEO 1.1 Motor insert a #10-32 x 3/8in long socket head screw into the hole in the back of the motor to support the internal shaft while pressing pinions.
    • If the tolerances are not in your favor and the pinions slip on the shaft, or you feel that the press fit it too weak, an adhesive is required to transfer torque. The procedure is the same for all motors.
      • Apply a few rings of red Loctite to the shaft, and the bore of the pinion, then slip the pinion onto the shaft so that it is flush with the tip of the shaft.
        • Red Loctite has been tested to a factor of safety of 4x the stall torque of a CIM when let to cure for 24 hours.

    If you are are unable or uncomfortable performing these procedures, we recommend purchasing a motor with the pinion pre-installed. They are available as am-0255_16T for the CIM and am-4258a_16T for the NEO.

title: TileRunner 6WD - Configurable FTC Chassis
body_html:
• Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • Your one-stop-shop for all your FTC Chassis needs!

    Configurability

    FIRST Tech Challenge teams are unique and require unique solutions. The Configurable FTC Chassis has been developed around five main configurations: The original TileRunner 6-wheel drop center or 4-wheel drive (mecanum), the TreadRunner (tank treads), and the super smooth MecanAM Chassis.
    • Need a balanced drivetrain that can turn on a dime? Choose a 6-wheel configuration.
    • Precision movements in all directions part of your game plan? Mecanum variations allow for omnidirectional movement of your robot.
    • Need to get up and over obstacles? TreadRunner can overcome those pesky hurdles.
    • The MecanAM Chassis has omnidirectional movement capabilities that can help drivers smoothly avoid obstacles and quickly change drive direction.

    When selecting your options, rest assured we've considered all the pieces and parts you'll need for the build. You'll only need some tools and your favorite workspace. If you already have many of the components that make up a TileRunner we have options above as well for no motors and/or no plates and/or no wheels!

    Recommendations

    Knowing where to start is no problem! The brief objectives listed below provide you with the best TileRunner Options.
    • The standard basic 6-Wheel TileRunner to get started - BT6S841
    • High Maneuverability in any Direction - BTRMH4E
    • High traction and pushing power - BT6S46A
    • Fast and Easy to turn - BT6O62A

    Looking for the Original TileRunners

    Original TileRunners still exist, just as a different configurator product number! Below you will see links for equivalents under this new structure.
    • TileRunner Frame Only (This requires your own PicoBox plates, NeveRest Motors, and Wheels) as BTFNWNN
    • TileRunner Original 6WD am-3437 as BT6S84E
    • TileRunner Limited Edition (am-3437_LE) as BT6S841
    • TileRunner BullDozer (am-3437_bd) as BT6S56E
    • TileRunner Hulk (am-3437_hulk) as BT6PB4E

    Understanding Part Numbers

    FIRST Tech Challenge Chassis Configurator

    Speed & Gearing

    With four ratios of NeveRest motors and three PicoBox gearbox ratios, a TileRunner can achieve 12 different speeds based on your needs. Just remember that a faster robot will have less torque available to push, climb, or bulldoze.

    Structure & Usage

    The foundation of this drive base is a set of aluminum plates, brackets, and struts that provide a sturdy frame to build upon. All of the holes in the sheet metal are on a global 16 mm pattern, which integrates with numerous structure components across several vendors.

    A 15.75-inch by 11.34-inch perforated polycarbonate sheet acts as a belly pan in the TileRunner and TreadRunner chassis. The sheet features 0.15-inch holes on a 16 mm square and has a thickness of 0.09 inches. This pan adds rigidity and a multitude of mounting locations for additional components like electronics!

    The Peanut and Churro cross members can also be moved into a number of alternate locations to best suit your robot's configuration needs.

    Performance, Rugged, Configurable

    The TileRunner was designed with the FIRST Tech Challenge community in mind. The usage doesn't stop there, however, it can work well for many other robotic competition platforms of similar size. Years of lessons from designing, building, and competing with championship-winning drive systems have gone into this robust drive system that integrates well with teams' existing FTC parts.

    Availability

    To streamline component allocation, please allow for 2-3 days for processing on Configurable FTC Chassis orders.
