title: TileRunner Upgrades
body_html:
Use a TileRunner Upgrade to change options on your existing TileRunner Original 6WD Chassis.

  • Description
  • What's in the Box?
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • Change up your motors and wheels to get more grip, faster speeds, or more pushing power. Swap out your 6WD for mecanum drive and gain the ability to move from side to side.
    TileRunner is the standard for drive systems in FIRST Tech Challenge. We designed it to be configured in many different ways to suit the teams using it. From multiple gearbox locations and options to wheel choices, TileRunner gives you endless adjustment to build your robot your way.

    We identified a few common upgrades on TileRunner's standard drive system. These upgrade kits cover a wide range of use cases, from high-speed maneuvering to moving heavy loads with ease and loads of grip and are used with the TileRunner Original 6WD (am-3437):
    • TileRunner GTO (am-3734): For increased maneuverability, this version substitutes NeveRest Orbital 20 gearmotors (am-3637) and black 4 in. Stealth Wheels (am-2648_Blk) with higher grip than stock and the proper mounting plate, PickBox GEO Plate (am-3476), for the Orbital Gearmotors.
    • TileRunner BullDozer (am-3457): When you want to push, pick this! NeveRest Classic 60 gearmotors (am-3103) provide maximum torque, while six of our softest compound blue 4 in. Stealth Wheels (am-2648_Blue) put that to the ground for maximum pushing force. Pushing hard will increase wear on these wheels, so have a spare set handy for competition time.
    • TileRunner Performance Wheel (am-3459): The TileRunner Performance Wheel Upgrade is your go-to for heavy robots! Six 4 in. Performance Wheels (am-3612) and a 10' roll of our Gray Grippy Tread (am-2611a) replace the Stealth Wheels and provide a very robust drive system.
    • TileRunner SD Mecanum (am-3455): Get set to strafe with four PicoBox Unos replacing the two PicoBox Duos of the standard TileRunner. You'll receive four 4 in. standard-duty mecanum wheels (am-2538) instead of Stealth Wheels, as well as all the spacers, shafts, and gears to get you up and running.
    • SD to HD Mecanum (am-3996): If you already have a TileRunner with SD mecanum wheels this kit will upgrade your chassis to run the new for 2018 HD Mecanum Wheels. This setup continues to use PicoBox Unos and updates the spacers for the new wheels.
    • TileRunner HD Mecanum (am-3997): Get set to strafe with four PicoBox Unos replacing the two PicoBox Duos of the standard TileRunner. You'll receive four 4 in. HD FTC Mecanum Wheels (am-3919) instead of Stealth Wheels, as well as all the spacers, shafts, and gears to get you up and running.
    • TreadRunner (am-3969): Traverse any terrain with a tread equipped TileRunner. This robot drive chassis drives a pair of 2 in. wide timing belt treads to push, climb, and overcome obstacles in it's path. Like other standard TileRunners, it uses two PicoBox Duos along with sturdy aluminum sheet metal frame components. This version of the TileRunner retains the drop center performance boost by adding an idler pulley where the traditional center wheel goes. This way the TreadRunner turns on a dime and trucks in a straight line like no TileRunner kit before.
    Also find each of these upgrades in complete kits on the TileRunner page.

  • TileRunner GTO Upgrade (am-3734):

    • 4 - NeveRest Orbital 20 (am-3637)
    • 2 - PicoBox GEO Plate (am-3476)
    • 6 - 4 in. Stealth Wheel, 8 mm Bore, 60 Durometer Black (am-2648_blk)

    TileRunner BullDozer Upgrade (am-3457):

    • 4 - NeveRest Classic 60 Gearmotor (am-3103)
    • 2 - Duo Plate for PicoBox (am-3405)
    • 6 - Blue (softest compound) 4 in. Stealth Wheel with 8 mm Bore (am-2648_blue)

    TileRunner Mecanum Upgrade (am-3455):

    • 4 - 4 in. Standard Mecanum (am-2538)
    • 2 - Hall Effect Encoder Cable with 4-Pin Connector (am-2992)
    • 4 - PicoBox Uno Plate (am-3423)
    • 8 - PicoBox Spacer (am-3406)
    • 6 - 9 mm x 6.15 mm ID Aluminum Spacer (am-3426)
    • 4 - Spacer, aluminum, 3/8 in. OD x 0.257 in. ID x 19/32 (am-1290)
    • 4 - HD Nub - Bore: 6 mm D Style: Double Boss (am-4311)
    • 2 - 6 mmD x 100 mm Shaft (am-3226-100)
    • 2 - 40t 32dp Gear (am-3407)
    • 8 - 1/4-20 x 1.75 in. BHCS (am-1420)
    • 8 - 1/4-20 Nylock Jam Nut - Bulk Qty (am-1102)
    • 8 - 6-32 0.5 in. Hex Head Screw (am-1436)
    • 16 - 6-32 1.25 in. Hex Head Screw (am-1437)

    TileRunner Performance Wheel Upgrade (am-3459):

    • 6 - 4 in. Aluminum Performance Wheel, 8 mm bore (am-3612)
    • 1 - 10' roll, Gray Grippy Tread 1 in. Wide 10 ft. Long (am-2611a)

    TreadRunner Upgrade (am-3969):

    • 2 - TreadRunner Tread (am-3963)
    • 6 - Pulleys (12 halves) (am-3967)
    • 2 - Tensioner Kits (am-3970h)
    • 6 - 6x4x8 Nylon Bushing (am-1289)
    • 24 - 6-32 x 1.000in Hex Head Screws (am-1426)
    • 36 - 10-24 x 1.250 Self-Tapping Screws (am-1266)
    • 1 - Letter O sized Drill bit (Clearance holes for 8 mm parts) (am-3978)

    SD to HD Mecanum Upgrade (am-3996):

    • 2 - 4 in. HD FTC Mecanum wheels, RIGHT (am-3919R)
    • 2 - 4 in. HD FTC Mecanum wheels, LEFT (am-3919L)
    • 8 - 1/4 in. Aluminum Spacers (am-3424)
    • 16 - 6-32 x 2.000 in. Hex Head Screw (am-1499)

    6wd to HD Mecanum Upgrade (am-3997):

    • 2 - 4 in. HD FTC Mecanum wheels, RIGHT (am-3919R)
    • 2 - 4 in. HD FTC Mecanum wheels, LEFT (am-3919L)
    • 8 - 1/4 in. Aluminum Spacers (am-3424)
    • 16 - 6-32 x 2.000 in. Hex Head Screw (am-1499)
    • 8 - 6-32 x 0.500 in. Hex Head Screw (am-1436)
    • 2 - 40t PicoBox Gear (am-3407)
    • 4 - PicoBox Uno Plate (am-3423)
    • 2 - Aluminum Spacer, 0.242 in ID x 0.5 in OD x 0.354 in (am-3426)
    • 4 - HD Nub - Bore: 6 mm D Style: Double Boss (am-4311)
    • 2 - Encoder Cable (am-2992)
    • 2 - 6 mm D Shaft, 100 mm long (am-3226-100)
    • 8 - PicoBox Spacers (am-3406)
    • 8 - 1/4-20 Nylock Jam Nut (am-1102)
    • 8 - 1/4-20 x 1.750 in. Button Head Cap Screw (am-1420)

body_html:
• Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • Your one-stop-shop for all your FTC Chassis needs!

    Configurability

    FIRST Tech Challenge teams are unique and require unique solutions. The Configurable FTC Chassis has been developed around five main configurations: The original TileRunner 6-wheel drop center or 4-wheel drive (mecanum or traction + omni), the high clearance TileRiser 4-wheel drive (mecanum or traction + omni), the TreadRunner (tank treads), and the super smooth MecanAM Chassis.

    • Need a balanced drive train that can turn on a dime? Choose a 6-wheel configuration.
    • Want to use one end of your robot as the center of rotation to help with alignment? Choose a traction + omni option.
    • Precision movements in all directions part of your game plan? Mecanum variations allow for omnidirectional movement of your robot.
    • Need to get up and over obstacles? TileRiser or TreadRunner variants can overcome those pesky hurdles.
    • The MecanAM Chassis has omnidirectional movement capabilities that can help drivers smoothly avoid obstacles and quickly change drive direction.

    When selecting your options, rest assured we've considered all the pieces and parts you'll need for the build. You'll only need some tools and your favorite workspace. If you already have many of the components that make up a TileRunner we have options above as well for no motors and/or no plates and/or no wheels!

    Recommendations

    Knowing where to start is no problem! The brief objectives listed below provide you with the best TileRunner Options.
    • The standard basic 6-Wheel TileRunner to get started - BT6S841
    • High Maneuverability in any Direction - BTRMH4E
    • High traction and pushing power - BT6S46A
    • Fast and Easy to turn - BT6O62A

    Looking for the Original TileRunners

    Original TileRunners still exist, just as a different configurator product number! Below you will see links for equivalents under this new structure.
    • TileRunner Frame Only (This requires your own PicoBox plates, NeveRest Motors, and Wheels) as BTFNWNN
    • TileRunner Original 6WD am-3437 as BT6S84E
    • TileRunner Limited Edition (am-3437_LE) as BT6S841
    • TileRunner BullDozer (am-3437_bd) as BT6S56E
    • TileRunner Omni (am-3437_omni) as BT6OC4E
    • TileRunner Hulk (am-3437_hulk) as BT6PB4E

    Understanding Part Numbers

    FIRST Tech Challenge Chassis Configurator

    Speed & Gearing

    With four ratios of NeveRest motors and three PicoBox gearbox ratios, a TileRunner can achieve 12 different speeds based on your needs. Just remember that a faster robot will have less torque available to push, climb, or bulldoze.

    Structure & Usage

    The foundation of this drive base is a set of aluminum plates, brackets, and struts that provide a sturdy frame to build upon. All of the holes in the sheet metal are on a global 16 mm pattern, which integrates with numerous structure components across several vendors.

    A 15.75-inch by 11.34-inch perforated polycarbonate sheet acts as a belly pan in the TileRunner and TreadRunner chassis. The sheet features 0.15-inch holes on a 16 mm square and has a thickness of 0.09 inches. This pan adds rigidity and a multitude of mounting locations for additional components like electronics! The added flanges of the TileRiser chassis provide additional rigidity without the need for a bellypan, opening up more space within the footprint of your robot.

    The Peanut and Churro cross members can also be moved into a number of alternate locations to best suit your robot's configuration needs.

    Performance, Rugged, Configurable

    The TileRunner was designed with the FIRST Tech Challenge community in mind. The usage doesn't stop there, however, it can work well for many other robotic competition platforms of similar size. Years of lessons from designing, building, and competing with championship-winning drive systems have gone into this robust drive system that integrates well with teams' existing FTC parts.

    Availability

    To streamline component allocation, please allow for 2-3 days for processing on Configurable FTC Chassis orders.

title: ToughBox S Series 1/2 in. Hex Output Shaft
body_html:
This is the 1/2 in. hex steel output shaft for the Toughbox® series gearboxes when used with the AM14U5.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation


  • The AM14U5 uses round bearings in the outside plate rather than hex bearings. As a result, this shaft differs from previous AM14U output shafts by having a round portion at the end.

    Thanks to the feedback from teams, we've made different versions of this shaft available. If you're using magnetic encoders and need magnets in your shaft, you can order shafts that come with magnets. Want to use non-magnetized dowels for your encoders? We have those too. Don't plan on using encoders? Save some money and order them without pins or magnets.

    Options:
    • No Pins (Supply your own Dowels or Magnets later if needed)
    • Included Magnets - for use with the SRX Magnetic Encoder (am-3445).
    • Included Steel Dowels - for use with the E4T OEM Miniature Optical Encoder (am-3132) or the REV Through Bore Encoder (am-4650)
    Usage:
    To install the provided magnets or pins clean off the pin, apply a few drops of super glue to the hole in the shaft and push the pin in by hand. Give it a turn to spread the glue and wait for it to dry.

    If using this shaft with the SRX Magnetic Encoder (am-3445), the SRX Magnetic Encoder Mounting Hardware Kit (am-3565) will be needed. The hardware allows for proper spacing of the encoder from the shaft magnet on Toughbox® Series Gearboxes.
    • Diameter of Magnet or Pin: 0.25 in.
    • Diameter of Small End: 0.37 in.
    • Hex Width: 0.5 in.
    • Material: Steel

title: Toughbox Classic Series 1/2 in. Output Shafts
body_html:
• Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • The keyed short steel output shaft is optional for the Toughbox® series gearboxes. This shaft includes a pre-installed magnet designed specifically with the E4T OEM Miniature Optical Encoder (am-3132) and SRX Magnetic Encoder (am-3445) encoder in mind. This shaft has replaced am-0153. When used in a Toughbox Series gearbox, this shaft needs to be supported with a 1/2 in. round bearing such as am-0030.
    The hex short output shaft is but one of many options for output when it comes to Toughbox series gearboxes. This shaft includes a magnet pressed into the small end of the output shaft making it compatible with magnetic encoders.

    The keyed steel output shaft can be used in any Toughbox® series gearbox. This shaft includes a pre-installed magnet designed specifically with the E4T OEM Miniature Optical Encoder (am-3132) and SRX Magnetic Encoder (am-3445) encoder in mind. This shaft has replaced am-0506. When used in a Toughbox® series gearbox this shaft needs to be supported with a 1/2 in. hex bearing such as am-0279.

    The long steel output shaft is optional for the Toughbox>® series gearboxes. This shaft includes a pre-installed magnet designed specifically with the E4T OEM Miniature Optical Encoder (am-3132) and SRX Magnetic Encoder (am-3445) encoder in mind. This shaft has replaced am-0211.

    Usage:
    If using this shaft with the SRX Magnetic Encoder (am-3445), the SRX Magnetic Encoder Mounting Hardware Kit (am-3565) will be needed. The hardware allows for proper spacing of the encoder from the shaft magnet on Toughbox® Series Gearboxes and the EVO Shifter.

    Specifications for am-0153a:

    • Diameter of Large End: 0.49 in.
    • Diameter of Small End: 0.37 in.
    • Keyway Length: 1.43 in.
    • Keyway Width: 0.13 in.
    • Overall Length: 3.62 in.
    • Thread: 1/4-20 tapped hole
    • Weight: 0.177 Ibs

    Specifications for am-0802a:

    • Diameter of Small End: 0.375 in.
    • Hex Width: 0.5 in.
    • Large End Includes: 1/4-20 tapped hole
    • Weight: 0.2 Ibs

    Specifications for am-0506a:

    • Depth of Round Portion: 1.52 in.
    • Diameter of Large End: 0.49 in.
    • Diameter of Magnet End: 0.25 in.
    • Keyway Depth: 0.063 in.
    • Keyway Length: 1.395 in.
    • Keyway Width: 0.128 - 0.131 in.
    • Overall Length: 3.755 in.
    • Weight: 0.217 Ibs

    Specifications for am-0211a:

    • Diameter of Large End: 0.49 in.
    • Diameter of Magnet End: 0.24 in.
    • Diameter of Small End: 0.37 in.
    • Hex Width: 0.5 in.
    • Overall Length: 7.14 in.
    • Thread: 1/4-20 tapped 0.5 in. deep
    • Weight: 0.39 Ibs

title: TreadRunner Track Drive - Configurable FTC Chassis
body_html:
• Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • Your one-stop-shop for all your FTC Chassis needs!

    Configurability

    FIRST Tech Challenge teams are unique and require unique solutions. The Configurable FTC Chassis has been developed around five main configurations: The original TileRunner 6-wheel drop center or 4-wheel drive (mecanum or traction + omni), , the TreadRunner (tank treads), and the super smooth MecanAM Chassis.

    • Need a balanced drive train that can turn on a dime? Choose a 6-wheel configuration.
    • Want to use one end of your robot as the center of rotation to help with alignment? Choose a traction + omni option.
    • Precision movements in all directions part of your game plan? Mecanum variations allow for omnidirectional movement of your robot.
    • Need to get up and over obstacles? TreadRunner variants can overcome those pesky hurdles.
    • The MecanAM Chassis has omnidirectional movement capabilities that can help drivers smoothly avoid obstacles and quickly change drive direction.

    When selecting your options, rest assured we've considered all the pieces and parts you'll need for the build. You'll only need some tools and your favorite workspace. If you already have many of the components that make up a TileRunner we have options above as well for no motors and/or no plates and/or no wheels!

    Recommendations

    Knowing where to start is no problem! The brief objectives listed below provide you with the best TileRunner Options.

    • The standard basic 6-Wheel TileRunner to get started - BT6S841
    • High Maneuverability in any Direction - BTRMH4E
    • High traction and pushing power - BT6S46A
    • Fast and Easy to turn - BT6O62A

    Looking for the Original TileRunners

    Original TileRunners still exist, just as a different configurator product number! Below you will see links for equivalents under this new structure.

    • TileRunner Frame Only (This requires your own PicoBox plates, NeveRest Motors, and Wheels) as BTFNWNN
    • TileRunner Original 6WD am-3437 as BT6S84E
    • TileRunner Limited Edition (am-3437_LE) as BT6S841
    • TileRunner BullDozer (am-3437_bd) as BT6S56E
    • TileRunner Omni (am-3437_omni) as BT6OC4E
    • TileRunner Hulk (am-3437_hulk) as BT6PB4E

    Understanding Part Numbers

    Speed & Gearing

    With four ratios of NeveRest motors and three PicoBox gearbox ratios, a TileRunner can achieve 12 different speeds based on your needs. Just remember that a faster robot will have less torque available to push, climb, or bulldoze.

    Structure & Usage

    The foundation of this drive base is a set of aluminum plates, brackets, and struts that provide a sturdy frame to build upon. All of the holes in the sheet metal are on a global 16 mm pattern, which integrates with numerous structure components across several vendors.

    A 15.75-inch by 11.34-inch perforated polycarbonate sheet acts as a belly pan in the TileRunner and TreadRunner chassis. The sheet features 0.15-inch holes on a 16 mm square and has a thickness of 0.09 inches. This pan adds rigidity and a multitude of mounting locations for additional components like electronics!

    The Peanut and Churro cross members can also be moved into a number of alternate locations to best suit your robot's configuration needs.

    Performance, Rugged, Configurable

    The TileRunner was designed with the FIRST Tech Challenge community in mind. The usage doesn't stop there, however, it can work well for many other robotic competition platforms of similar size. Years of lessons from designing, building, and competing with championship-winning drive systems have gone into this robust drive system that integrates well with teams' existing FTC parts.

    Availability

    To streamline component allocation, please allow for 2-3 days for processing on Configurable FTC Chassis orders.

title: West Coast Drive Chassis
body_html:
The AndyMark West Coast Drive Chassis is everything you need to build a robust, 2x1 aluminum box tube West Coast Drive chassis.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • A West Coast Drive has cantilevered wheels on the sides, so wheels stick out from the frame rather than be contained within it as in the AM14U family of drive bases. This kit is sold WITHOUT motors. The AM WCD has lots of useful features that make it an excellent choice for any team wanting to build a drivetrain in this style.

    • Unique geometry enables teams to build it in the efficient chain-in-tube and easily-repairable chain-out-of-tube configurations.
    • Corners are firmly held together with AndyMark's 2x1 box tube plugs AND our 90 degree gussets.
    • Eight wheel drive with an 0.080 in. center drop to ensure smooth driving out on the carpet.
    • Compatibility with AndyMark's EVO line of transmissions, full compatibility with the EVO Slim.
    • All hex-shaft design to enable easy wheel swaps and repair.
    • Compatibility with the am-4576 bearing block kits enables custom drive configurations.

    Configurations! Configurations Everywhere!

    The West Coast Drive is sold in a number of different configurations, so we have created a handy guide to describe all of them.

    Frame Configurations

    • Chain-in-Tube
      • In this configuration, the chain that powers each side of the drivetrain is set inside the 2x1 box tube, saving space, weight, and parts.
    • Chain-out-of-Tube
      • In this configuration, the chain that powers each side of the drivetrain is set outside the 2x1 box tube, giving you the ability to quickly repair the chain and powertrain.
    • Frame Only
      • This is for purchasing only the frame, with no power transmission, drive shafts, or anything of the kind.

    Wheel Type

    • HiGrip Wheels
      • Tried and true wheels for FRC, with an 80A durometer outer tread, plastic interior, and aluminum hub.
    • Performance Wheels
      • AndyMark's highest performing treaded wheel, made out of pure aluminum with our nitrile tread riveted on.
    • No Wheels
      • For buying a frame with no wheels included.

    Wheel Size

    • 6 in. Diameter Wheels
      • Your selected wheels will come as 6 in. diameter wheels.
    • 4 in. Diameter Wheels
      • Your selected wheels will come as 4 in. diameter wheels.
    • Not Applicable
      • For when you do not have any wheels selected.

    Gearbox

    • EVO Slim - SOLD WITHOUT MOTORS.
      • The transmission the WCD was designed around. Guaranteed performance.
    • No Gearbox
      • For when you want to order a separate gearbox for your West Coast Drive.

title: Battery Beak
body_html:
This is a battery load tester, capable of determining the health of a battery.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • Warranty
  • The Battery Beak is produced by Cross the Road Electronics.
    This is a battery load tester, capable of delivering an 18 amp load and measuring:
    • Internal resistance
    • State of charge (SOC)
    • Can determine the overall health of the battery
    The Battery Beak supports all battery chemistries but has additional features to determine battery health for both Lead Acid and NiMH chemistries in a variety of voltages and capacities. The Battery Beak mates directly with the SB-50A connector used in the FIRST Robotics Competition, but we've created bundles for FIRST Tech Challenge users to give them the same great experience. These bundles ship with the Battery Beak configured for the correct battery type and with the appropriate adapter cable for those battery terminals.

    The high resolution OLED display displays all the information you need for a quick decision on battery health:
    • Internal resistance
    • SOC
    • Open-load voltage
    • Voltage at 1 amp and 18 amps
    • Battery status of 'Good', 'Fair' or 'Bad'
    The internal resistance measurement is useful in determining if any bad cells are present. When the Battery Beak is used to track a battery's internal resistance over time and compared to its manufacturer specs, it is possible to determine when to take a battery out of service before a failure occurs. The built in power down feature allows the Beak to be connected to your battery indefinitely without draining your battery. The housing of the Beak is a durable ABS/Polycarbonate blend and mates directly to the Anderson SB-50A connector.

    Included with this part is the Battery Beak and a stylish lanyard.

    FIRST Tech Challenge Version Overview (am-3430)

    This version of the Battery Beak is designed with FIRST Tech Challenge teams in mind. When you order this version, your Battery Beak will arrive configured for the 12V 3Ah NiMH batteries used in FIRST Tech Challenge. You will also receive the SB-50 to XT30 & XT60 & PP45 adapter cable necessary to connect to your batteries, whether you left them stock or converted them to PowerPole connectors.

    Included Hardware:

    • One - FIRST Tech Challenge Battery Configured Battery Beak
    • One - SB-50 to XT30 & XT60 & PP45 adapter (am-2070b) Note: Don't use more than 2 of the connectors at once or you risk causing a short circuit with the battery.

title: Climber in a Box
body_html:
The AndyMark Climber in a Box is a robust, lightweight, configurable, and affordable solution for FRC climbing challenges.

  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • What's in the Box?

  • NEW FOR 2026: This product now includes two styles of hook, allowing teams to choose which style best fits their robot build.

    The AndyMark Climber in a Box is a robust, lightweight, configurable, and affordable solution for climbing challenges historically present in FRC end game periods. The design of Climber in a Box has been inspired by many team designs along the way, including 254 and 2056. The final prototype for this climber was developed in partnership with FRC Team 3940 CyberTooth for the 2020/2021 Infinite Recharge season. This mechanism has been battle-tested with hundreds of climbs on a full-weight FRC Robot without failures, both in development and real match play. Available in single and two-stage configurations, this product should help teams of all levels elevate their team's performance at competitions.

    This product uses a "spring out, winch back" powertrain strategy, using off-the-shelf 3.5lb constant force springs to raise the included Hook Kit, and 3 mm Dyneema Rope to retract it with the included Winch Kit. Simply unspool the included rope using a planetary gearbox to raise the hook(s), drive the robot up to the bar, and winch it back to elevate your robot. The AndyMark Climber in a Box does not include a motor or gearbox, but is compatible with many off-the-shelf planetary gearboxes on the market that have a 2 in. bolt circle mounting pattern and support a 2 in. long 1/2 in. hex output shaft, including the highly durable blue Sport Gearboxes when a 2 in. replacement shaft is purchased.

    The bearing kits within this product are designed to go from 2 in. square 1/16 in. wall aluminum tubing, down to a 1 in. square 1/16 in. wall tube, with a 1.5 in. square 1/16 in. wall tube in between for the 2 stage flavor of this product. A combination of durable 608 bearings and custom molded plastic components provide the bearing surfaces for a free-flowing telescoping tube mechanism with no 3D printed parts. Each stage has a maximum travel of 24.5 in.

    The AndyMark Climber in a Box is an unassembled kit of everything you need (excluding gearmotor), which is designed to require no precision machining in order to make your FRC robot climb. The plates included within the Hook Kit, Bearing Kits, and Winch Kit are all designed to be assembled and used as drill guides for match drilling their mounting locations onto the aluminum tubes. Each tube is pre-cut to a 30 in. length so no cutting of the tubes is required to achieve maximum travel. This product is available with and without aluminum tubes. If a team has access to extrusion locally, ordering this product without tubes can cut down on product and shipping prices.

    Motor and Gearbox Pairings:

    Driving the Climber in a Box can be simple and easy. Not sure which gearbox or motor to use? Below is a list of recommended reductions for whichever motor you may have on hand utilizing our CIM Sport and 57 Sport planetary gearboxes. These recommendations are based on one climber and one robot and are based on the minimum safety factors for the motors, gearboxes, and other components. Utilizing two climbers instead of just one may allow for lower ratios.

    • RedLine - Paired with 48:1 Sport
    • CIM - Paired with a 16:1 Sport
    • NEO 550 - Paired with a 36:1 Sport
    • NEO - Paired with a 16:1 Sport
    • Kraken X60 - Paired with a 12:1 Sport

    When using a Sport Gearbox, a 2 in. shaft is needed to extend across the full pulley width.

    Assembly:

    Assembled Weight (without motor or gearbox):

    • 2 Stage Climber in a Box - 6 pounds
    • 1 Stage Climber in a Box - 3.75 pounds

    Assembly instructions can be found below. Watch this video for more in-depth instruction about adding the rope to the assembly.

title: Compliant Wheels
body_html:
• Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • Compliant wheels are not intended for moving robots, but moving objects. The now ubiquitous intake wheel in competition robotics, compliant wheels give way to allow rigid objects to be manipulated easily. A line of multiple wheels on a driven hex shaft creates a very effective roller that ignores variations in the objects being driven. This makes for high-performance intakes and internal conveyors.
    Different durometer ratings give each wheel unique characteristics. Green wheels (35A durometer) are the softest, grippiest, and most compliant around objects, while orange (40A), blue (50A), and black (60A) wheels are increasingly firm. The increased firmness also gives the harder wheels a higher RPM rating.
    The hex bore wheels are designed to be used on a hex shaft, bunched together, or separated by collar clamps or hex spacers.
    The Nub Bore wheels are designed to work with our line of Nubs.
    The hex bore on the 2 in. versions of this wheel are undersized, and are intended to be an interference fit on their respective hex shafts. This interference fit allows for effective torque transfer from the hex shaft to the wheel, as well as allowing the wheel to remain in place along the shaft without the need for spacers or collar clamps:

    • Bore: 0.500 in. [12.7 mm] (1/2) Hex, 3/8 in. Hex, 5mm Hex, Nub
    • Color: Green, Black, Blue, Orange
    • Core Material: Polycarbonate
    • Diameter: 2 in., 2.25 in., 3 in., 4 in.
    • Durometer: 35A (Green), 40A (Orange), 50A (Blue), 60A (Black)
    • Maximum RPM: 3500 - 9000 RPM
    • Tread Material: TPU
    • Weight: 2 in. = 0.035 lbs., 2.25 in. = 0.08 lbs., 3 in. = 0.12 lbs., 4 in. = 0.228 - 0.269 lbs.
    • Width: 2 in. = 0.5 in., All others = 1 in.

The driver station tray is a convenient way to carry FRC controllers and hardware.

  • This product ships as an unassembled kit and requires drilling some holes.

    You have enough to worry about when preparing for FIRST Robotics Competition events. Ensure your driver station setup is worry-free, by using this Driver Station Tray.

    The driver station tray is a lightweight solution to a problem that all FIRST Robotics Competition Teams face:

    Getting the drivers' controllers and hardware to the field without forgetting anything AND making sure that when a robot slams into the alliance wall, your expensive laptop and beautiful controllers are not tossed onto the ground.

    Features:

    Even More Comfort:

    To make for a better grip, you may 3D print a Handle Grip with the STL files below. These handles sandwich the polycarbonate handles for a smoother rounded grip and the screws to attach these are already included in your purchase.

    Some Assembly Required:

    • Screw two handle sheets per side into the peanut.
    • Use the pre-drilled holes in the polycarbonate bottom as a drill guide to match drill the peanut.
    • Rivet the bottom on.
    • Drill mounting holes for the wire strap mounts in the desired locations.
    • Install wire strap mounts and straps.
    • Install hook and loop as desired to secure the laptop to the tray and the tray to the driver shelf at events.

  • Select your choice of a pneumatic meter-out or meter-in flow control valve. The port is a 1/8 in. NPT male thread, and 1/4 in. diameter tube can be pressed in to the push-to-connect fitting.

    Meter-out allows for the flow away from the cylinder to be controlled. This definition assumes that the pneumatic cylinder is on the NPT thread side of the value. The opposite flow is not restricted.

The hollow and cutouts design reduces the distance the ball can fly and slows down its traveling speed, making it a safer and less intimidating option for younger students or in indoor classes where there is limited space. The Screamin' Yellow color make these softballs easy to see and track - great for both the hitter or a player in the outfield.

    Made for Durability
    The balls feature excellent durability thanks to a crack-resistant design, which allows them to stand up to use by higher level players who are practicing their hitting in tighter spaces. The tough and rigid polyethylene allows it to hold up to contact with metal, plastic, and rubber bats without denting or breaking. These are the entry-level plastic style balls from Gopher, and their flexibility and durability make them superior to others found on the market.

title: HiGrip Wheels
body_html:
These wheels feature an aggressive tread pattern for superior traction.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • Superior grip and exceptional performance. Say hello to HiGrip wheels!

    These wheels provide superior traction for robot movement. They feature an aggressive tread pattern providing maximum transfer of power to the ground.
    A robust polycarbonate core means these wheels are up to the challenge for high impact and speed applications, drop em and bob em but they'll keep going.

    Varying durometers mean you can choose just how grippy these wheels can be. White or 80A durometer HiGrip wheels have a long life and provide good traction. Black or 60A durometer HiGrip wheels have an intermediate life and higher grip than white. Blue or 50A durometer HiGrip wheels provide the most traction and will wear quickly as a result.

    The bolt pattern and bore of these wheels allow for convenient bearing placement and easy attachment to other motion parts like sprockets and pulleys.

    Product Usage:
    Use #10-24x3/4 thread forming screws to attach sprockets or hubs to this wheel. Many thread locking materials are not compatible with polycarbonate and can eat away at the plastic. Be sure to check which adhesives are okay to use with this product. This link will allow you to check which materials are okay to use with what adhesives, https://bit.ly/loctitematerialcheck

    With Axle and Hub:
    • If you wish to drive this wheel with an Axle and Hub, you can pick your hub by fitting any of the AndyMark hubs (not included) to this wheel. If this is your choice, then no bearing is needed. Use #10-24x3/4 thread forming screws to fasten a hub to this wheel.
    With Sprocket:
    • If you wish to drive this wheel with a sprocket, then the sprocket needs to be attached to the side of the wheel, and two ball bearings need to be pressed into the wheel (one on each side). The ball bearing must have a 1.125 in. od. For a 1/2 in. id, use am-0181 or am-0029. For a 3/8 in. id, use am-0209. Use #10-24x3/4 thread forming screws to fasten the sprocket to the wheel.
    With Bearings:
    • To press bearings into this wheel (for a free spinning wheel or for use with a sprocket), two ball bearings need to be pressed into the wheel (one on each side). The ball bearing must have a 1.125 in. od. For a 1/2 in. id, use am-0181 or am-0029. For a 3/8 in. id, use am-0209.

    Learn how to attach these wheels to your robot by watching this video!

    • Diameter: 4 in. [100 mm], 6in.
    • Durometer: 80A, 60A, 50A
    • Load Capacity: 90-100 lbs.
    • Weight: 0.3, 0.5 lbs.

title: AndyMark Hubs
body_html:
These high-strength aluminum Hubs are designed for competition robots.

  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • AndyMark has been selling hubs specifically designed for competition robots since 2006. Over the past 13 years, we've expanded upon this line, making subtle changes along the way. We took everything we've learned, and we designed a brand new line of high-strength, high-quality hubs for competition robots. These new designs take the best features cherry-picked from our different hub designs of the past and combine them all into one unified design.

    Every hub still maintains a closed-profile hole for maximum strength. Every shaft hub has been designed with bearing bosses on both sides that have been sized appropriately for the mating bearings that would pair with the bore through the hub, which means you can run each hub right against a bearing with no need for extra spacers. All of these hubs are also made from high strength 7075-T6 or 6061-T6 aluminium. Where possible, the shoulder on shaft hubs was reduced to 7/8 in. in diameter for an easier fit with our molded plastic wheels, while still maintaining a precise 1.125 in. diameter boss for locating in wheels, sprockets, gears, and more.

    The holes are evenly spaced on a 1.875 in. circle and 0.201 inches in diameter. Hexes are timed to the holes, but keyways are not.

    If you are looking for any of our legacy hubs they are located here:

    0.5 in. Hex Hub, Extruded (am-2568)

title: navX2-Micro Navigation Sensor
body_html:
The navX2-Micro is a second-generation 9-axis inertial/magnetic sensor and motion processor.
  • Description
  • What's in the Box?
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • Warranty

  • This item is restricted for shipment in some countries. Please check international shipping restrictions before ordering.

    The navX-2 Micro is the greatest sensor for orientation in competitive robots. navX2-Micro is a second-generation 9-axis inertial/magnetic sensor and motion processor. Designed for plug-n-play installation onto robots such as those used in the FIRST Technology Challenge (FTC) and the FIRST Robotics Challenge (FRC), navX2-Micro helps build better robots by adding sophisticated navigation capabilities. Significant improvements over the classic navX-Micro allow for more accuracy, decreased yaw drift, and faster boot time. navX-2 Micro includes software algorithms for enhanced sensor calibration as well as KalmanFilter-based data fusion combining gyro, accelerometer, and magnetometer data into a 9-axis heading and high-quality magnetometer calibration including magnetic disturbance detection.

    In addition to being an Inertial Measurement Unit, navX-Micro capabilities are referred to within the aerospace industry as an “Attitude/Heading Reference System” (AHRS). Kauailabs brings this high-tech AHRS capability to FIRST teams – to use, learn, and explore. navX-Micro is a key component of Kauailabs’ ongoing efforts to make state-of-the-art navigation technologies used in drones and autonomous vehicles (e.g., the Google Car) available to robotics students and enthusiasts as low-cost, open-source products.

    Improvements over navX "Classic":
    navX2-Micro features a new set of IMU & Magnetometer sensors with superior sensor specifications to those on the MPU-9250 sensor. This board has a faster 180Mhz microcontroller and an optimized startup time at 5 seconds versus 15 seconds. In addition, it has a completely new Kalman Filter-based Sensor Fusion algorithm running internally at a blazing fast 416Hz.

    Features:

    • 3-axis Magnetometer,LIS2MDL
    • 32-bit ARM processor, ST Micro LSM6DSM IMU
    • KalmanFilter-based data fusion

    Sophisticated Motion Processing:

    • High Accuracy, Low-latency Yaw, Pitch and Roll Angles calculated by real-time Kalman Filter running at 416Mhz
    • Factory Accelerometer Calibration, Automatic Gyroscope Calibration
    • Quaternions and Gravity-corrected Linear Acceleration and Velocity Measurements
    • High-sensitivity Motion Detection
    • Tilt-compensated Compass Heading
    • 9-Axis absolute heading w/Magnetic disturbance detection

    Inertial/Magnetic Measurement Unit:

    • Configurable Update Rate from 4 to 200Hz
    • Access to Raw Data from Gyroscopes, Accelerometers, and Magnetometers

    Easy to Use:

    • Plug-n-Play connection on FTC and FRC robots via I2C and USB interfaces
    • 5V and 3.3V-compatible I2C Signaling
    • Can be powered by either 5V or 3.3VDC
    • Connection to Windows PC via USB Cable
    • FTC and FRC Software libraries and sample code
    • Support for Mounting in horizontal, vertical and even upside-down configurations via Omnimount
    • Tools for Magnetometer Calibration

  • Sensor Bundle (am-4076a):

    • 1 - navX-2 Micro Navigation Sensor (am-3554a)

title: REV NEO 550 Brushless Motor
body_html:
The REV NEO 550 Brushless Motor is the smaller version of the NEO family of brushless motors.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • The REV NEO 550 Brushless Motor is the newest member of the NEO family of brushless motors. Its output power and small size are specifically designed to make NEO 550 the perfect motor for intakes and other non-drivetrain robot mechanisms. Mounting holes and pilot match a standard 550 series motor, making it natively mount to many existing off-the-shelf gearboxes.

    NEO 550 has been optimized to work with the REV SPARK MAX Motor Controller to deliver best-in-class performance and feedback. Brushless motors like the NEO 550 can ONLY be driven using brushless motor controllers and will be damaged if used incorrectly. Currently, the only FRC legal brushless motor controller is the SPARK MAX.

    Pre-Pressed Pinions:
    This motor can be selected without a pinion for you to use existing hardware, or you can select one of two pinion options. We offer a pre-pressed twelve tooth pinion preparing the NEO 550 for use in any number of custom gearbox designs. We also offer a version with a sixteen tooth pinion. This pinion allows the NEO 550 to be used in the super strong planetary gearbox, the 57 Sport.

    Features:

    • Mounting features match 550 series DC Motors: Drop the NEO 550 in wherever another 550 motor was.
    • Out-Runner Construction: Allows you to mount motion components to the rear bolt circle.
    • Front and Rear Ball Bearings: The output shaft is supported in several places making it superior at handling loads.
    • High-Temperature Neodymium Magnets: Strong magnets capable of handling the abuse of competitive robotics.
    • High-Flex Silicone Motor Wires: For superior wire management.
    • Integrated Encoder: For built-in position feedback.
    • Motor Temperature Sensor: Understand the stress your motor is under by reading its temperature.

    Warranty:
    Email support@revrobotics.com and include your AndyMark order number.

    Note:
    Per REV: NEO 550 Brushless Motors, with date code 202109, may have an undersized shaft which causes press-fit components to be a slip fit on the shaft. We're recommending the components be retained with Loctite 635, 638 ("green loctite") or an equivalent "retaining compound". If neither of these are available, Loctite 680 or Loctite 380 are also an acceptable alternative.
    REV has also published a solution if you find that Loctite is not working for you.

    ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

title: Nubs
body_html:
The nub is a specific hub intended to connect motion components to spinning shafts, like sprockets gears, pulleys and wheels.

  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • The nub is a series of hubs intended to connect motion components to spinning shafts, like sprockets gears, pulleys and wheels. It supports the output shaft of the AndyMark NeveRest motors as well as other motors on the market. It also supports the AndyMark 6 mm D shafts for robust motion systems and impeccable torque transfer.

    We carry several body profiles of the Nub too! Their use cases are:

    • Single Boss for installing an individual Nub Bore item on a shaft
    • Double Boss for locating two Nub Bore items on a shaft
    • Double Boss XL for high-torque applications or connecting two shafts together
    • Single Boss Bearing for making free-spinning motion components (am-3667 has been replaced by am-4316)
    • Single Boss Servo for interfacing with 24T spline-based servos

    The four mounting holes on these nubs are sized at 0.128 in. diameter, with the intention of accepting a #6-32 threaded screw. They are not tapped, but can be tapped by most machine screws due to this diameter.

    Note:

body_html:
Peanut Extrusion is the 1 in.x1" installment of our easy-to-use structure system.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • Peanut Extrusion is the 1 in. x 1 in. installment of our easy-to-use structure system. The profile of this extrusion looks like a peanut, and has two holes sized for 1/4-20 thread-forming screws. The added mid-spans are positioned to flank a pair of bolts that self thread into an adjoining piece of Peanut Extrusion. These spans prevent the extrusion from getting crushed by over-tightening. Enjoy the ease of creating rigid corner joints without gussets, with a closed profile that prevents dust and debris build up. Whether you are making a table in your shop or a strong frame for a robot, this extrusion is the one for you!

title: Performance Wheels
body_html:
• Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • The Performance Wheel is a virtually indestructible wheel made out of solid 6061 aluminum. This competition-proven design has been used on FIRST Robotics Competition robots for many years. This wheel can take anything an FRC robot can throw at it, and much more.

    Three options of Bore are available:

    • Nub Bore:
      • Designed to be driven by an AndyMark Nub and a 6 mm D shaft. This also allows for other motion hardware that utilizes a 1.875 in. 6-hole bolt circle found in many AndyMark and competition robotics products. To mount one of these to the rear (flat) side, use a 250 Sprocket and Pulley Spacer. To mount one to the front, use a 550 Sprocket Spacer.
    • 0.5 inch Hex Bore:
      • This wheel is supported and driven by a 1/2 in. hex shaft. These wheels also have a 1/8 in. thick boss on the rear (flat) side of the wheel to prevent unwanted friction in bearing outer races. This also reduces the part count on drivetrains. Optionally, it can be driven by motion hardware utilizing a 1.875 in. 6-hole bolt circle found in many AndyMark and competition robotics products. To mount one of these to the rear of the wheel use a 250 Sprocket and Pulley Spacer. To mount one to the front, use a 550 Sprocket Spacer.
    • 1.125 inch Bearing Bore:
      • This wheel is designed to be supported by 1.125 in. OD (FR8) flanged bearings, and driven by motion hardware that utilizes a 1.875 in 6-hole bolt circle found in many AndyMark and competition robotics products. To mount one of these to the rear (flat) side, use a 250 Sprocket and Pulley Spacer. To mount one to the front, use a 550 Sprocket Spacer.

    These wheel do not include tread material, which is available separately, and depends on your application. With the exception of the Nub Bore option, these wheels are designed to utilize rivets to attach the tread to the wheel. AndyMark recommends using the Performance Wheel Tread Attachment Kit (am-4366). The wheel has been manufactured with no holes on the rim, as it is intended to be a blank canvas for teams to install rivets freely.

    Here you can see a short instructional video on how to use this kit.

    The Nub Bore option is designed to utilize a zip-tie to attach and tension the tread to the wheel. The method of attachment is similar to the previous version, except that the zip tie goes around the bolt instead of through the hole.

    • Bolt Pattern: 6 #10-32 holes on a 1.875 in. bolt circle
    • Bore: Nub Bore, 0.5 in. Hex, 1.124 in.
    • Diameter: 4 in. [100 mm], 6 in.
    • Load Capacity: 500 lbs.
    • Material: 6061-T6 Aluminum

body_html:
This strong, lightweight wheel is an ideal drive wheel for smaller robots, or for intakes and other auxiliary robot mechanisms.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • The inside black portion of these wheels are made from molded polycarbonate plastic. The outer tread is TPU (Thermoplastic PolyUrethane). This robust but lightweight wheel provides good traction on carpet and soft tiles. Stealth wheels are the perfect drive wheel for smaller (<50 lb.) robots, and both Stealth and Sushi rollers are great for intakes and other auxiliary robot mechanisms. These wheels are available in a variety of bores and durometers. 3 in. and 4 in. Stealth Wheels feature a 6 bolt pattern on a 1.875 in. bolt circle for mounting sprockets, hubs, and gears. Nub Bore Stealth Wheels feature a 4 bolt pattern on a 16 mm bolt circle found in most FIRST Tech Challenge building systems. The lower the durometer the softer the wheel is, this makes it wear away faster, but also makes it more grippy.

title: Time-On Meter
body_html:
This meter can gauge how much time a robot has been powered on.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • This neat little gadget mechanically counts hours when it has power. Typically found on farm equipment for timing maintenance schedules, it can be used on robots to gauge how much time your robot has been powered across it's entire life. This can be useful for seeing when certain components fail or wear out, or just keeping track for fun. You might be surprised how many hours you spend with your robot!

    This Time-On Meter is compatible with most DC 6-80V powered equipment. The meter cannot reset, if it exceeds the maximum value, it will be cleared automatically. The maximum value is 99,999.9 Hours.

    Installation:

    The timer comes packaged with a polycarbonate bracket that has 0.5 in. pitch #10 holes compatible with common FRC building systems for easy mounting to your robot. For wiring simply wire the positive and negative leads to a free slot on your PDP/PDH. A 5A fuse is sufficient.

title: Flyer Overdrive Gearbox
body_html:
• Description
  • Gearbox Ratios
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • The Flyer Gearbox is our next generation of overdrive gearbox for FRC perfect for sending game pieces flying through the air, but it's also so much more! It is unique in that is it the first gearbox for FRC that is designed to be an "overdrive" (spinning the output shaft faster than the input) but also be an "underdrive" (reducing the output shaft speed compared to the input) all in a single versatile gearbox. Both gears have the same 1/2 in. hex bore on them letting the user decide if they want to put them in an underdrive or overdrive configuration. That's why there are two ratios listed when making your ratio selection, both are possible with the same purchase!

    The gearbox comes with a short 1/2 in. hex output shaft that protrudes about 2 in. from EITHER face of the gearbox, but ANY Toughbox Output Shaft can be selected to replace it. Since both the front and rear bearings are 1.125 in. OD you can even replace the rear bearing with another 1/2 in. hex bearing and run whatever length of 1/2 in. hex shaft you want as a pass through with no machining whatsoever. Just retain it with 2 collar clamps and be sure to support the end. This could make a great roller intake when paired with some of our wheels.

    The "wings" of the gearbox are designed to slot over any 1 in. wide extrusion such as Peanut or Box Tube for an easy mounting option to the frame of your robot.

    This gearbox has three hardware options for input, CIM/NEO, Falcon, and Sport Gearbox. The first two are great options for flywheel shooters that give you a nice bearing supported output shaft, dialed into the optimum gear ratio that can absorb the shock loads and deflection associated with a fast spinning wheel contacting game pieces. The third option, using a Sport gearbox, lets you get another stage of reduction while helping you securely mount your mechanism and getting a optionally reversed, offset shaft. This could be great for something like a climber. Please note, these options simply change the hardware that comes with the Flyer, they do not include a motor or planetary gearbox.

    We also offer the no gears option if you want to supply your own gears to get a ratio we don't currently offer. Any two 20DP 1/2 in. wide, 1/2 in. hex bore gears that total 70 teeth can be used inside this gearbox. You can also use an empty shell as the mount point for the other end of an extended shaft for a symmetrical setup.


  • Please contact support@andymark.com if you do not see a Ratio Table
    • Diametral Pitch: 20
    • Gear Spacing: 70 teeth
    • Gear Width: 0.500 in.
    • Motor Input: CIM/NEO, Falcon, 1/2 in. Hex
    • Motor Quantity: 1
    • Output Shaft: 0.500 in. Hex, 2 in. long.
    • Plate Material: 5052 Aluminum
    • Pressure Angle: 20°
    • Ratio: 1:2.88, 1:2.5, 1:1.92, 1:1.33, 1:1, 1.33:1, 1.92:1, 2.5:1, 2.88:1

title: FRC Roller Intake System Kit
body_html:
This intake system is a build your own intake system (assembly required) designed for FRC.
  • Description
  • What's in the Box?
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • These parts are intended so you can cut, change and adjust to make the intake for YOUR robot. There is included hardware to power the intake via either a gear drive or a belt drive from anything with a 1/2 in. hex output shaft. You can chose to buy it bundled with a PG27 gearmotor (FRC Legal only) or supply your own gearmotor with a 1/2 in. hex output shaft that you might already have.

    No assembly instructions, not for FTC:

    We intentionally do not have assembly instructions for this kit because it can be assembled many different ways to best suit your robot.

    It comes with both pulley and belt OR gear options to make this run as a belt driven roller, or as a gear driven roller. The mount brackets have a mounting pattern to handle either option. The components in this kit are designed around use in the FIRST Robotics Competition and the motor used is not FIRST Tech Challenge legal.

    Please keep this in mind when ordering.

    Check out the product photo for an example of how to build it.

  • Included Parts:

    • 2 - Intake Motor Mount Brackets (am-3311a)
    • 4 - 2.25 inch HD Compliant Wheels, 35a Durometer, 500 Hex Bore (am-3949_green)
    • 1 - 1/2 in. Steel Hex Shaft Stock, 3ft (Cut to length as needed) (am-0856-3)
    • 2 - 24T HTD Pulley with 1/2 in. Hex Bore (am-3403)
    • 2 - 24T HTD Pulley Extensions (am-3404)
    • 1 - 55 Tooth HTD Timing Belt (am-3925)
    • 2 - 32T 20dp 500H Bore Gears (am-3815)
    • Various Hardware and Spacers


    Optional Motor:

    • 1 - PG27 Gearmotor with 1/2 Hex Output (am-3654)

title: Double Acting 3/4 in. Bore Air Cylinders Different Lengths
body_html:
These double acting single rod stainless steel cylinders are a solid choice when you want air actuated motion.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • These cylinders have a strong 0.75 in. thick bore and are available in multiple stroke lengths.

    • Bore: 0.75 in. (3/4) Round
    • Manufacturer: SMC
    • Manufacturer Part #: NCME075-[stroke length]
    • Nose Thread: 5/8-18
    • Pivot Point: Rear
    • Port(s): 1/8 in. NPT
    • Retracted Overall Length: 5.1 in., 6.5 in., 8.5 in., 10.5 in., 11.5 in.
    • Rod Thread: 1/4-28 Thread
    • Stroke: 0.5 in., 2 in., 4 in., 6 in., 7 in.

title: ToughBox Mini S
body_html:
• Description
  • Gearbox Ratios
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • The best gets better! The ToughBox Mini, a staple of single-speed gearboxes, has improved! Say hello to the ToughBox Mini, now, with an S.

    The features everyone needs are here to stay; the drop-in option for the AM14U drive bases accept NEO and CIM-style Motors. "What has changed?", you ask. For starters, gears are now symmetrical. You will no longer need to ensure gears are installed in the correct orientation! Secondarily, pocketed gears are now an off-the-shelf option for you to choose when saving weight is a priority. If you have gear stock on hand and want to save money, you can order with output gears excluded.

    Like many gearboxes we offer, the ToughBox Mini S can be ordered with your plate, ratio, and shaft of choice based on your needs. If you want the ToughBox Mini as it was, now called ToughBox Mini Classic, will still around while supplies last.

    Components Included with All ToughBox Mini S Gearboxes:

    • 1 - 3/8 in. Round Shielded Bearing (R6ZZ) (am-0028)
    • 1 - ToughBox Series 0.375 in. Hex Cluster Shaft (am-0152)
    • 1 - 1/2 in. E-Clip (am-0206)
    • 2 - 3/8 in. ID Shielded Bearing (R6ZZ) (am-0516)
    • 1 - ToughBox Mini Housing (am-0650)
    • 1 - 1/4 in. Flat Washer Steel (am-1027)
    • 1 - Screw, BHCS 1/4-20 x 1/2 in. Zinc (am-1039)
    • 4 - 10-32 Nylock Nut (am-1042)
    • 4 - 10-32 x 3/4 in. Long Socket Head Cap Screw (am-1047)
    • 1 - Dowel Pin, 1/4 in. dia x 1.00 in. long, Steel (am-1323)
    • 1 - Red Tacky Grease, 14.2 gram (am-2768)
    • 1 - 1/2 in. Hex Shielded Flanged Bearing (FR8ZZ-HexHD) (am-2986)
    • 1 - SRX Encoder Cylinder Magnet (am-3505)

    Version-Specific Components

    Motor Hardware:

    • CIM/NEO
      • 2 - 8 mm Push On Retaining Ring (am-0033)
      • 2 - 14 Tooth 20 DP 8 mm Round Bore Steel Pinion Gear (am-0034)
      • 4 - 5/16 in. Flat Washer (am-1009)
      • 4 - Screw, SHCS 10-32 x 5/8 in. w/ Nylon Thread Lock Patch (am-1120)
      • 2 - 2 mm x 10 mm Machine Key Steel (am-1121)
    • Falcon 500
      • 2 - 8-32 x 0.5 in. Button Head Cap Screw with Thread Locking (am-1537)
      • 4 - 10-32 x 0.5 in. Socket Head Cap Screw with Nylon Patch (am-1744)
      • 2 - 14 Tooth 20 DP Falcon Spline Bore Steel Pinion Gear (am-4147)

    Gear Options:

    • Standard
      • All gears are 20 DP 4140 Steel, Zinc Plated, and contain symmetrical features.
    • Weight Relief
      • Gears are pocketed where possible. The material properties are the same as standard gears. Some gears are too small to reasonably pocket. This includes;
        • 3/8 in. hex bore gears between 25 and 52 tooth.
        • 1/2 in. hex bore gears between 30 and 56 tooth.
    • Exclusions
      • To save money, if you already have gears for the ratios desired, you can elect to receive only the gears you need.

    Shaft Options:

    All shafts are made of Steel; 1018, 1215, or 12L14, and zinc plated for rust prevention. For speed and distance measurements, all shafts are machined with a socket to accept a steel dowl or magnet for various encoders. The AM14U shaft has this feature at both ends.

    • Long
      • Length: 5.6 inches long.
      • Usage: For large drive rail spans or when multiple motion components must be driven, this extra-long shaft is a great choice.
    • Short
      • Length: 3.6 inches long.
      • Usage: Great for driving individual motion components such as a hub or pulley. Supporting the output shaft end with a bearing is not always needed.
    • AM14U
      • Length: 5.1 inches long.
      • Usage: This shaft should be used when installing a ToughBox Mini S in an AM14U drive base. The length is designed to be perfectly supported on the output shaft end.

    Plate Options:

    • Flat (discontinued): For face mounting a ToughBox Mini S to various structures or members wherever you need it to live! It also keeps the insides from falling out.
    • Angled: When you want to secure the ToughBox Mini S to a flat component face like 2x1 box tube.
    • None: Use this option if you wish to secure the ToughBox Mini S straight to your own flat plate. We do this on the AM14U!

    Break-in Period:

    All AndyMark gearboxes require grease for proper operation and long life. Grease is included with your gearbox, so please use it. We encourage you to power the gearbox continuously for 30 minutes without grease to allow the gear teeth to wear in. We design with short run times in mind, this 'run in' period for smooth gearbox operation is recommended. Once completed, thoroughly grease the gear teeth periodically to ensure smooth operation.


  • Please contact support@andymark.com if you do not see a Ratio Table
    • Motor Input: CIM, NEO, Falcon 500
    • Motor Quantity: 1, 2
    • Ratio: 5.95:1, 7.31:1, 8.46:1, 9.13:1, 10.71:1, 12.76:1

      • 1 - 8-32 x 0.5 in. Button Head Cap Screw with Thread Locking (am-1537)
      • 2- 10-32 x 0.5 in. Socket Head Cap Screw with Nylon Patch (am-1744)
      • 1 - 14 Tooth 20 DP Falcon Spline Bore Steel Pinion Gear (am-4147)

    Gear Options:

    • Standard
      • All gears are 20 DP 4140 Steel, Zinc Plated, and contain symmetrical features.
    • Weight Relief
      • Gears are pocketed where possible. The material properties are the same as standard gears. Some gears are too small to reasonably pocket. This includes;
        • 3/8 in. hex bore gears between 25 and 52 tooth.
        • 1/2 in. hex bore gears between 30 and 56 tooth.
    • Exclusions
      • To save money, if you already have gears for the ratios desired, you can elect to receive only the gears you need.

    Shaft Options:

    All shafts are made of Steel; 1018, 1215, or 12L14, and zinc plated for rust prevention. For speed and distance measurements, all shafts are machined with a socket to accept a steel dowl or magnet for various encoders. The AM14U shaft has this feature at both ends.

    • Long
      • Length: 5.6 inches long.
      • Usage: For large drive rail spans or when multiple motion components must be driven, this extra-long shaft is a great choice.
    • Short
      • Length: 3.6 inches long.
      • Usage: Great for driving individual motion components such as a hub or pulley. Supporting the output shaft end with a bearing is not always needed.
    • AM14U
      • Length: 5.1 inches long.
      • Usage: This shaft should be used when installing a ToughBox Micro S in an AM14U drive base. The length is designed to be perfectly supported on the output shaft end.

    Plate Options:

    • Angled: When you want to secure the ToughBox Micro S to a flat component face like 2x1 box tube or channel.
    • None: Use this option if you wish to secure the ToughBox Micro S straight to your own plate. We do this on the AM14U for mecanum drive trains!

    Break-in Period:

    All AndyMark gearboxes require grease for proper operation and long life. Grease is included with your gearbox, so please use it. We encourage you to power the gearbox continuously for 30 minutes without grease to allow the gear teeth to wear in. We design with short run times in mind, this 'run in' period for smooth gearbox operation is recommended. Once completed, thoroughly grease the gear teeth periodically to ensure smooth operation.


  • Please contact support@andymark.com if you do not see a Ratio Table
    • Motor Input: CIM, NEO, Falcon 500
    • Motor Quantity: 1
    • Ratio: 5.95:1, 7.31:1, 8.46:1, 9.13:1, 10.71:1, 12.76:1

title: SDS MK4n Swerve Modules
body_html:
• Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • *IMPORTANT NOTE ABOUT LAYOUT: The adjacent MK4n Swerve Modules on a typical drivetrain are mirrored from each other, and there are consequently two layout options: "A" and "B". Most customer will want to buy two modules of each layout plus spares.

    The MK4n Swerve Module leverages the proven MK4i architecture into a new form factor. With the narrow side being only 4 in. wide inside of the frame member, it helps enable:

    • Wide game piece intakes between the swerve modules.
    • Compact drivetrains (accommodates a flat mounted FRC battery in an 17.5 in. wide drivetrain).

    Additional functional differences as compared to the MK4i include:

    • Beyond supporting 0.25 in. magnet encoders it also supports 0.5 in. hex encoders. The hex encoder utilizes this Center Column.
    • 16T drive and steering pinion gears for faster drive and steering speeds.
    • 10-32 threaded holes in the motor plate for covers to be added.

    Like the MK4i Swerve Module, the MK4n incorporates:

    • On-axis steering encoder (zero backlash, and the module can be disassembled/reassembled without resetting encoder offset)
    • All plates made out of 7075-T6 aluminum
    • All steel gears
    • Includes secondary plate to box in frame
    • 10-32 mounting holes on main plate for subsystems (e.g., collector)
    • Encoder guard to protect steering encoder
    • Same frame-to-floor height as the MK4 and MK4i Swerve Modules
    • Same L1+, L2, and L3+ drive ratios as the MK4c and MK4i Swerve Module equipped with the 16T Drive Pinion Gear Adapter Kit
    • No 3D printed parts
    • Includes wheel tread cut-to-length, drilled, and pre-installed on the Billet Wheel option
    • Includes all hardware, including hardware to mount module to robot

    We are offering the option to assemble the modules for you so you can hit the ground running:

    • CANcoders shipping with the assembled version include pre-soldered wires for a true plug-and-play experience.

    The steering gear ratio of the MK4n is 18.75:1. The MK4n is available in 3 different drive gear ratios. The tables below outline the drive gear ratios and free speeds.

    The swerve module can be directly mounted to commonly available 2' x 1 in. aluminum tubing with pre-drilled 10-32 clearance holes.

    Please note, the NEO Vortex pinion option requires for the NEO Vortex motors to have the 8mm keyed shaft.

    Approximate weights:

    • MK4n Swerve Module with Kraken X60 motors - 6.5 pounds (Includes encoder, lower mounting plate, mounting hardware, etc.)
    • MK4n Swerve Module with NEO motors - 6.0 pounds (Includes encoder, lower mounting plate, mounting hardware, etc.)

title: SDS MK4i Swerve Modules
body_html:
The MK4i module from SDS is one of the most popular swerve drive solutions available.
  • Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • AndyMark is proud to offer the most popular swerve drive solution on the market today. AndyMark is more than just a passthrough distributer we are offering a bunch of value add features including:

    • We are a one stop shop where you can buy the modules, motors, encoders all in one place on one order.
      • SDS Modules are even valid for use with PDVs!
    • We are offering the option to assemble the modules for you so you can hit the ground running
      • CANcoders shipping with the assembled version include pre-soldered wires for a true plug and play experience.

    The MK4i module inverts the motors on an MK4 module to a lower position where they are out of the way and better protected. Overall height and center of gravity are therefore lower. The MK4i module also moves the wheel further into the corner of the chassis for a wider wheelbase which results in a more stable robot. Because the wheel is moved into an area the frame would typically occupy, the MK4i includes a secondary plate to properly box in the chassis.

    Other Highlights of the MK4i module include:

    • On-axis steering encoder (zero backlash, module can be disassembled/reassembled without resetting encoder offset)
    • All plates made out of 7075-T6 aluminum
    • All steel gears
    • All moving parts are protected under top plate
    • Includes secondary plate to box in frame
    • 10-32 mounting holes on main plate for other robot subsystems
    • Encoder guard to protect the steering encoder
    • Same frame-to-floor height as previous Swerve Drive Specialties modules
    • Same L1 - L3 drive ratios as the MK4 module
    • No 3D printed parts
    • Cable-tie “nubs” keeps cable-ties in place
    • Bottom and top mounted chassis options
    • Includes wheel tread cut-to-length, drilled, and pre-installed on wheel
    • Includes all hardware, including hardware to mount module to robot
      • As of July 2023 mounting hardware is #10-32, this change is reflected by an "a" in the part number.

    The MK4i module has many parts in common with the MK4 module. Kits to convert the MK4 to MK4i are available.

    NEO V1.1, Neo Vortex, Falcon 500, and Kraken X60 motors are compatible with the MK4 module. CIM motors are not compatible with the MK4 due to their larger diameter. The MK4 module is available with the appropriate pinion kit for any of the above motors.

    The full steering ratio of the MK4i is 150/7:1, passing through one gear pair, then a pulley pair using a 64 tooth belt.
    The MK4i is available in 3 different drive gear ratios. The table below shows the drive gear ratios and free speeds with NEO V1.1 and Falcon 500 motors. L1 and L2 ratios are the most popular ratios and are suitable for standard full weight competition robots. The L3 ratio is more aggressive and is recommended for light weight robots.



    The module easily mounts to common 2x1 frame material. The module main plate typically mounts on top of the robot chassis, however, there is also clearance to mount the chassis on top of the module main plate to maximize ground clearance.

title: SDS MK4c Swerve Modules
body_html:
• Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • The MK4c combines the non-inverted motor layout of the MK4 module with the corner bias of the MK4i module. This results in the smallest footprint SDS module yet. The MK4c occupies a 4” X 4” area measured from the inside edge of the chassis.

    The MK4c incorporates:

    • On-axis steering encoder (zero backlash, and the module can be disassembled/reassembled without resetting encoder offset)
    • All plates made out of 7075-T6 aluminum
    • All steel gears
    • Includes secondary plate to box in frame
    • 10-32 mounting holes on main plate for subsystems (e.g., collector)
    • Same frame-to-floor height as the MK4, MK4i, and MK4n Swerve Modules
    • Same L1+, L2+, and L3+ drive ratios as the MK4n, as well as the MK4i Swerve Module equipped with the 16T Drive Pinion Gear Adapter Kit
    • No 3D printed parts
    • Includes wheel tread cut-to-length, drilled, and pre-installed on the Billet Wheel option
    • Includes all hardware, including hardware to mount module to robot

    The steering gear ratio of the MK4c is 12.8:1 The MK4c is available in 3 different drive gear ratios. The tables below outline the drive gear ratios and free speeds. L1+ and L2+ ratios are the most popular ratios and are suitable for standard full weight competition robots. The L3+ ratio is more aggressive and is recommended for light weight robots.

    The swerve module can be directly mounted to 2 in. x 1 in. aluminum tubing with pre-drilled 10-32 clearance holes.

    The MK4c module ships unassembled, and the following components are not included:

    • Drive motor (REV Robotics NEO, REV Robotics NEO Vortex, VEX Falcon 500, or WestCoast Products Kraken X60 recommended)
    • Steering motor (REV Robotics NEO, REV Robotics NEO Vortex, VEX Falcon 500, or WestCoast Products Kraken X60 recommended)
    • Steering encoder (CTRE CANcoder, Thrifty Absolute Magnetic Encoder, Redux HELIUM Canandmag, or equivalent)
    • Optional: Use these Motor Risers to not have to otherwise reduce the length of both motor shafts by approximately 0.25 in..

    Note: The above steering encoders come with the ⌀.250”x 0.500” magnet that gets installed in the Swerve Module's Center Column. That magnet is not included in the Swerve Module kit.

    Please note:

    • The NEO or NEO Vortex kit works for the NEO and NEO Vortex motors with the 8mm keyed shaft.
    • The Falcon 500 kit is primarily for the Falcon 500 motor. It can also work for the NEO Vortex motor with the Falcon spline shaft, but the shaft spacers are not included (they are supplied with the Falcon motors). Going this route for the NEO Vortex utilizes a splined steering pinion gear, so no press/slip fit is needed there.

    Approximate Weights:

    • MK4c module with NEO motors - 5.4 pounds
    • MK4c module with Kraken motors - 5.9 pounds

title: SDS MK4 Swerve Modules
body_html:
• Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation

  • AndyMark is proud to offer the most popular swerve drive solution on the market today. AndyMark is more than just a passthrough distributer we are offering a bunch of value add features including:

    • Every module gets a free injection molded motor spacer saving you time and money during assembly.
    • We are a one stop shop where you can buy the modules, motors, encoders all in one place on one order.
      • SDS Modules are even valid for use with PDVs!
    • We are offering the option to assemble the modules for you so you can hit the ground running
      • CANcoders shipping with the assembled version include pre-soldered wires for a true plug and play experience.
    The MK4 Swerve Module is the latest swerve drive iteration from SDS. The MK4 features a 1.5 in. wide Billet Wheel. Because of the 50% increase of width from previous generations you get greater tread life and slightly better traction. To accommodate the new wheel the MK4 uses the SDS 2nd Generation bevel gear set. As of December 2023 modules use all "V3" components and are sold with part numbers that end in an "a". See assembly guide for details.

    Despite it being one of the most compact and lightweight modules available, the MK4 module does not compromise on robustness. MK4 modules use all steel gears for superior wear resistance. Under typical use and with grease, the modules will be able to handle multiple seasons of robotics competition. In order to keep weight to a minimum, the steel gears are pocketed.

    Like the MK3, the MK4 uses a centrally located steering encoder to directly measure steering angle without the use of gears. This eliminates encoder backlash and reduces complexity. The module is specifically designed for the user favorite CTRE CANcoder.

    NEO V1.1, Neo Vortex, Falcon 500, and Kraken X60 motors are compatible with the MK4 module. CIM motors are not compatible with the MK4 due to their larger diameter. The MK4i module is available with the appropriate pinion kit for any of the above motors.

    The full steering ratio of the MK4 is 12.8:1, passing through one gear pair, then a pulley pair using a 64 tooth belt (am-4921).

    The MK4 is available in 4 different drive gear ratios. The table below shows the drive gear ratios and free speeds with NEO V1.1 and Falcon 500 motors. L1 and L2 ratios are the most popular ratios and are suitable for standard full weight competition robots. The L3 ratio is more aggressive and is recommended for light weight robots. The L4 ratio is very aggressive and is only recommended for very light weight mini bots.

    The module easily mounts to common 2x1 frame material. The module typically mounts on top of the robot chassis, however, there is also clearance to mount the chassis on top of the module to maximize ground clearance.

title: Electronic Bundles Builder
body_html:
• Description
  • Specifications
  • Documentation
  • Electronics are the power and brains behind every incredible robot and machine. Figuring out all the individual pieces needed to make a robot go can be tedious which is why we've made it easy with this electronic bundles builder page!

    Choose your processor, motor controllers, motors, and system components to create a complete electronics system to suit your needs. The only thing you'll need after configuring this Builder is a battery. For Mecanum chassis that you want to drive with a Radio Link controller you will need to purchase a Mecanum Mixer (am-2715b) to spin the wheels in the correct directions for translational motion.

    NOTE: Customers who are not affiliated with FIRST teams are required to purchase the NI roboRIO product through National Instruments, not AndyMark.


    Understanding Part Numbers

    :
    Electronic bundles product numbers are built to identify components within the code. Below is the breakdown of how these part numbers are built.
    • The first two positions identifies the product number:
      • BC - Bundle for Controls
    • The third position identifies the controller and will come with components needed to hook it up (see link):
      • F - roboRIO READY (BYOr) - Bring Your Own roboRIO - this kit matches the roboRIO one exactly, it just doesn't have a roboRIO in it, so if you have your own, this is perfect for you.
      • L - RadioLink - a simplistic approach of a simple Radio Control with limited programming capability in the controller
      • N - No Processor - so you'll need to have your own controller.
      • R - roboRIO - the fully capable controller used within FIRST Robotics Challenge
    • The fourth position identifies the motor controller and will come with the components needed to hook it up (see link):
      • X - SPARK Max - multiple possible inputs, able to control both brushed and brushless motors
    • The fifth position identifies the quantity of motors and will come with wires needed to hook them up:
      • 2 - Two Motors
      • 4 - Four Motors
    • The sixth position identifies the type of motor:
      • C - CIM - a brushed motor with power
      • R - RedLine - a brushed motor to designed for speed and power both
      • N - NEO 1.1 - a brushless motor built to be a drop in replacement for the CIM
      • 5 - NEO 550 - a brushless motor for anywhere a 550 sized motor fits
    • The seventh position identifies the type of power distribution and will come with components needed to hook them up (see links):
      • B - ATC 8 Gang Fuse Block - lightweight single input terminal for simple power distribution
      • 3 - PP45 Power Board - simple and compact power distribution with PP45 secure connections
